steps: First, roast wheat flour and urad dal flour in separate vessels with ghee until they turn brown.
Now take jaggery in a pan, add ghee, melt the jaggery, and let it boil for 5 minutes.
Now add the roasted wheat flour and urad dal flour to it.
And add mawa (khoya) and let it roast on the gas stove.
Then take it off the heat, add edible gum (gond), cardamom, and other spices, and stir well.
Once it cools down, shape into ladoos.
Mix one spoonful of ghee moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) into gram flour (besan) and make a thin batter.
Take sugar in a pot, add just enough water to submerge it, and boil.
Add a little lemon juice to remove the scum.
Warm the saffron and add it to milk.
Now once the sugar syrup reaches a one-string consistency, keep it on low heat to keep it warm.
Heat ghee in a pan, and once hot, hold a large-holed strainer over it and pour the prepared batter through it.
This will drop bundi into the pan. Fry it and put it into the sugar syrup.
When the second batch of bundi is ready, take out the bundi that was added first from the syrup and add the new batch of bundi.
Once the bundi has absorbed the syrup and is ready, add cardamom powder and peeled almond slices.
Start shaping the ladoos while the bundi is still warm and arrange them on a plate.
3.note: If the batter is whipped until its color changes from yellow to whitish, the bundi will be completely round.

steps: First, grate the paneer.
Now roast the paneer in a pan on low heat for 2 minutes and remove it to a plate.
Now in the same pan, add ghee, and once the ghee is hot, add milk.
After the milk comes to a boil, keep adding milk powder little by little while stirring well.
Once the milk and milk powder thicken, add grated dry coconut and let it cook on low heat.
Now add sugar, and once the sugar dissolves, add paneer and keep stirring on low flame.
Once the mixture leaves the pan and ghee separates, remove it to a dish and let it cool.
Then shape into ladoos, roll them in coconut powder, and garnish with pistachio slices.
Paneer ladoo is now ready.
First, take half of the ghee from the half cup of ghee in a pan.
Sauté the cashew pieces in it until they do not turn brown.
Then take those cashew pieces into another bowl and in the same pan take the ragi flour and keep stirring on low heat for 5 minutes.
Keep stirring until the lumps break, a sand-like texture is ready and the flour is not raw.
After the flour is roasted, let it cool down.
Then add one cup of powdered sugar, sautéed cashews, cardamom powder, and the remaining ghee to it and mix well.
After mixing well, roll laddu of appropriate size from it.
First, put one cup of water to heat in which add one tablespoon of ghee and salt to taste and boil the water.
After the water boils, turn off the gas and add rice flour to it, mix it and let it cook covered for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, to prepare the stuffing, roast the poppy seeds in a hot pan and take them out into a bowl.
Then add jaggery in the same pan, let it heat until the jaggery melts.
Once the jaggery melts, add fresh coconut scrapings to it and stir and mix on low heat and let it cook.
Now add cashew pieces, raisins, cardamom powder, and poppy seeds to it.
Now after the rice flour cools down, apply a little ghee in your hands and knead the dough well to make it smooth.
Now make dough balls from the bound dough, take one ball and keep spreading it thinly from the edges with your hands and make it the size of a puri.
Then make a cavity in it, fill one spoon of the prepared stuffing and pack the puri by making 5-6 pleats.
Keep moving those pleats upwards and seal it.
Steam the prepared modak.
Put them to steam in a steamer for 10-12 minutes.
Take them out after 10-12 minutes.
12.note: If you are not able to make the shape shown in the photo, you can also roll straight round laddus.

steps: Heat half of the ghee in a pan, as soon as a little ghee gets hot, add edible gum (gond) to it.
After the edible gum (gond) puffs up nicely and roasts from inside, take it out onto a plate.
Add pearl millet (bajra) flour in the remaining ghee in the pan and keep stirring it continuously with a spatula until the color changes.
If there is not enough ghee in the pan so that the flour feels wet, add a little more ghee before roasting the flour further.
Roast the flour until the ghee starts separating from the flour and a fragrance starts coming from it.
It takes about 10-15 minutes to roast the flour.
As soon as the flour is roasted, take it out in a bowl immediately, otherwise, as the pan is hot, there is a possibility of the flour burning.
Cut the jaggery into small-small pieces.
Heat the remaining ghee in the pan, add jaggery pieces and melt the jaggery on very low flame.
When the jaggery melts, take it out from the pan immediately, otherwise, if the jaggery syrup becomes hard, the laddus will become hard.
Cut almonds and cashews into small pieces and add to the roasted flour.
Now add grated coconut, roasted gum powder, cardamom powder, and melted jaggery and mix all the ingredients well.
The mixture for making laddu is ready.
Take a little mixture from the mixture and make laddus of the size you like.
About 10-12 medium laddus will be prepared from this much flour.
13.note: Fry the gum on very low flame so that it gets fried well from inside. You can use sugar instead of jaggery in bajra laddu. You can add charoli or dry fruits of your choice in bajra laddu.

steps: First roast the peanuts on medium heat until the outer skin of the peanuts separates.
Now let the peanuts cool and then separate their outer skin.
Take the roasted peanuts in a mixer and make a coarse powder-like mixture and keep it aside.
Now heat ghee in a pan and add jaggery to it.
Keep stirring on low heat until the jaggery melts completely.
Boil for one minute or until the syrup turns orange in color.
Now on low heat, add the prepared peanut crumb into the jaggery syrup.
Add 2 spoons of roasted sesame seeds, 2 spoons of grated dry coconut, and 1/4 spoon of cardamom powder to it.
Mix well until the mixture is well combined.
Take the laddu mixture into a bowl and let it cool down a bit.
Start making laddus when the mixture is still a little warm.
Put 2 tablespoons of oil to heat in a pan.
Then add jaggery and keep stirring continuously.
Keep the heat low.
When the jaggery starts boiling, just check it. (5-7 minutes)
Now mix the daliya in the jaggery and stir well.
Turn off the gas, apply oil to your hands and roll small sized laddus and put them in a vessel.
Ready to eat once they become hard.
15.note: Ghee can also be used instead of oil.

steps: First, add 1 spoon of oil in a kadhai and put it on the gas to heat.
Then put jaggery in it.
Keep stirring the jaggery continuously.
Keep the heat low.
When the jaggery starts boiling, check it, then turn off the gas and when the jaggery becomes a bit hard, add puffed rice to it and mix thoroughly.
Immediately apply oil to your hands and start shaping into ladoos.
16.note: Ghee can also be used instead of oil.

steps: First, take chocolate cake in a bowl and mash it (crumble it).
Then mix condensed milk into it.
Add melted chocolate to it and mix it well.
Then keep it in the fridge for 15 to 20 minutes.
After that, make small-sized balls from it.
Then again keep the plate with the made balls in the fridge for 15 to 20 minutes.
Now dip the balls in melted dark chocolate and put whatever you want on top for decoration.
After the chocolate on the balls sets, serve them.
First, roast the wheat, grind it in a mixer to make flour.
Now sift it, mix ghee, sugar and spices in it, and shape into ladoos.
First, roast the moong dal in a pan on low heat until it becomes golden in color.
Then when it cools down, grind it in a mixer to make flour.
Put the prepared flour in a kadhai, add ghee to it, and roast it on low heat until it turns golden brown.
Take the prepared mixture in a bowl and let it cool.
Now mix powdered sugar and cardamom powder into it.
Shape into ladoos and garnish with pistachios.
First, heat ghee in a kadhai, fry cashews and raisins in it, and once fried, take them out into a bowl.
Now in the same pan, add 1 cup semolina (rava) and roast on low heat until it turns golden brown color.
Now add grated dry coconut to it and roast for one more minute.
Turn off the stove and let the rava cool.
Meanwhile, take another vessel and take sugar and water in it to prepare a one-string sugar syrup.
Now turn off the stove and add the roasted rava to the sugar syrup.
Add roasted cashews, raisins, and cardamom powder to it and mix well.
Now take a little rava-based mawa (khoya) and prepare small ladoos with your palms.

ing: Sliced almonds and pistachios - as required
steps: In the gram flour (besan), mix a little warm milk and 2 teaspoons of ghee to make it crumbly.
Then sift it through a wheat flour sieve.
Heat ghee in a pan, add the flour and roast it.
Allow the flour to turn reddish brown on low heat.
Take enough water to submerge the sugar, boil it and make a 1 ½ (one and a half) string sugar syrup.
Add saffron, orange (yellow) color, cardamom powder, and the roasted flour to it and stir well in a circular motion.
Once cooled, grease a plate and set it to cool.
Sprinkle charoli (chironji) and sliced almonds-pistachios on top.
Pour heated ghee over it.
Then cut into diamond-shaped pieces.
First, combine wheat flour, gram flour (besan), and semolina (rava) and mix well.
Then add two tablespoons of ghee and two tablespoons of milk to it and mix.
Then knead a firm dough using lukewarm water.
Then shape small handfuls (muthiya) from it and fry them in oil on low flame.
After it cools down, grind it in a mixer to make churma.
Add a little water to half a cup of sugar to make a single-string sugar syrup, and add churma, grated coconut, cardamom powder, and sliced cashew-almonds to it and mix.
Slowly keep adding two to three spoons of ghee to it.
Mix well and spread it flat on a wooden board.
Press it down properly and decorate the top with sliced pistachios.
After it cools down, cut into pieces.
27.note: Half of the sugar can be mixed into the churma and the other half can be layered on top of the barfi churma layer. This dish can also be made without sugar syrup. Favorite colors can be added to this.

steps: Heat ghee in a pan and roast the coarse gram flour until it turns brown.
Then remove it from heat, and once cooled, add powdered sugar and cardamom powder.
Spread it on a plate or a wooden board, flatten it by patting, and top it with charoli (chironji) and sliced pistachio-almonds.
Now cut it into square pieces.
First, grind cashews, almonds, pistachios, melon seeds, and walnuts in a mixer.
Grind dates and figs together in a mixer.
Now heat ghee in a large heavy-bottomed pan, then add milk and let it boil.
Then add sugar and let the sugar dissolve.
Then add the ground cashews, almonds, pistachios, melon seeds, and walnuts, and mix well.
Now add the ground figs and dates, mix well, and keep stirring.
Now add water chestnut flour (singoda atta) and powdered dry dates, mix well, and keep stirring.
Then add lotus seed powder, gokhru powder, dry ginger powder powder, ganthoda powder, and poppy seeds and mix.
Now add white pepper powder, black pepper powder, white musli powder, black musli powder, panja salam, and piprimul, mix, and keep stirring.
If the ghee seems less, you can add a spoon. Ensure that it does not stick to the bottom.
Now add mawa (khoya) and mix. After adding mawa (khoya), reduce the heat to medium.
Now keep stirring this mixture until it thickens and ghee begins to separate. Add more ghee if needed.
Once thickened, turn off the gas and add nutmeg powder and mace powder, mixing well.
Now spread this mixture on a wooden board or plate greased with ghee, garnish with sliced pistachios on top, and cut into square pieces.
29.note: Nutmeg powder and mace powder should be added only after turning off the gas so that they taste good; if added earlier, the taste becomes bitter. This salampak is immunity-boosting and energizing.

steps: First, put ghee to heat in a pan.
Now in another pan, add water to the sugar and make a single-string sugar syrup.
Now add gram flour (besan) little by little into this syrup and stir continuously to ensure there are no lumps.
Now add the heated ghee little by little, keep stirring, and continue adding ghee.
Keep stirring this mixture and let it heat until it thickens and ghee starts separating in the pan while stirring.
Then turn off the gas, add cardamom seeds, spread it on a wooden board, and cut into pieces.

ing: cardamom powder - to taste milk - as needed
steps: Grind raw methi finely, mix with soft jaggery, and let it rest for two to three days.
Add 1 spoonful of ghee and 1 spoonful of milk to urad dal flour and mix well.
Then sift this flour and roast it in a kadhai on low heat until it turns brown.
Now, add 1 spoonful of ghee and 1 spoonful of milk to gram flour (besan) and mix well.
Then sift this flour and roast it in a kadhai on low heat until it turns brown.
Next, roast wheat flour directly on low heat until it turns brown.
Now, combine all three roasted flours and add the methi mixed with jaggery to it.
Break any lumps of jaggery completely.
Now add dry ginger powder, poppy seeds, grated dry coconut, almonds, crushed charoli (chironji), cardamom powder, and powdered sugar to this mixture and combine well.
Now heat ghee and add it to the prepared mixture, mixing thoroughly.
Grease a plate with ghee, spread this mixture onto it, and cut square pieces.
31.note: This methipak is beneficial for arthritis patients. Consuming it every year in winter helps with arthritis.

steps: First, add ghee to a kadhai and put it on heat to melt.
Then add wheat flour and roast it well on low heat while stirring continuously.
Once the flour is roasted, add dry ginger powder, ganthoda powder, and sugar into the hot flour itself.
Stir it well, ensuring there are no lumps, and mix everything together.
Now add cashew-almond pieces and poppy seeds, set it in a plate, cut lines, and make pieces.
32.note: Sukhdi can also be made by preparing a jaggery syrup base.

steps: Heat ghee in a vessel. Add wheat flour to it and roast on low heat until the flour turns light pink.
Once the flour is roasted, take it off the gas, add grated and crumbled jaggery to it, and mix thoroughly by stirring.
Spread it on a plate, rub the bottom of a small bowl over it to smooth the top surface, and cut lines immediately.
33.note: Fennel seeds and sesame seeds can also be added on top.

steps: Take ghee in a pan, heat it on the gas, add gram flour (besan) and maida (all-purpose flour), mix, and roast until it turns brown.
This mixture should remain in liquid form; keep it aside to cool.
Now take sugar in a vessel, add just enough water to submerge the sugar, and put it on the gas to make syrup.
Once all the sugar dissolves and the syrup starts thickening, squeeze the lemon into it.
Keep stirring the roasted flour in between so it does not set.
To check whether the syrup is ready or not, fill a small bowl with water.
Then drop half a spoonful of syrup into it; once it cools, take it in your hand to see if it forms a firm ball.
If it starts forming a firm ball, our syrup is ready.
Then grease a plate with ghee and pour the syrup into it.
Then use a spoon to move it around all sides and cool it quickly.
As the syrup cools, its color will become darker.
If it starts sticking to the plate, you can transfer it to another greased plate.
When the syrup is slightly cooled and ensuring it doesn't burn your hand, apply ghee to your hands and pull it.
Pull it like this, bring it together again, and pull again. (Do it the way dough is pulled while making urad papad.)
Pull it until it turns a whitish color, then add the previously roasted flour and pull again.
Pull and gather, pull and gather, until threads form and all the roasted flour mixes with the syrup.
Doing this for a while, at some point it will stop stretching.
Then, line a square box with butter paper, place a thick layer of it inside, press pistachio slivers on top, and cut into square pieces after an hour or so.
34.note: If the syrup is not right, sonpapdi will not form. Adding corn syrup prevents sugar crystallization.

steps: Wash the ginger nicely and peel it.
Cut it into small pieces.
Blend ginger, sugar, and milk together in a mixer.
Once blended well, heat one tablespoon of ghee in a kadhai on the gas.
Pour the blended ginger-milk mixture into that kadhai and let it heat.
When the milk reduces and thickens, add dry ginger powder and take it off the heat.
Add one tablespoon of ghee to it.
Grease a plate with ghee and set the pak.
Apply varakh on top.
Then make pieces.
35.note: A great pak can also be made with 4 tablespoons of malai and 200 ml of milk. Add malai when the milk reduces and thickens. Keep adupak slightly softer compared to other paks.

steps: Heat ghee in a pan, add semolina (rava), and roast on low heat until it turns light brown.
Meanwhile, in another pan, add sugar to 1 cup of water and place it on the stove to heat.
Once the sugar dissolves in the water, add the roasted semolina (rava), cashew pieces, and cardamom powder, and stir on low heat.
When the mixture becomes slightly thick and soft, turn off the heat and stir for a while with the heat off.
Once the mixture is ready, grease a plate with ghee and spread it evenly.
Spread the sliced almonds on top.
After 10-15 minutes, cut into your desired shape.
36.note: The mixture will become slightly hard once cooled, so keep it a bit soft initially. Amrutpak can also be made with different colored layers, such as orange, white, and green, by dividing the prepared Mawa into three parts, mixing colors, and making three layers.

steps: Heat ghee in a pan, add rice flour, and roast until light brown.
Next, take 2 cups of water in a pan, add sugar, let it heat, and make a single-thread syrup.
Now add the roasted rice flour and cardamom powder to it. Once it reaches the consistency of Shira, spread it on a plate greased with ghee and scatter sliced almonds and pistachios on top.
Once the Hariso cools down, cut into your favorite shapes.
Put milk to boil in a pot.
In a parallel pan, add ghee and roast the vermicelli on low heat until light brown.
When the milk comes to a boil, first add the vermicelli to it.
Then mix in the dry fruits and add the sugar.
Let it boil for 10-15 minutes, then turn off the heat and mix in the cardamom powder.
In a bowl, mix wheat flour, maida (all-purpose flour), salt, oil, and cardamom powder thoroughly and knead a slightly firm dough.
After half an hour, take pieces of this prepared dough the size of a Sata and poke holes on the top side.
Then fry all the pieces in ghee until brown in color.
Now, in a pan, make a syrup slightly thicker than a two-thread consistency, add the fried Thor, and mix well so that the syrup coats all the Thor evenly, then place them on a plate to cool.
39.note: Rava can also be added to the dough. Rose water can also be added to the syrup.

steps: Remove the inner core and skin of the ash gourd (pumpkin) and cut into large 2-2 inch square pieces.
Put 2 spoons of baking soda in a pot, poke holes in all the pieces, and soak them in water for 12 hours.
Then wash all the pieces 7-8 times in clean water and boil them in fresh water for 20 minutes.
Next, add 1200 grams of sugar to about 2 liters of water, and as soon as the sugar dissolves, add all the pieces and boil while stirring for 20 to 25 minutes.
Then let it sit for 12 hours, put the pot back on the stove, and thicken the syrup again for 12 minutes.
Once all the pieces absorb the syrup, drain them on a slotted rack and leave them spread out in the open air for 10 hours.
This will not spoil for up to two months.
Heat 3 tablespoons of ghee in a pan, add cinnamon, cloves, and bay leaf, then add the rice soaked for 2 hours.
Once roasted for 3 minutes, add 2 cups of water and let it roast for another 5 minutes.
Then add 1/2 cup of sugar and then add saffron.
Let it cook for another 7 minutes.
Once the sugar dissolves completely, garnish with cashews, almonds, pistachios, raisins, and cardamom powder, and serve hot.
First, make a one-string sugar syrup and add cardamom powder, kewra water, and lemon juice to it.
Now take ghee in a mixer jar, add cold dahi and 2-3 ice cubes, and mix well.
Then add some cold water and mix. Now add maida (all-purpose flour) in two parts and blend.
At the same time, add cold water and finally besan and water to prepare the batter.
About 500 grams of water will be used; make sure the batter is neither too thin nor too thick.
Prepare a medium consistency batter, fill it in a bottle, and keep it in the fridge to keep it cold.
Now heat ghee for frying in a pan or deep vessel.
Once the ghee is hot, slowly pour the batter filled in the bottle.
Do not pour all the batter at once so the ghee does not spill out; keep pouring the batter repeatedly until the circular shape is fully formed and the ghebar turns brown.
Once the ghebar is fried well, prepare the remaining ghebar.
Place 3-4 ghebar on top of each other, pour the prepared sugar syrup all over them, and garnish with pistachios and saffron.
In a bowl, add warm milk and ghee to the urad dal flour and rub for 3-4 minutes to give moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour).
Then heat ghee in a pan and add the moyan-mixed flour.
Continuously stir this mixture on medium heat until it turns brown.
Add fried edible gum (gond), grated dry coconut, cardamom powder, dry ginger powder, and nutmeg, and transfer the mixture to a bowl.
Then prepare a 1-string sugar syrup, add the flour mixture to it, and mix both together.
Grease a plate with ghee, transfer this mixture into it, spread it evenly, and press it down with your hands.
Then add almond and pistachio slices and cut into square pieces.
43.note: After the mixture cools down a bit, it can be shaped by hand as shown in the photo.

steps: To make the filling:
Roast mawa (khoya) in a pan on low heat in half a spoonful of ghee for 5-7 minutes.
In another pan, roast gram flour (besan) in 1 spoonful of ghee.
In a bowl, mix the roasted mawa (khoya) and roasted gram flour (besan) and keep it aside to cool.
After cooling, mix cardamom powder, almond powder, crushed pistachios, and bura (powdered sugar), and make small balls. Ghari puri:
For the puri, mix maida (all-purpose flour) and ghee, add water to make a roti-like dough.
Make small-sized puris from that dough, place a ball of the prepared filling in each puri, stuff it, and fry it in hot ghee on medium heat.
Fry only until the color of the ghari remains white.
After the ghari cools down, mix ghee and powdered sugar and spread it over the ghari, and garnish on top with pieces of pistachios, almonds, and saffron.
Heat the ghee and roast the flour in it on low heat.
When about 25% roasted, crush the jaggery and add it.
When about 50% roasted, the jaggery will blend in.
Take it down and add cardamom.
If the jaggery is not hot, press it with a bowl and mix it while hot.
It will remain loose and crumbly.
First take the flour.
Add jaggery to it and mix well.
Then add ghee little by little and mix well.
46.note: It can also be made with bajra (pearl millet) flour using the same method. It can be kept loose or shaped into lundus.

steps: Rub moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) into the maida (all-purpose flour) and knead into a stiff dough like sata.
Make a long roll from the dough like a kajurol and cut it into 2 or 2-1/2 inch pieces.
Fry them on low heat in ghee or oil just like sata.
After frying well, put them aside to drain.
The next day, make sugar syrup by adding just enough water to submerge the sugar.
Then dip the prepared gagan ganthia into it.
Then remove them from the syrup and place them on a plate.
First heat ghee in a pan.
Now sauté the cracked wheat in it until it turns pink.
Now heat water on the stove on the side.
Now add water to the cracked wheat after it is sautéed.
Now add cashews, charoli (chironji), almonds, and raisins to it.
Now cover it.
Now after all the water has evaporated, check whether the lapsi is cooked or not. If the lapsi is cooked, then add sugar and stir.
Stir until the sugar water evaporates.
Now add cardamom powder and stir.
Hot lapsi is ready.
48.note: Do not sauté too much in ghee initially, because if it is over-sautéed, it will not absorb water. Add sugar only after adding water and when it is completely cooked, otherwise it will become chewy.

steps: Mash the boiled potatoes by hand and add green peas, salt to taste, coriander-cumin powder, turmeric, garam masala, and fresh coriander leaves, and mix everything well.
Now mix salt and oil well into the maida (all-purpose flour) and knead a moderately soft dough with water.
Apply oil, cover it, and keep it aside for 10 minutes.
Then make equal-sized dough balls, roll them into oval rotis, and fill the stuffing in the center.
Now bring both sides together, shape it like a ghughra, and seal it.
Put oil to heat in a pan and fry all the ghughra in it on medium heat until light brown.
Make a hole in the center of the ghughra and serve by adding all the chutneys, sev, masala peanuts, and fresh coriander leaves on top.

ing: moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) oil – 100 grams
steps: First mix oil moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) into the flour. Put water to heat on the stove and add jaggery to it.
After the jaggery dissolves, let it come to a boil.
Lower the gas and sprinkle the flour mixed with moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) on top. Spread it all around so a layer forms on top.
Add more where it pops up on top.
When it is spread all around on top and water tries to come up, make holes with a rolling pin and bubbles will start to form.
Make holes in several places and the water will slowly start absorbing into the flour.
Slowly move the dry flour on top. Water will start getting absorbed on top again.
Make cuts with a spatula as the water almost blends in.
Slowly slide the spatula underneath and prevent it from sticking. Keep the gas very low.
Add a little 25% ghee, now it will not stick.
Keep covering while ensuring it does not stick. Add the remaining 50% ghee and keep stirring, the lapsi will be made in 30 minutes.
Take it off the heat, add cardamom and cashews-almonds, add the remaining 25% ghee, and let it cool.
The lapsi will separate, do not worry if it burns a little bit, it will bring sweetness.
In a heavy-bottomed vessel, add ghee and then add the vermicelli (sev).
Sauté the vermicelli on low heat for about 7 minutes until it turns brown.
Then add milk and one cup of water, and cook for another 5 minutes.
After that, add sugar, saffron, and cardamom powder, and keep stirring until the sugar dissolves completely and the water and milk evaporate.
Now garnish with sliced pistachios and serve hot.
First, take cornflour and 1 1/2 cups of water in a bowl and mix well.
Now take sugar in a large non-stick pan, add 1 cup of water, and let it boil.
Now pour the cornflour mixture into the boiling sugar syrup.
Additionally, keep stirring continuously on medium heat.
Then, as soon as the cornflour mixture starts boiling and thickening, add the lemon juice.
Keep stirring until this mixture thickens completely.
Now add ghee to it and mix continuously until all the ghee is absorbed.
Then, when the mixture becomes transparent and silky and starts releasing ghee, add orange food color, cardamom powder, and chopped cashews.
Now continue mixing until the mixture begins to form a lump.
Afterwards, transfer the mixture into a tray.
Garnish the top with sliced almonds and set aside for an hour.
Now cut it into square pieces.
First, combine maida (all-purpose flour) flour, sugar, and milk in a non-stick pan and keep stirring and mixing until the sugar dissolves.
Now place the pan with the mixed ingredients on medium heat to warm and keep stirring.
When the mixture starts to heat and bubbles appear, lower the heat, and it will gradually become thicker and start binding.
Meanwhile, soak the saffron and add it to this mixture so it takes on a nice color, and if a stronger color is desired, a little turmeric can be added.
While stirring continuously, the mixture will thicken and should not stick to the pan.
Once the halwa is properly cooked, remove it and let it cool on a sheet of foil paper greased with ghee.

Now once cooled, spread it on the foil paper, roll it thin, spread cardamom powder and almond-pistachio slices over it, place butter paper on top of the rolled halwa, and gently roll it again with a light hand.
Leave this halwa outside for 5 hours so that it dries, and cut it into appropriately sized square pieces using a roller cutter.
First, heat a pan and add ghee to it.
Once the ghee melts, add the flour and roast it on medium heat, ensuring no lumps are formed.
Roast until the color turns brown.
Now add sugar, turn the gas to high, and immediately add water while stirring continuously.
Now stir for 3-4 minutes to ensure no lumps form.
Now add grated dry coconut and cardamom powder to it.
Mix everything well and roast on low heat for 2 minutes.
Add dry fruits and mix.
Heat ghee in a pan and roast the cashews, almonds, and pistachios in it.
Once they are roasted, add raisins and then remove everything into a bowl.
Now in the same ghee, add semolina (rava) and roast it until each grain appears separate and the ghee separates.
Now add water, mix well, cover it, and let it cook on medium heat for 1 minute.
Then stir, add the roasted dry fruits, sugar, and cardamom powder, mix well, and serve piping hot.
Soak the yellow moong dal for 3-4 hours, drain the water, and grind it.
Now, heat ghee in a pan and roast semolina (rava) and besan in it until golden.
Now add the ground moong dal to it and roast until golden.
In another pan, take water, add sugar to it, add saffron and cardamom, and let it boil for five minutes.
Then add the sugar syrup to the pan containing the roasted moong dal and rava mixture, stir on high flame until the syrup is properly absorbed and ghee separates.
Top with dry fruits and serve hot.
56.note: Always roast the moong dal on a low flame, otherwise lumps will form.

steps: First, take maida (all-purpose flour), add water, and knead a dough like for puri. (Keep covered for 10 minutes)
Now mix and whisk ghee, oil, and corn starch.
After it is mixed, make balls from the maida (all-purpose flour) dough.
Make a hole in the center of the dough ball with your finger, roll it in the ghee-oil mixture, and keep it for 10 minutes.
Then gently stretch the dough ball lengthwise, leaving space in the middle, and fold it twice by hand.
Twist 1 dough ball like this 5-7 times and double the folds each time, such as 2 into 4 and then 8.
Thus there should be 36 folds.
Prepare all the dough balls by stretching and using your finger in the ghee-oil mixture this way.
Now heat oil for frying in a pan.
Then, when the oil is fully hot, drop one ball of tangled dough into it and fry on a low flame.
Keep stirring the tangled dough occasionally using a fork.
Now nice thin strands will separate out.
Take it out and make the sugar syrup while it cools. Method for making sugar syrup:
Add sugar and water in a vessel.
Heat on low flame.
Stir until a 1-string consistency syrup is formed.
Then add some saffron (5-7 strands) and cardamom to it.
Then pour the sugar syrup over the sutarfeni using a spoon and garnish with pistachio slivers on top.
57.note: Add water depending on whether you want the sugar syrup thick or thin.

steps: First, mix the baking soda, ghee, and water as needed into the maida (all-purpose flour) to knead a stiff dough like paratha.
Cover and rest the dough for 25-30 minutes.
Now make flat dough balls like roti dough, and prick them slightly with a fork so they do not puff up while frying.
Then heat oil/ghee in a pan and fry the dough balls on low heat.
Keep turning them on both sides and fry until they turn light yellow.
Next, dip them in the sugar syrup. Method for making sugar syrup:
Mix sugar and water in a pan and heat it on the stove.
Now, after a few bubbles form, take a little syrup in 1 spoon to check.
The syrup should be of two-string consistency.

Then, after the syrup cools down a little, drop the fried sata into it one by one and turn them on both sides. Grease a plate with a little ghee and place them in it so the syrup does not stick to the plate.
After 30 minutes, the sata will be ready to eat.

ing: edible gum (gond) from babul tree - 2 tablespoons
steps: First, put the milk to boil in a pan, and after it gets a little warm, add the curd to it and keep stirring the milk frequently.
In the meantime, crush the lumps of babul gum and fry it in 1 ½ tablespoons of ghee on low heat; it should puff up completely and get a light brown color.
After adding curd to the milk, it will start curdling. During this, add this gum directly into it without needing to powder it because it will dissolve in the milk on its own.
Now roast the coarse wheat flour in 1 ½ tablespoons of ghee on low heat.
Meanwhile, add malai to the milk. Roast the flour until it turns golden brown, and once roasted, add it to the milk.
The texture of the milk will have become like paneer, and it should be stirred frequently so it does not stick to the bottom.
Now the sugar needs to be melted without water. Once the sugar is caramelized, add it to the milk while stirring.
As the milk heats up, the sugar will blend into it. Now add 2-3 strands of saffron to the milk.
After it thickens a little, add the cardamom powder, nutmeg powder, and mace powder combined.
Keep stirring the prepared mixture, and when it becomes like thick mawa (khoya), increase the heat a little and stir it continuously, letting it heat until it forms a ball.
Now turn off the gas and keep stirring it so that the steam escapes and water does not separate.
After it cools down, spread it on a plate, roll it into peda-shaped balls, and place sliced pistachios and almonds on top.
Consume this sweet after 24 hours.
First, sift the rice flour in a bowl, add bura (powdered sugar) to it, and mix well.
Then add ghee to it and mix the mixture well with light hands.
And afterwards, shape them into small-sized balls.
60.note: In Saurashtra, Kansaar is made this way, and in the Gujarat region, wheat flour lapsi is called Kansaar.

ing: oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) – 3 tablespoons
steps: Take maida (all-purpose flour) in a bowl, mix oil in it, and give proper moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour).
Khaja tastes good only if it has enough moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) that holds its shape when clenched in the fist.
If the oil feels less, you can add another teaspoon.
Now, adding water little by little, prepare the dough.
Knead the dough such that it is neither too hard nor too soft, knead for 2-3 minutes, and then cover and keep it aside for 15 minutes.
Now, take sugar and half the amount of water in a pan and make a sugar syrup on the stove over low heat.
To make a single-thread consistency syrup, check it; when a single thread forms, the syrup is ready.
Now knead the prepared dough again for a short while to make it smooth.
Then make roti-sized dough balls and roll out rotis using dry flour (dry maida (all-purpose flour)) for dusting.
Then apply oil on the roti and sprinkle dry flour.
Now spread it with your hand and place another roti on top of it, placing a total of five rotis one on top of the other.
Then from one side, roll all the rotis tightly ensuring no air remains inside.
While rolling, bring the edges of all rotis together and apply water properly so the layers do not separate.
Then cut equal-sized pieces about half an inch thick from it.
Then take one piece and apply light pressure with your hands to give it an elongated shape.
Then fry them in moderately warm oil on a low flame.
Frying on low heat will cause the layers to start separating.
Fry them to a light golden brown color.
If the prepared sugar syrup has cooled down, warm it up.
Once the khaja cool down, dip them one by one into the sugar syrup and take them out after a little while.
Sweet khaja are ready.
Sift the gram flour (besan) in a bowl.
Add 150 ml of water to it to make a slightly thick batter.
Make this batter by adding water little by little.
The batter should be thick enough so that when you keep it on a strainer, it falls drop by drop.
While preparing the mixture, take special care that there are no lumps in the gram flour (besan) mixture.
Stir the mixture well for 5-6 minutes or until it becomes completely smooth.
Add two big spoons of oil to it and stir again.
Cover and keep this prepared batter aside for 10-15 minutes.
Take sugar and water in a vessel and keep it on the gas on low heat until it comes to one boil to make sugar syrup.
When the syrup becomes sticky, mix cardamom powder in it.
Then heat oil for frying in a thick-bottomed wide pan.
After it becomes hot, drop boondi into it using a strainer.
When the color of the boondi changes and it becomes crispy, remove the boondi.
Take out the boondi from the pan and keep putting it into the sugar syrup, pressing it gently.
After 1-2 minutes, take out the boondi from the syrup.
Boondi is ready.

ing: Water - enough to submerge the sugar
Cashew and almond pieces – as needed
steps: First of all, mash the paneer.
Then add mawa (khoya) to it and mix and mash both.
After mixing, mix cardamom powder and maida (all-purpose flour) into it and mash well for 10 minutes.
Then make balls out of it.
Make balls, make a cavity in the center, place cashew and almond pieces mixed with red food color, and roll them round again.
Now fry them and take them out when they turn black.
Prepare a 1-thread sugar syrup by adding enough water to submerge the sugar.
Add kala jamun to it.
Juicy kala jamun is ready.

ing: A pinch of baking soda – 1/4 teaspoon
steps: Method: 1
First, soak semolina in a little milk in a bowl. Then grate mawa (khoya) into it.
Add maida (all-purpose flour), a pinch of baking soda, and crushed cardamom to the mawa and knead well.
Then roll 1 small ball and fry it in ghee to check; if it cracks, add a little maida (all-purpose flour).
Then fry all the balls on low heat until pink.
On the other hand, take enough water to submerge the sugar and make a 1/2-string syrup.
When the sugar dissolves and boils a little, it means the syrup is ready.
After the fried balls cool down, add them to the syrup.
After 5 to 8 hours, the gulab jamuns are ready after fully absorbing the syrup. Method: 2
Keep mawa (khoya), paneer, and maida (all-purpose flour) in a large vessel and knead it until it becomes soft and smooth.
The mawa (khoya) for making gulab jamuns is ready.
Prepare the sugar syrup before frying the gulab jamuns. Method of making syrup:
Mix sugar and 300 grams of water in a vessel (take half the water compared to sugar).
Put it on the gas stove to heat and make syrup.
When the syrup comes to a boil, let it cook for another 4-5 minutes.
Make a one-string syrup.
After making the one-string syrup this way, let it cool and then strain it. Method of making gulab jamuns:
Roll small balls from the prepared mawa.
Heat ghee in a kadhai.
Then drop one ball to check.
If it cracks, add a little maida (all-purpose flour) to the mawa and knead it again slightly.
Then fry 3-4 balls in the kadhai.
Keep the gas low and stir gently with a spatula.
After cooling slightly, submerge them in the syrup after two minutes.
Keeping the fried gulab jamuns in the syrup for 8-10 hours will make them sweet and delicious.
Gulab jamun is ready.
64.note: Method-1: Using 50 grams of maida instead of 50 grams of semolina also makes good gulab jamuns. Method-2: If the mawa becomes too stiff, add 1 ½ teaspoons of milk to it and knead the mawa well. Do not add gulab jamuns to very hot syrup.

steps: Apply ghee to the inside of the vessel in which the milk is to be heated.
Then pour the milk and put it on to heat, stirring continuously so it doesn't stick.
When it comes to a proper boil, wash the rice, wipe it dry, and add it.
Once the rice is cooked, add sugar; when it boils well and gets a good color, take it off the heat.
Afterwards, add sliced almonds and pista.
Add charoli (chironji) and crushed cardamom.
Add crushed nutmeg and saffron (dissolved) to the milk.
Doodhpak tastes good warm.
First make the jaggery water, soak the jaggery in 150 ml of water. (for 1 to 2 hours)
Then strain the water using a strainer so that all the impurities are removed and the water becomes completely clean.
Then add wheat flour to it, adding a little bit at a time and keep mixing so that there are no lumps, make sure of this.
Add 250 ml of water and add more if needed.
Make a batter like dosa which should be smooth and keep it covered for 1 hour.
Add about 1 spoon of pepper into it and then mix well.
Once the oil is hot, pour the batter into the oil and fry it. (pour the batter into the oil using a ladle)
After pouring the batter, do not touch it, once it is properly fried it will come up on its own which means it is fried.
When it turns slightly reddish, remove it from the oil.
As soon as you take it out of the oil, sprinkle poppy seeds over it. Hot hot malpua is ready.
66.note: Instead of water in the wheat flour batter, milk can also be added.

steps: Combine all the ingredients for the jalebi batter to make a batter and keep it covered for 30 minutes.
The batter should be neither too thick nor too thin.
Now take a vessel, add sugar and water to prepare the sugar syrup.
Once the sugar dissolves, add cardamom powder and saffron to it and stir.
Now heat ghee in a flat kadhai (pan).
Fill the jalebi batter into a jalebi squeeze bottle.
Pipe the jalebi into hot ghee and fry it.
Dip the fried jalebi in the sugar syrup for a short while and take it out.
Make all the jalebis in this manner.
Place them in a dish and decorate with almond and pistachio slivers on top.
Hot hot jalebi is ready.
Always use fresh paneer to make rasgulla.
Take the paneer in a dish and knead it very well using the palm for 10 minutes.
It should become completely soft.
Then make medium-sized balls from it.
Then now heat 5-6 glasses of water in a kadhai to make sugar syrup and add 3 cups of sugar to it and stir.
After the sugar dissolves, when the syrup starts boiling, add the rasgulla balls into it.
Now let it boil for about 10 minutes, the size of each ball will double.
Then add them one by one into some cold water to cool down.
Now take them in another bowl, slowly pour the prepared sugar water over them and add saffron strands on top.
Now let them rest in the fridge for 7 to 8 hours.
Sweet and delicious rasgulla are ready.
First wash the urad dal properly in two or three waters and soak it for 5 to 6 hours.
Then to make the sugar syrup, heat 300 grams of sugar and 1/2 liter of water in a kadhai.
Heat it until the syrup becomes thick (2-3 thread consistency) and sticky, then let it cool.
Then make a paste of the soaked urad dal in a mixer.
Then add one tea spoon of orange food color to it.
Then stir it very well to mix the ingredients.
Now put oil in a kadhai to heat.
Then fill the prepared paste into a plastic bag or sauce bottle and pipe ring-shaped round shapes in the oil.
Then once fried, submerge it in the sugar syrup for 5 minutes. Then take it out in a dish.
Bengali Kamal Bhog:
First knead the paneer well to make it completely soft.
Then add 1 spoon of semolina (rava), 1 spoon of maida (all-purpose flour) and 1 spoon of orange powder to it and knead well using the palm for 5 minutes.
Then make medium balls from it.
Then heat 3 cups of orange juice in a kadhai, add 1 ½ cups of sugar to it and make its syrup.
Once the syrup is made, add cardamom to it.
Then add the prepared balls to it.
Keep the gas on low heat and cover for 10-15 minutes so the size of the balls will double and they will become very soft.
Then strain the syrup and serve the prepared kamal bhog. Kaju Kamal Bhog:
First grind cold cashews into a complete powder.
Heat milk in a kadhai, add sugar to it and let the sugar dissolve.
Now add cashew powder, milk powder and ghee to that milk and keep stirring it well.
Now when it becomes like stiff mawa (khoya), turn off the gas, take it out onto a good plastic sheet and knead it.
Now divide it into three parts.
Mix red food color in one part, yellow in the second and green in the third.
Now make uniform small balls from the red colored portion.
Apply a layer of yellow color over those balls and apply a layer of green color over it.
Now apply silver leaf over the entire ball and cut it like a lotus as shown in the photo.
Kaju Kamal Bhog is ready.
First, turn on the stove on low heat, place a kadhai on it, and add 1 spoonful of butter.
Mix 1 cup of milk powder and 1/4 cup of cocoa powder in this kadhai.
Now add 400 grams of malai and mix. Stir until it is well mixed and thick.
Then add 1/4 cup of milk to it and stir well for exactly 4 minutes.
After letting it cool for 5 minutes, shape it into penda.
Finally, place one cashew nut on top of each.
First, put sugar and water in a kadhai.
Now keep stirring it on the gas until the sugar dissolves.
Then, when a few bubbles form, take it off the heat.
Now mix ghee and water in a bowl.
Then add baking soda, curd, and maida (all-purpose flour) to it, knead a medium dough, and let the dough covered for 5 minutes.
Then make equal-sized dough balls.
In each dough ball, press with your finger to make a hole halfway through.
Then fry them in oil on low heat.
Immediately after frying, keep them in the sugar syrup for a short while and take them out.
Balushahi is ready.
72.note: Ghee can also be used for frying.

steps: Soak the rice, dry it, and then grind it (grind in a mixer).
Next, take 100 ml of milk in a bowl and dissolve the chocolate powder so that no lumps form.
Then boil the remaining milk and add the ground rice to let it cook.
Add the chocolate powder milk to the boiled milk and add rice powder to it.
Boil until the milk thickens and serve after it cools down.
73.note: You can use any dry fruit of your choice as a topping.

steps: First, boil the milk and soak the saffron strands in warm milk in a bowl.
Then coarsely grind the rice.
Next, add the rice to the boiling milk and stir continuously.
Keep stirring until the rice is cooked. Then add sugar.
Stir until the rice is cooked in the milk and thickens.
Then add the soaked saffron, pista, cashew nuts, and cardamom powder.
Then chill it in the fridge for 3-4 hours.
First, take a pan and put the milk to heat on medium flame.
After it comes to a boil, lower the flame a bit.
Then add saffron strands and cardamom powder to it and stir.
Stir until the milk is reduced to half.
Once the milk is reduced to half, turn off the gas and put it in the fridge to cool.
Once cooled, add the bundi and sliced almonds and serve.
75.note: Bundi can also be added while the dudhpak is warm.

steps: First of all, heat the milk.
As soon as the milk comes to a boil, add sugar to it.
Then keep stirring.
After that, add the soaked poha into the hot milk.
Boil until it becomes slightly thick.
Then add the dry fruit pieces and saffron strands to it.
Then add cardamom powder.
Mix everything well.
Then place it on the terrace to cool down.
Take 5 cups of milk and rice in a pan and boil it well.
Now check whether the rice is cooked properly or not.
Once the rice is cooked, add the remaining 1 cup of milk to it.
Then add sugar, cardamom powder and nutmeg powder and let it boil again for 10-15 minutes.
After that, cut the cashews into pieces and add them.
Now chill the kheer and serve it.
77.note: Pista or almonds can also be added.

steps: For the stuffing (puran):
Soak the chana dal for 2-3 hours.
Then take the chana dal in a cooker, add water, salt, turmeric powder and oil to it and boil it.
Once the chana dal is boiled, crush the jaggery and add it, mixing until the jaggery dissolves.
Now let this mixture cook until it becomes thick like mawa (khoya).
Once it becomes thick, remove it from the stove and let it cool down.
Now take this stuffing in a mixer jar, add nutmeg powder and cardamom powder, and blend it into a smooth mixture.
Make equal-sized balls of it. For making the dough:
Now take wheat flour, maida (all-purpose flour), turmeric powder and salt in a bowl, mix well, add water and knead a soft dough.
Now take a large dough ball from the dough, roll it slightly, place a stuffing ball inside and seal it from all sides.
Make a dough ball again, dust dry wheat flour on the platform and roll it out to the size of a roti.
Now take a hot tawa to roast it, roast it like a paratha using ghee or oil, and serve it hot.
78.note: It can also be made using only wheat flour without maida.

ing: Deshi ghee (for roasting dates) – 2 small spoons
Oil (for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour)) – 2 teaspoons
steps: First, wash the dates thoroughly once with lukewarm water and then twice with plain water.
Keep all the ingredients ready for ease of preparation.
Now keep the dates in a perforated colander, drain the water and dry them.
Then remove the seeds and chop them finely.
Crush the dry fruits, and make powders of cardamom and nutmeg.
Now heat ghee in a pan, add the chopped dates, roast on medium flame and keep stirring.
Roast for 5 minutes or until they become slightly soft.
Now add crushed dry fruit, cardamom and nutmeg powder, and grated dry coconut to it and mix.
Transfer this mixture to another vessel and let it cool.
Then knead the dough, add moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) and keep it like roti dough so that it can be rolled without dry flour.
Then make equal dough balls of the prepared dough.
Knead the date mixture with your hands just like kneading dough and make 6 equal balls, pressing them slightly with your hands.
Place a tawa on the gas to heat, take a dough ball on the rolling board, roll it slightly, place the date ball in the center by pressing it slightly and seal it from all sides.
Press slightly and keeping the sealed side facing upwards, roll lightly. (Roll to a size smaller than a roti.)
Roll it this way and roast on both sides on the tawa on medium flame until pink.
Then take it out on a plate and apply pure ghee on top.
Keep rolling and roasting all of them in this way.
So the very delicious and healthy sweet khajur puran poli is ready.
For the stuffing (puran):
Soak the toor dal for 1 hour.
Then boil the toor dal with water in a pressure cooker.
Once the toor dal is boiled, transfer it to a kadhai.
Add jaggery and sugar to it, heat on the stove, and keep stirring.
When it starts to thicken, add nutmeg powder and cardamom powder.
Then take it off the stove. (Ensure it does not stick to the kadhai.) Method for kneading the dough:
Now, in a bowl, mix wheat flour with oil moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour), add water, and knead into a soft dough like roti dough.
Now take a large ball of dough, roll it out slightly, place a ball of stuffing in the center, and seal it from all sides.
Make a ball of it again and roll it out gently like a roti.
Now roast it on a hot tawa.
Flip it with a spatula, and once roasted, apply ghee on the top and bottom of the puran poli and serve hot.
Stuffing:
Heat ghee in a pan, add semolina (rava) and roast well until it turns golden in color.
Now add milk and jaggery to it, and stir until the jaggery dissolves and the milk evaporates.
Add cardamom and nutmeg powder to this mixture.
Then make small balls out of it. Outer crust:
In another bowl, take semolina (rava), a pinch of sugar and maida (all-purpose flour), add warm ghee and mix.
Add enough milk to make a soft dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, add a little more milk if needed, then make small-sized balls.
Roll them into small puris, stuff the filling inside, and roll out the puri again.
Heat medium ghee in a pan and fry the puris until they turn golden brown.
Place the fried puris on paper to absorb excess oil and let them cool down.
For the stuffing:
First, heat ghee in a pan.
Add figs and pitted dates to it, sauté well while stirring continuously.
Now add mixed dry fruit powder and cardamom powder and mix well.
Turn off the stove, and once it cools down, make small balls out of it. For the dough:
Now in a bowl, add wheat flour, maida (all-purpose flour), turmeric, salt and oil, and mix well.
Then add water and knead a soft dough.
Take a large lump of dough, flatten it slightly, place an fig stuffing ball inside, and seal it from all sides.
Make a ball again, dust the platform with dry wheat flour, and roll it out to the size of a roti.
Now roast it on a hot tawa like a paratha using ghee or oil and serve hot.
82.note: If you want to make this sweeter, you can add sugar to taste. The dough for puran poli can also be made using only wheat flour.

steps: First, heat ghee in a pan and roast the roasted split gram (daliya) in it.
Now in another pan, take jaggery and a little water to make the jaggery syrup (payo).
When the jaggery syrup turns brown, add the roasted split gram (daliya) to it.
Then add cardamom powder and baking soda and mix well.
Adding baking soda keeps the chiki soft.
Now mix everything well, remove it from the stove, spread it flat on a platform, and cut it into pieces of appropriate size.
83.note: Keep the gas flame medium while making the jaggery syrup. To check if the syrup is ready, take a little water in a bowl. Add a pinch of the syrup into it and try to break it with your hand. If the syrup is raw, it will stretch like rubber, and if it is done, it will break immediately.

steps: Take ghee in a pan and heat it on medium flame.
Once the ghee melts, add condensed milk to it.
Then add sugar and mix well.
When the milk starts thickening, add cocoa powder and mix well while stirring.
When the mixture starts thickening, turn off the gas and spread it evenly in a greased dish.
Let the barfi cool down. Cut it into your favorite shape with a knife before it sets completely.
Now garnish it with sliced pistachios.
84.note: After adding condensed milk, keep the gas on low flame and stir continuously, otherwise it will burn from the bottom.

steps: Sauté walnuts in a pan for 2 to 3 minutes.
Then, after they cool down, grind them in a mixer to prepare a fine powder.
Now take ghee in a pan, heat it, add the walnut powder and mix.
Roast until the ghee is fully absorbed.
Now add milk, sugar and saffron to it.
Mix everything well and stir until the mixture thickens.
After 15 minutes, the mixture will become very thick and start leaving the sides of the pan.
Now add cardamom powder to it and mix well.
Then apply a little ghee on a plate, spread the mixture, add small walnut pieces on top and let it cool down.
After it cools down, make cuts into it.
So the walnut barfi is ready.
Saute the pineapple pieces in a pan for 2 minutes and grind them to prepare.
Now take this mixture in a pan and heat it on medium heat.
Add sugar to it and mix the sugar well.
Now add ghee, mawa (khoya) and grated dry coconut to it and mix well.
Then add pineapple essence, yellow color and cashew pieces, mix well and let it thicken.
When the mixture becomes thick, turn off the gas and spread it evenly in a greased dish.
Let the barfi cool and before it hardens, cut it into your favorite shape using a knife.
First of all, make a three-thread sugar syrup using sugar and water.
Boil until the syrup becomes thick and stir it well.
Now take some ghee in a pan, and roast the mawa (khoya) in it, add cardamom powder to it.
Now add pistachio powder, green color, saffron and sugar syrup to this mixture and mix well.
Now spread this pistachio mixture in a greased dish.
Add sliced pistachios on top and after some time cut into your favorite shape.
First of all, make a three-thread sugar syrup using sugar and water.
Boil until the syrup becomes thick and stir it well.
Now take some ghee in a pan, and roast the mawa (khoya) in it.
Then add sugar syrup to it and mix it.
Now add rose petals and rose essence to it and mix well.
Then divide this mixture into two parts.
Add pink color to one part and mix well.
Now first spread the white mawa (khoya) in a greased dish, and spread the pink mawa (khoya) over it.
After some time, cut them into squares, garnish with sliced pistachio-almonds and serve.
First of all, make a three-thread sugar syrup using sugar and water.
Boil until the syrup becomes thick and stir it well.
Now take some ghee in a pan, and roast the mawa (khoya) in it.
Divide the roasted mawa into three parts.
Now add one-third of the sugar syrup to one part of the mawa and mix well.
No color is to be added to this barfi.
Now spread this mixture in a greased dish.
Add pistachio powder and green color to the second part of mawa along with the second part of syrup and mix it.
Now spread this green colored mixture over the white mawa in the greased dish.
Now add saffron, orange color and the remaining part of sugar syrup to the third part of mawa and mix well.
Now spread this orange colored mixture over the green colored mixture.
After some time cut into squares and serve.
Which will appear in white, green and orange colors.
Peel the mango, cut it into pieces, and make a smooth paste in a mixer.
Cut the almonds into vertical slices.
Heat ghee in a non-stick pan, once the ghee is hot, add milk and keep stirring well.
After the milk comes to a boil, lower the flame.
Then add milk powder and keep stirring so that lumps do not form.
Boil and stir continuously until it thickens.
Once thick, add sugar and after the sugar dissolves, add the mango pulp to it.
Mix and stir on medium heat of the gas, and add cardamom powder to it.
Turn off the gas after it becomes sufficiently thick.
Now pour this mixture into a greased tray and spread it evenly.
Then garnish it with almonds and cashews.
After a while, make square pieces with a knife.
Then keep the barfi in the fridge or under the fan to set.
Once set, remove the pieces and serve.
90.note: Mawa can be used instead of milk powder. The amount of sugar can be increased or decreased according to the sourness of the mango.

steps: Knead the mawa well to loosen it.
Heat ghee in a non-stick pan, add mawa (khoya) and roast it on low heat while stirring continuously.
After mawa (khoya) melts, add condensed milk and mix well.
Then add the kesar previously soaked in milk and add the yellow color dissolved in a little water.
When this mixture thickens and does not stick to the pan, turn off the gas and transfer it to a bowl.
Once the mixture cools down a bit, shape them into penda of your favorite shape.
You can decorate it by placing pistachios or almonds on top.
In a pan, add ghee, milk, saffron, and mango pulp and heat it.
Stir it so that everything mixes well.
Then add sugar to it and stir until the sugar dissolves completely.
After that, add milk powder and cashew powder to it.
Make sure no lumps are formed in the milk powder.
Now keep roasting this mixture until it becomes thick and starts leaving the sides of the pan.
When the mixture becomes thick and does not stick to the pan, turn off the gas and take it out in a bowl.
When the mixture cools down a bit, shape them into pedas of your favorite shape.
You can decorate them by putting almond pieces on top.
Deseed the dates, clean them, cut them into pieces, and then boil the dates and milk in a pan.
After it comes to a good boil, turn off the gas and let it cool down.
After it cools down, add paneer to it and make a smooth paste in a mixer.
Now take ghee in a pan and roast the paneer and date paste on low heat.
After roasting for a while, add milk powder and sugar to it and mix well.
When the water from the sugar evaporates, turn off the gas.
When the mixture cools down a bit, make pedas of your favorite design.
Decorate by placing one raisin on top of each peda.
97.note: Mawa can also be used in place of paneer and milk powder.

98.serves: Quantity can be increased, and decreased according to taste. Here the time for preparing shrikhand after the curd is set is given. Even without ice cream
steps: First heat the milk until it is lukewarm, then add a spoon of curd to it.
Let it sit until the curd sets or for 6-8 hours.
Now after 6-8 hours, take out the set curd in a muslin cloth, make a tight bundle, and hang it.
After all the water drains out in about four hours, untie the bundle and take out the mawa (khoya) of the curd in a bowl.
Then add powdered sugar to it and sift this mixture through a fine sieve.
Now add essence, ice cream, cream, and pineapple pieces to it and mix everything well.
Then it can be served chilled from the fridge.
98.note: While setting the curd, make sure that the curd starter is not sour. Otherwise, the curd that sets will become sour. If the curd turns sour, sugar can be added to it.

99.serves: Quantity can be increased, and decreased according to taste. Here the time for preparing shrikhand after the curd is set is given. Even without ice cream
ing: Mix dry fruit – 100 grams (cashew, almond, pistachio, fig)
steps: First heat the milk until it is lukewarm, then add a spoon of curd to it and let it sit until the curd sets or for 6-8 hours.
Now after 6-8 hours, take out the set curd in a muslin cloth, make a tight bundle, and hang it.
Cut the dry fruits into small pieces and keep them ready.
After all the water drains out in about four hours, untie the bundle and take out the mawa (khoya) of the curd in a bowl.
Then add powdered sugar to it and sift this mixture through a fine sieve.
Now add essence, ice cream, cream, and mix dry fruits to it and mix everything well.
Then it can be served chilled from the fridge.
99.note: While setting the curd, make sure that the curd starter is not sour. Otherwise, the curd that sets will become sour. If the curd turns sour, sugar can be added to it.

100.serves: Quantity can be increased, and decreased according to taste. Here the time for preparing shrikhand after the curd is set is given.
steps: First heat the milk until it is lukewarm, then add a spoon of curd to it and let it sit until the curd sets or for 6-8 hours.
Now after 6-8 hours, take out the set curd in a muslin cloth, make a tight bundle, and hang it.
Now extract the juice of 1 Kesar mango, and cut 2 mangoes into pieces and put them in the fridge to chill.
After all the water drains out in about four hours, untie the bundle and take out the mawa (khoya) of the curd in a bowl.
Then add powdered sugar to it and sift this mixture through a fine sieve.
Now add orange color, mango pieces, and juice to it and mix everything well.
Then it can be served chilled from the fridge.
100.note: While setting the curd, make sure that the curd starter is not sour. Otherwise, the curd that sets will become sour. If the curd turns sour...

steps: Set the milk to make curd, then strain the water from that curd and prepare the masko like shrikhand.
Approximately 1 ½ kg of masko will be prepared from 4 liters of milk.
Sift this mixture through a sieve.
Then add water and mix in cardamom, nutmeg, almonds, pistachios, and saffron.
Shadki is ready.

ing: Mixed dry fruits – 100 grams (cashews, almonds, figs, raisins)
steps: First, heat the milk and when it remains lukewarm, add one spoon of curd to it and let it rest for 6-8 hours until the curd sets.
After 6-8 hours, remove the set curd into a muslin cloth, make a tight bundle and hang it.
Now cut the mixed dry fruits into small pieces.
After all the water has drained out in about four hours, untie the bundle and take the curd masko out into a bowl.
Then add powdered sugar to it and sift this mixture through a fine sieve.
Now add essence, ice cream, cream, dry fruits, jelly, and chocolate chips and mix everything well.
Then it can be served chilled from the fridge.
102.note: Use a starter culture that ensures the curd does not turn sour. If the curd turns sour, the amount of sugar can be increased, and it can also be reduced according to taste.

steps: Put the curd in a muslin cloth, tie the cloth from all four sides and hang it in such a way that the water drains out from it.
It will take about 7-8 hours.
Then press the cloth from the outside to remove any excess water.
Then whip the curd in an empty vessel for 10 minutes until it becomes light.
Then add powdered sugar and cardamom powder to it, mix and stir until smooth.
When the shrikhand is ready, chill it in the fridge and serve.
103.note: The measurement of sugar depends on the solid mass (mawa) remaining after straining the curd. Bricks used in construction can be used to quickly drain water from the curd. For that, spread the bricks on the ground to make a flat layer. Spread paper on it and spread a muslin cloth on top of it. Now put the curd on the cloth, fold the cloth properly and spread another cloth on top of it. Then place a layer of paper and bricks on top of it again. Doing this will separate all the water from the curd in about 1 hour.

steps: Put the curd in a muslin cloth, tie the cloth from all four sides and hang it in such a way that the water drains out from it.
It will take about 7-8 hours.
Then press the cloth from the outside to remove any excess water.
Then whip the curd in an empty vessel for 10 minutes until it becomes light.
Then add powdered sugar, sapodilla pieces, grapes, pineapple pieces, strawberry pieces, and custard apple pulp to it.
Mix well and stir until smooth.
When the shrikhand is ready, chill it in the fridge and serve.
104.note: The measurement of sugar depends on the solid mass (mawa) remaining after straining the curd. Bricks used in construction can be used to quickly drain water from the curd. For that, spread the bricks on the ground to make a flat layer. Spread paper on it and spread a muslin cloth on top of it. Now put the curd on the cloth, fold the cloth properly and spread another cloth on top of it. Then place a layer of paper and bricks on top of it again. Doing this will separate all the water from the curd in about 1 hour.

steps: Put the curd in a muslin cloth, tie the cloth from all four sides and hang it in such a way that the water drains out from it.
It will take about 7-8 hours.
Then press the cloth from the outside to remove any excess water.
Then whip the curd in an empty vessel for 10 minutes until it becomes light.
Soak the saffron in a little warm milk and keep it aside.
Then add powdered sugar, cashew pieces, dry grapes (raisins), saffron, and sliced almonds to it, mix and stir until smooth.
When the shrikhand is ready, chill it in the fridge and serve.
105.note: The measurement of sugar depends on the solid mass (mawa) remaining after straining the curd. Bricks used in construction can be used to quickly drain water from the curd. For that, spread the bricks on the ground to make a flat layer. Spread paper on it and spread a muslin cloth on top of it. Now put the curd on the cloth, fold the cloth properly and spread another cloth on top of it. Then place a layer of paper and bricks on top of it again. Doing this will separate all the water from the curd in about 1 hour.

steps: Put the curd in a muslin cloth, tie the cloth from all four sides, and keep it in another vessel for 2 hours so that the water drains out.
After 2 hours, squeeze the cloth from the outside to remove any excess water.
Then take out the curd in an empty bowl, add powdered sugar, butterscotch chips, butterscotch essence, and butterscotch sauce, and mix well until smooth.
Once the shrikhand is ready, chill it in the refrigerator and serve.
Put the curd in a muslin cloth, tie the cloth from all four sides, and keep it in another vessel for 2 hours so that the water drains out.
After 2 hours, squeeze the cloth from the outside to remove any excess water.
Then take out the curd in an empty bowl, add powdered sugar, cashew pieces, almond slivers, pistachio slivers, and cardamom powder, and mix well until smooth.
Once the shrikhand is ready, chill it in the refrigerator and serve.

ing: Mixed dry fruit – 150 grams (cashews, almonds, pistachios, figs)
steps: First, boil the milk and let it cool down to lukewarm. Then add a teaspoon of curd to it and let it set until it turns into curd or for 6-8 hours.
Now, after 6-8 hours, transfer the set curd into a muslin cloth, make a tight bundle, and hang it.
Cut the dry fruits into small pieces and keep them ready.
After about four hours, once all the water has drained completely, untie the bundle and take out the mawa (khoya) of the curd in a bowl.
Then add powdered sugar to it and sift this mixture through a fine sieve.
Now add essence, ice cream, cream, chocolate chips, tutti frutti, and mixed dry fruits, and mix everything well.
Then chill it in the refrigerator and serve.
108.note: Keep the curd mawa quite firm; if the mawa remains soft, it will turn into matho.

steps: Put the curd in a muslin cloth, tie the cloth from all four sides, and keep it in another vessel for 2 hours so that the water drains out.
After 2 hours, squeeze the cloth from the outside to remove any excess water.
Then take out the curd in an empty bowl, add powdered sugar and cardamom powder, and mix well until smooth.
Once the shrikhand is ready, chill it in the refrigerator and serve.
109.note: Cardamom seeds can be added as a topping on top.

steps: First, boil the milk and let it cool down to lukewarm. Then add a teaspoon of curd to it and let it set until it turns into curd or for 6-8 hours.
Now, after 6-8 hours, transfer the set curd into a muslin cloth, make a tight bundle, and hang it.
Cut the dry fruits into small pieces and keep them ready.
After about four hours, once all the water has drained completely, untie the bundle and take out the mawa (khoya) of the curd in a bowl.
Then add powdered sugar to it and sift this mixture through a fine sieve.
Now add saffron soaked in milk, cream, and mixed dry fruits, and mix everything well.
Then chill it in the refrigerator and serve.
110.note: Keep the curd mawa quite firm; if the mawa remains soft, it will turn into matho.

steps: First, grate the dudhi.
Now, let the milk boil in a vessel.
Until the milk boils, squeeze the grated dudhi between both hands to remove excess water.
Then, heat 3-4 spoons of ghee in a pan and sauté the dudhi in ghee for 5-7 minutes.
Next, add the dudhi, sugar, cashew-almond pieces, and cardamom powder to the milk.
Boil the dudhi kheer while stirring continuously until it becomes thick.
111.note: Sugar can be increased or decreased according to taste. If the dudhi has seeds, remove them while grating.

steps: Heat ghee in a pan, cut the boiled sweet potatoes into pieces, and sauté the pieces until they turn slightly red.
Then, add milk, milk cream, and sugar, and let it cook in a cooker on very low flame for up to 2 whistles.
After the pressure releases from the cooker, open it, run a blender, and add the cardamom nutmeg powder and pistachios.
112.note: Keep a larger cooker so that the milk does not spill out during the whistle. Saffron can be added if desired.

steps: In a bowl, add saffron to 3 spoons of lukewarm milk and keep it aside.
Heat milk in a vessel, and once it comes to a boil, add the dry fig pieces and boil for 15-20 minutes while stirring continuously.
Then, add sugar, saffron milk, cardamom powder, and cashew-almond powder, boil for 5-10 minutes, and turn off the gas.
Afterward, let it cool and keep it in the fridge for at least 1 hour before serving.
113.note: Cashew-almond powder is optional. The basundi should be thickened until half the milk reduces.

steps: Heat milk in a vessel, and while waiting for it to boil, chop the cashews, almonds, and pistachios on the side, make cardamom powder, and add them to the milk.
Add saffron and sugar to the milk and let it boil until the milk reduces to about 1/3.
Once the basundi is ready, let it cool, place it in the fridge for 1 hour, and serve.
114.note: Saffron is optional in this basundi.

steps: For making angoor:
Put 2 liters of milk to heat.
After the milk comes to a boil, add the lemon juice gradually, one spoon at a time, while stirring.

Once the paneer separates from the milk, turn off the gas, pour the paneer into a cotton cloth, and once the water drains, squeeze out the excess water by making a bundle and pressing with your hands.
Once the water drains out, wash the paneer by adding plain cold water.
Once the water drains from the paneer, knead it well in a vessel until smooth and make small grape-sized rasgullas.
Now, add 1 cup of sugar and about 2 cups of water in a pan and heat it until it comes to a boil.
Here, the sugar just needs to be dissolved; syrup (chasni) does not need to be made.
Now, add all the rasgullas into the syrup.
Once the rasgullas double in size, turn off the gas, take the rasgullas out into a bowl along with some syrup. For making basundi:
Now, to make basundi, put milk to heat in a vessel and boil it until it reduces to half.
Now, add the saffron soaked in a little milk beforehand and keep stirring.
After a while, add the cardamom powder.
The milk for this basundi is ready; let it cool down.
Now, take the rasgullas from the syrup into a bowl, pour the basundi over them, garnish with pistachio slivers, chill in the fridge, and serve.
Put milk to boil in a pan and boil it until it reduces to half.
Now add sugar, saffron, cardamom powder, and chopped almonds-pistachios, and let it boil for 8-10 minutes.
Then let it cool, and afterwards add the pineapple and place it in the refrigerator to chill.
116.note: The amount of sugar can be increased or decreased according to taste. Instead of adding pineapple pieces directly to the milk, you can add sugar to the pineapple pieces, cook for 2 whistles in a cooker, grind them in a mixer to make a paste, add this paste to a little milk, then strain it through a large sieve so that the pineapple flavor is enhanced, and mix this into the prepared rabdi.

steps: Put the milk to boil.
While stirring the milk, on the side, remove the seeds from the dates and coarsely crush them in a mixer.
Then add the dates and let it boil for 10-15 minutes.
Next, add the dry fruits and boil while stirring until the basundi thickens.
Once the basundi is ready, it can be served hot or cold.
117.note: Usually, dates are sweet so sugar is not needed, but sugar can be added while making if needed according to our taste.

steps: Total fat in 1 liter of milk should be 600 grams.
While boiling the milk, on the 2nd or 3rd boil, mix in the milk cream.
When it thickens to the right measure, add sugar, take it off the heat, and let it cool.
Then mix in all the fruits.
118.note: Custard powder is not used here, but it can also be made with its help.

steps: First, take 100 ml of milk in a bowl and mix the milk powder into it.
Then take all the milk in a kadhai and put it on the gas to heat.
After one boil, lower the flame and add the milk powder mixture.
Then add the saffron.
Keep the gas low while boiling the milk powder mixture.
Then add the almond and pistachio slivers.
Boil for 20-25 minutes and keep sticking the malai to one side on the edge of the kadhai.
Then add the cardamom and two-three drops of rose water.
Then add the sugar and stir very well.
Then, after the milk thickens, blend the malai that was stuck to the sides back into the milk.
Let it cool for 1-2 hours.
Lachha rabdi is ready.
First, take a wide-bottomed kadhai, pour milk into it, and put it on to heat.
Boil until the milk reduces to half.
Then extract the pulp of the custard apple, remove the seeds, and keep it ready.
Next, mix sugar into the milk.
Now add saffron and cardamom.
Then mix in the custard apple pulp and add the almond-pistachio slivers.
First, remove the inner core of the carrots and grate them.
Then take ghee in a kadhai and saute the grated carrots.
Next, take a pan, put it on heat, and add milk to it.
After one or two boils, keep the flame high and then lower it.
Apply the milk cream (malai) to the sides of the pan and keep stirring the milk.
After 10-15 minutes, add sugar as well.
Once the milk thickens, add the grated carrots and stir.
Then mix the malai applied on the sides and the cashew-almond-pistachio slices into the milk.
Add cardamom and let the rabdi cool down once it is ready.
For making angoor:
Put 2 liters of milk to heat.
After the milk comes to a single boil, add the lemon juice little by little, one spoonful at a time, while stirring.

Once the paneer separates from the milk, turn off the heat, put the paneer in a cotton cloth, and once the water drains out, squeeze out the excess water by making a bundle and pressing with your hands.
Once the water drains out, wash the paneer by adding plain cold water.

While the water drains from the paneer, take a kadhai on the side, add 1 cup of sugar and about 2 cups of water, and heat it until it comes to a boil. Here the sugar just needs to be dissolved, a syrup (chashni) is not to be made.
Once the paneer becomes dry, knead it well in a vessel until smooth and make small rasgullas out of it.
When the syrup comes to a boil, drop all the rasgullas into it.
Once the rasgullas double in size, turn off the heat and take the rasgullas out into a bowl along with some syrup. For making rabdi:
Now, to make rabdi, put milk to heat in a vessel and boil it until it reduces to half.
Now add the saffron pre-soaked in a little milk and keep stirring.
After a short while, add the cardamom powder.
The milk is ready for this rabdi; let it cool down.
Now take the rasgullas out of the syrup into a bowl, pour the rabdi over them, garnish with pistachio slices, chill in the fridge, and serve.
First, heat and saute the pineapple pulp in a pan and set it aside to cool.
Then put milk to heat in a kadhai.
Once it comes to one or two boils, add the saffron.
Now add cardamom powder and sugar to it and let the milk heat until it reduces to half.
Once the milk thickens, add the cooled pineapple, stir for five minutes, and remove from heat.
Add almond and pistachio slices to prepare the rabdi.
First, chop the mangoes into small pieces and set them aside to cool.
Then put milk to heat in a kadhai.
Once it comes to one or two boils, add the saffron.
Now add cardamom powder and sugar to it and let the milk heat until it reduces to half.
Once the milk thickens, add the cooled mango pieces, stir for five minutes, and remove from heat.
Add almond and pistachio slices to prepare the rabdi.
Boil the figs with required amount of water.
Then cool them, drain the water, add milk powder to the boiled figs, and mash them gently.
Put sugar and water in a pan to make a one-string sugar syrup.
Add cashew powder and saffron to the syrup and mix well.
Grease a plate with oil, spread this mixture on it, and let it cool down.
Then apply the fig paste over it and roll it up.
Apply silver foil on the roll, cut into 1-inch pieces, and serve.
125.note: Poppy seeds (khaskhas) can be applied on the roll.

steps: Mash the paneer with your hands until it becomes completely smooth.
Then make small and flat shaped balls from it and keep them ready on the side. Sugar syrup recipe :
Boil sugar and water in a pan for 10 minutes and then add the prepared paneer balls into this syrup.
Let it boil for 15 minutes and then take out these balls and press them to drain out the sugar water. Rabdi recipe :
Put the milk for rabdi to heat and heat it until it reduces to one-third and becomes thick.
Now add sugar, cardamom powder and saffron milk to it and boil it.
Boil it well and keep it in the fridge for 2-3 hours to cool down. Ras malai recipe :
First of all, put the paneer balls into the rabdi.
Prepare the rabdi by adding sliced almonds, pista and cashews to it.
126.note: Do not put hot rabdi in the fridge.

steps: Knead the prepared paneer well for 10 minutes.
Knead until the paneer becomes smooth and soft.
Now add powdered sugar and mix well.
Put the prepared paneer mixture in a pan to heat on low flame.
Let the water content evaporate for 5 minutes, then add cardamom powder and mix well.
