Let it cool for 5 minutes.
Next, once it cools down a bit, prepare small flat balls and make a depression in the middle, garnish with tutti fruitti, almonds or pista and serve the sandesh.
First of all, put the milk to boil in a pan and when it comes to 2-3 boils, add alum to it.
Adding alum will start curdling the milk and keep stirring it continuously.
Now put sugar to heat in another pan, make sure not to add water to it.
Now once the sugar melts properly, add it to the boiling milk, mix well and boil it thoroughly.
Now add liquid glucose to it and let it boil.
Now when it becomes very thick, take it out on a plate and serve it hot. Pendas can also be rolled from this.
Method to make basundi:
Take milk in a large vessel and put it to boil.
Keep stirring the milk continuously so that the milk does not stick.
When the milk becomes a little thick, add 130 grams of sugar to it.
Boil until the milk reduces to half.
Then let the prepared basundi cool down. Method to make pine cruise:
Properly mix pineapple ice cream, cream, powdered sugar and cashew pieces into the prepared basundi.
129.note: Take pineapple ice cream which contains pieces of pineapple.

steps: First of all, mash the paneer well.
Then give oblong shapes to the paneer and make chamcham. Sugar syrup recipe :
Boil sugar and water with cardamom in a pan for 10 minutes and then add the prepared paneer chamcham into this syrup.
Let it boil for 15 minutes and then take out these chamcham and press them to drain out the sugar water. To make stuffing :
Put ghee to heat in a pan and add milk, milk powder and cream to it, mix well and let it boil.
Now add saffron milk and powdered sugar to it, mix well and prepare like mawa (khoya).
Now make a cut in the middle of the chamcham, fill the prepared mawa (khoya) in it, put tutti fruitti on top, roll it in grated coconut and serve.
First wash the ripe mangoes and peel them.
Cut the mangoes into pieces.
Take mango pieces in a vessel, add sugar to it and crush it in a mixer.
Then add 1/3 cup of water or milk or 5-6 ice cubes to it and crush again for 1-2 minutes to make it uniform.
131.note: A teaspoon of ghee and a pinch of dry ginger powder can also be added. If the mangoes are sour, more sugar can also be added.

steps: First, chill the cashews by keeping them in the fridge and crush them nicely in a mixer ensuring no oil comes out.
Add water to the sugar, put it on heat for sugar syrup and make a one-and-a-half-thread consistency syrup.
Once the syrup is ready, add cashew powder to it and stir well to mix.
When everything is mixed very well, turn off the gas and take it down.
Divide the mixture into two parts, add food color to one part and keep the other part white.
Then roll out rotlas of both, place the colored rotla on the white rotla and roll it using butter paper.
After rolling properly, apply varakh on it and cut into small pieces.
132.note: Specifically grind the cashews only after chilling them in the fridge so that oil does not come out. If oil comes out from the cashews, the sweet will get spoiled. Kneading the cashew dough will make the sweet very soft.

steps: Method no – 1 :
First soak unspiced/plain pistachios in hot water and grind them.
On the other hand, make a one-and-a-half-thread consistency sugar syrup, add the ground pistachios to it and stir well to mix.
Then add food color, mace, cardamom to it and mix well.
Roll it into a rotla, apply poppy seeds on it and cut into pieces. Method no – 2 :
Chill pistachios in the fridge and crush them in a mixer.
Add 1 cup milk powder, powdered sugar, 2 spoons ghee, 4 spoons milk to it, knead and make a dough.
Knead a little more to make rolls.
Apply poppy seeds on top and cut into pieces.
133.note: According to method no - 2, the pistachio roll can be made nicely. But take special care to add milk little by little as needed and keep the dough stiff. If it feels too stiff, milk can be added to make it soft, and the dough should become very soft upon kneading, and the pistachios must be chilled before crushing.

steps: Crush chilled cashews and add to the one-and-a-half-thread sugar syrup, then mix to make something like mawa (khoya) and let it cool.
Now soak figs in hot water, cut them into small pieces and crush them.
Heat ghee in a pan and roast the crushed figs in it.
Once all the water evaporates and the mawa (khoya) becomes a bit firm, add milk powder to it, mix and then turn off the gas.
Now let the fig mawa (khoya) cool and make thin rolls out of it.
Now make a thin strip from the cashew mawa (khoya), place the fig roll made on top of it and roll the cashew strip around it.
Apply varakh on the cashew anjeer roll and cut it into small pieces.
134.note: Kneading the cashew dough with the help of plastic will prevent cracks in the cashew roll.

steps: First chill the cashews and crush them.
Take milk, sugar and cashew powder in a pan, put it on low heat to warm and keep stirring.
Now add color and milk powder to it and stir well until it does not stick to the pan.
Now let it cool and then knead it.
Now mix mixed dry fruits and mawa (khoya) into gulkand and mix well.
Now make a small puri from the cashew mawa (khoya), divide it into four parts and place the gulkand-infused mawa (khoya) in one of its parts.
Give it the shape of a paan, keeping it open at the top while shaping so that the gulkand-infused mawa (khoya) is visible.
Make all the remaining paans in this way.
First, crush the cold cashews and grind them into a fine powder.
In a kadhai, put milk to heat, add sugar, and let the sugar dissolve.
Now add the cashew powder, milk powder, and ghee to that milk and keep stirring well.
When it becomes like a firm mawa (khoya), turn off the gas, take it on a good plastic sheet, and knead it.
Then spread it evenly in a square board or dish and cut it using a cutter.
136.note: Keep the cashew mixture firm, it can be made soft later by kneading. But if it is loose, the kaju katli will also turn out loose.

steps: First, soak the almonds for half an hour.
Then boil them in hot water for 10 minutes.
Cool the almonds and peel off their skins.
Now grind them smoothly in a mixer by adding a little water.
Take the almond paste in a pan, add sugar to it, and heat for 10 minutes.
When the mawa (khoya) is well mixed, check if it does not stick to your hands, then it is ready.
Now let it cool, take it in a good plastic sheet, and knead it well.
Spread it evenly on a square board to form a uniform layer and cut it into equal pieces using a cutter.
First, crush the cashews cold.
Then mix sugar and water in a bowl to make a 3-string sugar syrup and add the cashew powder to it.
Meanwhile, put ghee to heat on another burner.
Now slowly add this ghee into the cashew mixture while stirring.
This way the mesub will puff up, and once it is fully puffed, quickly transfer it to a tray.
After it cools down, make cuts in it and invert the tray to separate the pieces.
138.note: Spread the cashew-pistachio crush at the bottom of the tray. Then pour the mesub so that it sticks well. Keep the ghee hot on medium flame. Stirring the mesub continuously will create a good lattice texture in the mesub.

steps: Put ghee to heat in a kadhai. Make the ghee quite hot.
Take sugar in a kadhai, add just enough water to submerge the sugar, and put it on to make a one-string sugar syrup.
Now mix the maida (all-purpose flour) and almond powder, add ghee to it, and prepare a paste-like mixture.
Once the syrup is ready, add the almond and maida (all-purpose flour) paste into it and keep stirring continuously.
Now slowly keep adding the hot ghee into the mixture while stirring.
As the ghee is poured, the mesub will puff up, and once it puffs up properly and starts releasing ghee, quickly transfer it into a tray.
Sprinkle cardamom seeds on top, and once it cools down, make cuts and invert the tray to separate the pieces.
Take sugar in a kadhai, add just enough water to submerge the sugar, and put it on the stove to heat for making sugar syrup.
When a one-string syrup is formed, add the peanut powder to it and keep stirring continuously.
On the other side, heat the ghee.
Keep the stove with the syrup on low heat and keep stirring.
When it is roasted a bit, add about a spoonful of ghee from the heated ghee and keep stirring continuously.
Once the added ghee is absorbed, pour another spoonful of ghee.
Slowly pour all the ghee in this manner.
After adding the ghee, a nice porous texture (jali) will form, and when the ghee separates, understand that the mesub is now ready.
Then transfer it onto a plate.
Do not stir or tap it, as doing so will cause the formed porous texture to collapse.
Sprinkle cardamom seeds on top, and once it cools down, make cuts and let it set for 5-6 hours.
140.note: Always add hot ghee; if the ghee is cold, the porous texture will not form properly.

steps: Heat about 150 grams of ghee in a pan, once hot, add the rajgira flour and roast it.
Roast until the ghee separates, then take it off the heat.
In another pan, roast the cashews and almonds for 2 minutes.
Take the cashews and almonds out, put the remaining ghee in that same pan and heat it.
Add the jaggery to it and stir, heat it until bubbles form in the jaggery to prepare the jaggery-ghee syrup base.
Then add the roasted flour to it and stir to mix.
Once mixed well, add the cashews and almonds; you can also add them chopped or sliced.
Spread it evenly on a plate and cut into pieces.
141.note: Cut into pieces while it is still warm, otherwise they will not cut properly after cooling down.

ing: Walnuts - 50 grams (to be roasted in ghee)
steps: Heat ghee in a pan and sauté the dry fruits.
Take a heavy-bottomed pan, add milk to it and heat it.
Keep stirring the milk continuously, taking care that it does not stick to the bottom.
Now add sugar to it.
Keep stirring until its mawa (khoya) is ready.
Once the mawa (khoya) is ready, add cashews, almonds, and walnuts to it.
Then pour it onto a greased flat tray, and cut into diamond shapes once it cools down.
First of all, roast the peanuts in a pan.
Once the peanuts are roasted and have cooled down, remove their skins.
After removing the skins, crush the peanuts in a mixer.
Take sugar in a pan, add just enough water to submerge the sugar, and put it on heat to make sugar syrup.
Keep stirring, take a drop of the syrup and test it; allow the syrup to reach a consistency where the drop does not move from where you place it.
As soon as the syrup is ready, immediately add the crushed peanuts and grated dry coconut to it, and then turn off the gas.
Mix well and add two teaspoons of ghee to it.
Spread it immediately on a flat tray and cut into diamond shapes.
143.note: The shing pak will turn out good only if the syrup is made correctly, otherwise it will remain loose or become too hard. If the syrup becomes too hard, adding two teaspoons of milk will bring it back to consistency. After the syrup is ready and the peanut powder is added to the shing pak, mawa and cardamom can also be added.

steps: First of all, roast the mawa with ghee in a pan.
Then in another pan, chop the dates into pieces, add ghee and roast them.
Once the dates are roasted, add milk and keep stirring.
Stir until all the milk evaporates; adding milk helps the dates melt quickly.
Then mash it with a masher to make it smooth and uniform.
Next, add the mawa to the dates and mix everything well.
Then add the grated dry coconut, cashews, almonds, and pistachios and stir everything well.
Spread it out on a plate, and cut into diamond shapes after it cools down.
144.note: If you do not want to cut diamond shapes, you can also roll them into small round ladees. Roast the dates on low heat otherwise they will stick.

ing: Unsalted pistachios - 50 grams (cut into small pieces)
steps: Soak the figs and dates for three to four hours.
Then take them out of the water and grind both finely in a mixer separately.
Afterwards, heat ghee in a pan and sauté the fig-date paste.
Once the mawa (khoya) becomes thick, add the cashew, almond, and pistachio pieces to it.
Then grease a plate with ghee, pour the mixture onto it, and cut into diamond shapes after it cools down.
145.note: Soak the figs and dates for three to four hours. Then take them out of the water and grind both finely in a mixer separately. Afterwards, heat ghee in a pan and sauté the fig-date paste. Once the mawa becomes thick, add the cashew, almond, and pistachio pieces to it. Then grease a plate with ghee, pour the mixture onto it, and cut into diamond shapes after it cools down.

steps: Peel and grate the bottle gourd, then squeeze out a little water from it.
Heat a little ghee in a pan and sauté the grated bottle gourd.
On the other side, boil the milk nicely.
Once the bottle gourd is sautéed, add the milk to it and keep stirring.
After a while, when the milk evaporates, add sugar to it.
Keep stirring until the milk and sugar water evaporates and it becomes thick.
Once it becomes like mawa (khoya), add a little ghee, take it off the heat, and add color as needed.
Then add cardamom powder, transfer it to a bowl, and garnish with dry fruits of your choice from the top.
146.note: Do not leave the grated bottle gourd unattended, if left it will turn black.

steps: First peel and grate the carrots.
Take 1 spoon of ghee in a pan, then add the grated carrots and sauté.
Then add milk to it and keep stirring.
When the milk reduces, add sugar.
Let it cook for a while, when the sugar water reduces, add mawa (khoya) and keep stirring.
Once the mawa (khoya) is mixed well, add cashews and raisins and mix.
Add 1 spoon of ghee, once the ghee separates, take it off the gas and add cardamom and poppy seeds.
Peel the sapodilla and cut them into small pieces.
Heat 1 spoon of ghee in a pan and sauté the pieces, let them cook for a while.
Then add milk to it, once the milk boils, add sugar and keep stirring.
When it thickens, add 1 spoon of ghee, mix well and take it off the heat.
Add cardamom powder and take it out on a plate.
First peel the beetroot and boil them semi-soft, then grate the boiled beetroots.
Take ghee in a pan, add the grated beetroot and keep stirring for two to three minutes.
Then add milk to it and keep stirring.
When the milk evaporates, add sugar and keep stirring.
After the sugar water evaporates, add roasted mawa (khoya) and keep stirring the whole mixture.
When everything thickens, take it off the gas and let it cool down.
Add cardamom powder from the top to the cooled mixture and serve.
149.note: If you want to add mawa, roast and add it once the sugar water evaporates. If mawa is added, milk will not be needed.

ing: cardamom powder, saffron, raisins, sliced cashew-almonds
steps: Remove the coconut shell and grate it using a mixer or grater.
Heat ghee in a pan and sauté the grated coconut.
When it turns pink, roast the mawa and add it to it.
Make a 2-string sugar syrup. Add the grated coconut to it.
Keep it on the gas for a while and stir.
When it thickens, add a little ghee and take it off.
Garnish with the spices given in the ingredients from the top,
Saffron can also be added to the syrup.
First of all, grate the apples along with their skin.
Then heat ghee in a kadhai.
Then add the grated apple to it and let it cook on low heat.
Then add saffron, sugar, sliced almonds-pistachios, and cardamom powder to it.
Then mix everything well and add mawa (khoya) to it, stirring continuously on low heat.
Now, once the water evaporates and everything is well combined, garnish the top with sliced almonds-pistachios.
151.note: Milk can also be used instead of mawa.

steps: First, coarsely grind the walnuts in a mixer.
Heat ghee in a kadhai and add the walnuts to it, stirring well.
Now add mawa (khoya) to it and roast.
Once uniform, add milk powder and milk, and keep stirring continuously.
Then add sugar and stir.
Next, add cardamom powder and sliced almonds, and stir.
Once it thickens, remove it from the gas.

ing: White or black sesame seeds – 125 grams (1 cup)
dry ginger powder powder – 1 tea spoon
ghee or sesame oil – 2-3 tea spoons
steps: Grind the sesame seeds well in a mixer grinder (grind at the highest speed for 3-5 seconds).
Add soft jaggery and deseeded dates to it and grind this mixture again.
Remove this mixture into a large bowl.
Add almonds, cashews, melon seeds, poppy seeds, dry ginger powder powder, and ganthoda powder to it.
Add about 1 spoon of ghee to it and mix the whole mixture well.
Sprinkle cashew, almond pieces, and tutti-frutti on top for garnish.
153.note: Sesame oil can also be used instead of ghee in the sesame mixture. Black or white sesame seeds can both be used, and sesame oil can be used instead of ghee. Fried gum (gond) and grated dry coconut can be added to this.

steps: First of all, soak the sabudana in water for 2 to 3 hours.
Heat milk in a kadhai on medium heat.
Take a little milk in a separate small bowl and soak the saffron in it.
Now add the sabudana to the milk and let it cook on low heat.
Let it cook until the sabudana becomes transparent like glass.
Then add sugar and let it boil.
After 5 to 7 boils, turn off the gas.
Now mix in all the dry fruits, cardamom powder, and the saffron mixture.
Sabudana kheer is ready.
It can be served piping hot as well as chilled from the fridge.
Soak the moraiya in water for approximately half an hour.
Then drain the water from it.
Heat milk in a kadhai on medium heat.
Add the moraiya to it and mix well with the milk.
Let it cook on the gas for about 20 minutes.
Then add sugar and keep stirring continuously until the sugar dissolves.
Let it cook until it becomes thick and creamy.
Add cardamom powder and saffron to it, and garnish with raisins and cashews.
155.note: Cardamom powder and saffron are optional.

steps: Heat the khiru on a low flame.
Stir this milk very well.
Keep stirring until it turns brown in color.
Add sugar to this milk mawa and keep stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Then spread it out on a plate and let it cool.
After it cools down, shape them into penda.
Method – 1
Heat the bali milk on a low flame, add sugar to it, and heat both together.
Keep stirring continuously until the milk becomes like mawa (khoya) ( curdles ). (Keep the color white only).
Once this mixture becomes like mawa (khoya), spread it on a plate and cut it into pieces.
Method – 2
Put water to heat in a large pot and place a steel stand or round sieve in the middle.
Now, add roughly 600 grams of powdered sugar and 50 grams of normal milk to 1 liter of bali milk.
Mix this well until the sugar dissolves completely.
Now pour it into a plate.
Then place the plate on the stand inside the pot and cover the pot with a lid from above.
It will set in 8 to 10 minutes, then remove the lid and check the milk in the plate.
If it has set, turn off the gas, leave the plate aside for a while, and then cut into pieces.
Give moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) of 150 grams of milk and 150 grams of ghee to the flour.
Mix well and sift it through a sieve.
Then heat the remaining ghee in a kadai and roast the moga flour on a slow flame.
Once the flour is roasted and turns light brown, turn off the gas.
Then after it cools down, add sugar and cardamom and shape into laddu.
Put ghee to heat in a kadai and roast cashews, almonds, and walnuts in it until they turn brown.
Now grind these roasted dry fruits.
Now take jaggery in a kadai, add 2 spoons of ghee to it, and prepare the jaggery syrup (payo).
Add that syrup, cardamom powder, and ghee to the dry fruit powder and shape them into laddu. To make the syrup:
Finely chop the jaggery.
Add 2 spoons of ghee to it and heat it on the gas.
Once the jaggery melts and starts bubbling, the syrup is ready. To check the syrup:
Take water in a small bowl and drop 3-4 drops of the syrup into it.
If it does not dissolve and stays as it is, then it is correct.
First of all, fry the almond pieces.
Add ghee to the moraiya flour and roast it until it turns pink.
Roast the mawa also until it turns light pink and let everything cool down.
Then add mawa (khoya), flour, powdered sugar, coconut, almonds, and cardamom to it and mix well.
Now shape into laddu and decorate by placing halved pista on top.
161.note: If you want to make it without mawa, milk can be used.

steps: First, pop the amaranth seeds.
To pop the seeds, take a thick-bottomed pan and heat it well.
Once hot, add a little amaranth at a time and continuously press it gently with a cloth.
Now, after the seeds pop, sift them using a thick sieve to separate the puffed seeds.
Now add the amaranth puffed seeds to the jaggery syrup and mix well.
Make ladoos of your desired size while it is still warm.
Wet your hands with water so the ladoos do not stick to your hands. To make the syrup:
Finely chop the jaggery.
Add ghee to it and heat it on the gas.
Once the jaggery melts and starts bubbling, the syrup is ready. To check the syrup:
Take water in a small bowl and drop 3-4 drops of the syrup into it.
If it does not dissolve and stays as it is, it is correct.
162.note: Dry fruits are optional. It is necessary to wet your hands with water while making each ladoo.

steps: Sauté the grated beetroot in ghee.
Then add sugar, milk malai, and milk, and mix.
Once ghee separates, add grated coconut and stir.
After it cools down, shape into small ladoos and coat with grated coconut.
Decorate by placing dry fruits on top.
163.note: Condensed milk can also be used instead of milk and dry fruits.

steps: First, sauté cashews, almonds, and dates in ghee on a low flame and take them out in a separate bowl.
Again in ghee, add walnuts, pistachios, sesame seeds, poppy seeds, and raisins, sauté, and take them out in a separate bowl.
Now roast the coconut until it turns light pink.
Now add 1 cup of water to 1 cup of sugar and boil until the sugar dissolves.
Now add cardamom powder and the roasted dry fruits to it.
Keep it on the gas and stir until the dry fruits absorb all the sugar syrup.
Once cooled, shape into ladoos.
First, roast the sesame seeds on medium flame for 5-6 minutes.
Add ghee to the jaggery along with 3-4 spoons of water to prepare the syrup.
Now add coarsely crushed peanuts and sesame seeds to it and mix well.
Shape the ladoos before the mixture cools down. To make the syrup:
Finely chop the jaggery.
Add ghee to it and heat it on the gas.
Once the jaggery melts and starts bubbling, the syrup is ready. To check the syrup:
Take water in a small bowl and drop 3-4 drops of the syrup into it.
If it does not dissolve and stays as it is, it is correct.
165.note: It is necessary to wet hands with water before making each ladoo. Peanuts are optional. Grated coconut can also be added.

steps: Heat ghee in a vessel. Once the ghee is hot, add grated dry coconut.
Stir it for a minute keeping the gas on low.
Take special care that it does not stick to the bottom.
Then add milk, sugar, and milk powder to it.
After that, keep stirring continuously on a low flame until it stops sticking to the vessel.
Then take it out on a plate.
Shape into ladoos after it cools down slightly.
166.note: Milk mawa can also be added instead of milk powder.

steps: First, wash the whole moriya 2 to 3 times.
Then soak it for 15 to 20 minutes and drain the water using a strainer.
Next, take ghee in a vessel, add almond pieces, lightly roast them, and remove them.
Then add the soaked moriya and roast it. Roast until the color of the moriya changes.
Once the color of the moriya changes, add the heated water.
After that, add sugar, stir until the water evaporates, and then turn off the gas.
Method – 2
First, put ghee in a bowl, let it warm slightly, and then add the moriya flour.
Add the flour and stir on low heat. Stir until the color of the flour changes.
After the flour is roasted, add hot water to it. Stir until the water evaporates, then turn off the gas.
Take it off the gas and add almond flakes and cardamom powder to it.
First, put ghee in a bowl. Once the ghee is hot, add the singoda flour and roast it.
Roast until the color changes.
Then add hot water, mix well so the water blends into the flour, and stir it.
Now, once the flour absorbs the water, add jaggery and stir.
If needed, add 2 spoons of ghee from the top and then turn off the gas.
Then take it down, transfer it to a vessel, and add cashews and almonds.
168.note: Instead of water, 1/2 liter of milk can also be added.

steps: First, heat ghee and add the rajgira flour to it.
Then stir on low heat until the rajgira flour is roasted.
Now mix the sugar and stir for 2-3 minutes.
Then mix in raisins, almonds, and cardamom powder and stir. Then turn off the gas.
169.note: Cut the almonds into small pieces. Jaggery can also be used instead of sugar. However, for that, first dissolve the jaggery in hot water before using.

steps: After boiling the ratalu, peel it and mash it.
Then take the mashed ratalu in a vessel, add milk to it, and put it on the gas to heat.
Boil the milk thoroughly.
Once the milk is hot and evaporates, add sugar and stir.
Then add grated dry coconut and cardamom seeds or cardamom powder, and take it off the heat.
Ratalu sheera is ready.
170.note: Dry fruits can be added to the sheera if needed. Dry fruits can be added to the sheera if needed.

steps: First, peel the potatoes and grate them using a grater.
Then heat ghee in a kadhai.
Once the ghee is hot, add the grated potatoes to it.
Keep stirring on medium heat for 10 minutes.
Stir until it turns slightly brown, then add milk and sugar.
After that, mix in the dry fruits. Cook until it thickens.
Then add ghee and cardamom powder from the top. Stir well and garnish.
First, peel the sweet potatoes and cut them into pieces.
Then mix them with sugar and milk in a mixer.
Then grind it into a uniform mixture.
After that, heat ghee in a pan, add the mixture to it and roast for 10 minutes.
Then decorate it with cashew, almond, pistachio.
172.note: Sugar can be increased or decreased according to taste.

steps: First of all, put the moraiyo in a mixer and grind it coarsely or like rava.
Then add sour curd, grated bottle gourd and carrot to it, add water if needed.
After that, make a ginger-chili paste and add it to mix well.
Whisk with hand for 5 minutes.
Then cover and keep it for 15 minutes.
Then put the steamer on the gas and keep the plate in which the batter is to be spread ready by applying oil.
After 15 minutes, add salt, turmeric and baking soda to the batter and stir well.
Spread it in the plate and put it to steam. After 5-6 minutes, check by inserting a knife, if it does not stick to the knife, understand that it is cooked, then cut pieces.
Now we will prepare the tempering.
Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds, sesame seeds and neem leaves to prepare the tempering.
Then pour it over the prepared khaman-dhokla.
Sprinkle coriander on top for garnish, so the khaman-dhokla are ready.
174.note: If you want to make these dhoklas sweet, you can make and add sugar water.

steps: First of all take ghee and powdered sugar in a bowl.
Then mix it completely.
Then add cardamom powder and coarse moraiyo flour to it and mix it.
Then make round dough balls and stick almond halves directly on top of them to prepare.
Preheat the oven at 160 degrees for 10 minutes.
Then keep it on convection mode at 160 degrees for 20 minutes.
Check after 20 minutes.
Let it cool for a while. The nankhatai is ready.
First, wash the potatoes, peel them, and cut them into medium-sized pieces.
Then place a cooker on the gas and put oil in it to heat.
Sauté cumin seeds in the oil, then add peanuts, and after they crackle, add whole dried red chillies and curry leaves.
Next, add the potato pieces and the washed moraiya.
Add turmeric and chilli powder, then mix well.
Add four times the amount of water compared to the moraiya and salt to taste.
Close the cooker lid, whistle 3 times, and let the pressure build up.
After that, open the cooker, add coriander for garnish, and the khichdi is ready.
176.note: You can finely chop and add other vegetables of your choice, such as carrots, cabbage, tomatoes, etc. Also, curd can be added while making the tempering.

steps: First of all, mix ghee and sugar in a bowl and whisk for 4-5 minutes.
Then add cardamom powder and milk to both flours and knead.
Lastly, add baking soda, baking powder and dry fruit powder and knead.
Then make small dough balls of any desired shape from the kneaded dough.
Now you can make horizontal and vertical lines on it with a fork. (If there is no oven)
Then put salt in a kadhai, cover with a plate and set to heat. (10 minutes)
Now grease a plate with ghee on top of that kadhai, place the dough balls on it and let them cook for 30 minutes.
If you are making it in an oven, bake it for 15 minutes.
Method to soak sabudana:
Take sabudana in a bowl, wash it, then add 1 ½ times as much water as the sabudana and let it soak for 3-4 hours.
First strain the sabudana in a colander.
Then heat oil or ghee in a kadhai, add cumin seeds, ginger-chilli paste, turmeric and chopped potatoes and stir.
After the potatoes are cooked, add sabudana, add salt and sugar to taste, then add a little water and let it cook for 8-10 minutes.
Then add crushed peanuts, add lemon juice to it and add chopped fresh coriander leaves and serve.
First roast the sesame seeds. After the sesame seeds are roasted, crush them.
Now put ghee and jaggery in a bowl. Then add 3 spoons of water to it.
Stir until it starts bubbling, then add the crushed sesame seeds to it.
Stir for 5-7 minutes then turn off the gas.
Then take it out on a plate and cut square pieces.
179.note: Do not overheat the jaggery otherwise it will become hard. Grated dry coconut can also be added here for taste.

steps: First roast coriander, fennel seeds and dill seeds separately on low flame just for a short while until aromatic and moisture evaporates.
Once cooled, crush them together in a mixer and sift through a flour sifter mesh.
Crush and sift the sugar in the same way.
Melt the ghee and after it cools down completely, add it slowly and mix everything.
Now add grated dry coconut to it and mix well.
Panjiri is ready.
First grind moraiyo and sabudana in a mixer.
Then add this ground mixture to a large bowl, add curd and salt to it and mix well.
Then add water as needed to prepare a dosa batter from it.
Keep it medium, neither too thick nor too thin.
Then after heating the dosa griddle on a low flame, spread a bowl of batter on it and apply ghee so that it becomes crispy.
183.note: Can also be made by adding 1 cup of water chestnut (singoda) flour.

steps: First of all, boil dudhi and potatoes in a cooker by adding one glass of water.
Then crush them in a mixer and take them out in a bowl.
After that, heat oil in a pan and temper it with sesame seeds, curry leaves, and cumin seeds.
Now add cloves and black pepper, and then add chopped tomatoes.
Stir until the tomato pieces become soft.
Then add the crushed dudhi and potato mixture to it.
Now add chopped green chillies, sugar, and salt to taste, and add 2 glasses of water to it.
Then boil it for 10 minutes.
Now add fresh coriander leaves and mix well.
First, take the sabudana in a vessel, wash it well 2 or 3 times and soak it.
After soaking the sabudana for 3-4 hours, strain it in a strainer or colander to dry it.
Now prepare grated boiled potatoes in a vessel.
Then grind the peanuts in a mixer.
Next, add the soaked sabudana and peanut powder to the grated boiled potatoes and mix slightly.
Then add the ground green chili, grated ginger, sesame seeds, sugar, lemon juice, and salt to taste into this mixture and mix well.
Then put oil to heat in a pan.
Then you can give the prepared mixture your favorite shape.
Then lower the flame and slowly fry the sabudana vadas in it. When they turn light red, take them out onto a plate.
Cut the bananas into round pieces in a bowl.
Then add ghee, powdered sugar, and cardamom to it, mix well, and serve.
189.note: The bananas should not be raw; ripe bananas are necessary. Cashews and raisins can be added according to preference.

steps: Take one spoonful of rajgira at a time in a pan on low heat and pop it by pressing gently with a clean cloth or handkerchief. Once all the rajgira is popped this way, sift it so that the popped grains and unpopped rajgira separate.
In another pan, take sugar and water and make a 1-string syrup.
Now mix the popped rajgira into it.
Grease a plate with ghee, spread the mixture, and make cuts.
Once cooled, break into pieces and serve.
190.note: Jaggery can also be used instead of sugar.

steps: First, cut all the cashews into 2 halves from the middle.
Heat 1 spoon of ghee in a pan and add sugar to it, heating it.
Once it melts completely, add 1 spoon of ghee to it.
Then add the cashews and mix well.
Spread this mixture on butter paper and make cuts on it.
And after it cools down, separate the pieces.
191.note: Chikki can also be made by using jaggery instead of sugar. This chikki stays good for up to 15 days.

steps: Cut the coconut into long, thin slices.
Put the coconut slices in a pan and roast for 5–7 minutes.
Take sugar in a pan and heat it until it melts.
Now take water in a bowl and drop 2–3 drops of the syrup into it.
If the syrup does not dissolve in water and becomes hard, the syrup is ready.
And if it sticks to the water, heat it again.
Once the syrup is ready, mix the coconut slices into it.
Grease a plate with ghee, spread this mixture, and make cuts. Once cooled, make pieces.
Take almonds in a pan and roast them. Roast for 5–7 minutes, take them down, and crush them.
Take jaggery in a pan and make its syrup.
To check the syrup, take cold water in a bowl and drop 2–3 drops of syrup into it.
If the syrup remains soft when dropped in water, heat it more.
After a while, drop 2–3 drops of syrup again, and if the syrup becomes hard in the water, the syrup is ready.
Once the syrup is properly ready, mix the crushed almonds into it.
Grease a plate with ghee, spread the mixture well, and make cuts.
After it cools down, serve this chikki.
193.note: Almonds can also be kept whole. Almonds can also be cut in half from the middle. Just like jaggery, it can also be made with sugar.

steps: To knead the dough:
First, in a bowl, add maida (all-purpose flour), ghee, salt, and ajwain (carom seeds), mix well, knead a stiff dough (stiffer than roti) using water, and let it rest for 15 minutes. For preparation:
Wash the moong dal and soak it for 2 hours. After 2 hours, drain all the water and coarsely crush it in a mixer (do not crush it too much). For the stuffing:
Take oil in a pan, and once the oil is hot, add fennel seeds, cumin seeds, whole coriander seeds (coarsely crushed), crushed dal, and besan, and sauté them.
Once the besan is roasted, add black salt, salt, chilli powder, turmeric, coriander-cumin powder, and garam masala, and sauté for 1-2 minutes.
Then add powdered sugar, stir for 2 minutes, and turn off the gas.
Once the stuffing cools down, roll it into 12 equal balls.
To make the kachori, knead the maida dough well and make 12 portions (dough balls).
Take one portion, roll it into a small puri, and place a ball of stuffing in the center.
Now, gather the maida puri from all sides and seal it inwards completely.
Press it gently with your hand to give it a puri-like shape.
Make all the kachoris in this way. For frying:
Heat oil in a pan. When the oil is lukewarm, drop the kachoris into it.
Putting the kachoris in lukewarm oil, fry them on a low flame until they turn golden brown.
199.note: Instead of soaking, moong dal can also be used by boiling it in hot water. Spices in the stuffing can be increased or decreased according to taste. Oil can be used instead of ghee for kneading the dough. If the oil becomes too hot, turn off the gas, let it cool, and then fry the remaining kachoris. If a kachori breaks while frying, make a slurry by adding water to maida and apply it to the broken part so the stuffing does not spill out into the oil. These kachoris stay good for 10-12 days in an airtight container.

steps: Take flour in a bowl, add 2 teaspoons of oil and salt, and mix well.
Now add water to knead a soft dough and cover it with a cloth and set aside. To make the stuffing:
First, crush the sev with your hands and grind the almonds and cashews.
Now heat 1 teaspoon of oil in a pan, add cumin seeds and let them fry.
Once the cumin seeds are roasted, add poppy seeds and sesame seeds and roast slightly.
Now add coriander powder, fennel seeds powder, cardamom, turmeric, cashews, almonds, and sev.
Then add garam masala, salt, amchur (dry mango powder), and red chilli powder, mix well, and let all the spices roast for 2-3 minutes.
Now add raisins and sweet chutney to the spices, mix well, and fry again for 1 minute.
Once ready, turn off the heat, take the stuffing out into a bowl, and let it cool.
Then make equal-sized balls from the kneaded dough and the mawa stuffing.
Now take a dough ball, roll it into a slightly thick puri, fill it with the prepared dry mawa (khoya), and seal the puri from all sides.
Roll it round between both palms to give it a nice spherical kachori shape.
Now fry these kachoris on low heat until they turn golden brown.
200.note: Knead a very soft dough for the kachoris.

ing: fresh fresh coriander leaves chopped – 2-3 teaspoons
steps: Take flour in a bowl, add 4 teaspoons of ghee and salt, and mix this mixture well.
Now add water to knead a soft dough, cover it with a cloth, and set it aside.
Grate the paneer in a bowl.
Now heat the remaining ghee in a non-stick pan.
Add cumin seeds, coriander powder, garam masala powder, red chilli powder, chaat masala, fresh coriander leaves, and salt, and saute for 30 seconds.
Then add the grated paneer and mix well.
Take this mixture out into a bowl and let it cool.
Now heat enough oil in a kadhai.
Then divide the kneaded dough and paneer mawa into equal parts.
Now take a portion of the dough, roll it like a slightly thick puri, fill it with paneer mawa (khoya), and seal the puri from all sides.
Press it gently with your hands to give it a thick puri shape, and roll all the remaining kachoris similarly.
Now fry these kachoris on low heat until they turn golden brown and serve piping hot.

ing: Oil (for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour)) – 1/4 cup
steps: First, combine the maida (all-purpose flour) with baking soda, salt, and oil, knead into a soft dough like roti, and let it rest for 20-25 minutes. For the stuffing:
First, coarsely grind the raw green peas with ginger and chillies in a mixer.
Heat oil in a kadhai, add cumin seeds, ajwain (carom seeds), and fennel seeds.
Add two spoons of gram flour and sauté for 1 minute.
Add turmeric powder and the pea paste, and let it cook.
After 2 minutes, add red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, amchur (dry mango powder), chaat masala, salt, garam masala, and fresh coriander leaves, and mix well.
The stuffing is ready. For the kachori:
Divide the dough into equal-sized portions.
Make equal-sized balls from the stuffing as well.
Take dough portions that are double the size of the stuffing balls.
Roll them out like a puri or press by hand, place the stuffing ball in the center, seal from the top, and shape into a round ball.
Then gently press with your hand and flatten it to the size of a puri again.
Drop the kachori into lukewarm oil and fry such that they rise to the top on their own.
Fry on both sides until they become very crispy, puffed, and golden.

ing: fresh coriander leaves (fresh coriander leaves) – 1/2 cup
steps: For the dough:
Add salt, oil, and ajwain (carom seeds) to maida (all-purpose flour), knead into a firm dough like puri, and let it rest for 20-25 minutes. For the stuffing:
First, take the pigeon pea seeds, ginger, and chillies, and coarsely grind them in a mixer.
Heat oil in a kadhai, add cumin seeds, sesame seeds, and then the pigeon pea seeds.
Let it cook for 3-4 minutes.
Then add salt, garam masala, sugar, cashew nut pieces, and fresh coriander leaves, and sauté for a short while.
Mix well, turn off the heat, and add the lemon juice. For the kachori:
Now roll out a thin puri, place 1 spoon of the stuffing ball in the center, and gather the edges like a potli.
Heat oil for frying.
Once the oil is moderately hot, fry on low to medium heat while stirring continuously.
203.note: Double frying can also be done. Add lemon juice only after turning off the heat. Stuffing spices can be adjusted according to personal taste. Adding 3-4 medium potatoes prevents the stuffing from falling apart.

ing: Kashmiri red chilli powder - 1 tea spoon
amchur (dry mango powder) powder - 1 tea spoon
steps: First, in a large bowl, add maida (all-purpose flour), semolina (rava), baking soda, and salt, and mix well.
Now add hot oil to it and mix it into the flour.
Now add water as needed and knead the dough for 5 minutes.
Add just enough water so the dough is moderately soft.
Now cover it and keep it aside for 15 minutes.
Then knead it a little again and make small balls out of it.
Roll each ball slightly larger than a puri size.
Now heat oil in a kadhai and fry the puris in such a way that each puri puffs up like a ball.
And fry on both sides.
Keep the puris on a paper napkin so that excess oil does not remain in the puris.
Now let them cool down.
Now whenever you want to serve the raj kachori, take a puri and break it open from the top.
Put 1 spoonful of potatoes, 1 spoonful of white chickpeas, and 2 spoonfuls of moong beans in it.
Now add 2 spoonfuls of curd into it.
Then add 1 spoonful of green chutney and sweet chutney.
Now add chilli powder, amchur (dry mango powder), and all other spices as needed.
Again add 1/2 spoonful of curd and both chutneys.
Now garnish with 2 spoonfuls of sev, 1 spoonful of boondi, 1 spoonful of pomegranate, and 1 spoonful of coriander.
So your raj kachori is ready this way.
Prepare all the puris this way and serve.
204.note: Use the puris only after they have cooled completely.

steps: Take flour in a bowl, add 4 spoons of ghee and salt to it, and mix this mixture well.
Now add water to it to knead a firm dough and cover it with a cloth and keep it aside.
Put potatoes to boil in a pressure cooker and after peeling the boiled potatoes, cut them into small pieces.
Now heat oil in a kadhai.
Add cumin seeds to the oil. Once the cumin seeds crackle, add coriander powder, green chillies, ginger, salt, and potatoes to it.
Fry for 2-3 minutes.
Once the potatoes form a smooth mawa (khoya) like consistency, make equal-sized balls out of it.
Now make equal-sized dough portions from the prepared dough.
Take one dough portion and roll it out like a slightly thick puri.
Fill the potato mawa (khoya) in it and seal the puri by gathering it from all sides.
Roll it out again into a slightly thick kachori. Roll out all the remaining kachoris similarly.
Now fry these kachoris on low heat until they turn golden brown and serve hot.
Crush 5-6 pcs of toast and add it to the boiled potatoes.
Then add salt, green chillies, ginger, sesame seeds, powdered sugar, fresh coriander leaves, coriander-cumin powder, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and lemon juice, and mix the mixture well.
Then make cutlets from the mixture in heart shape or round shape.
Crush the remaining 5-6 toast.
Coat the prepared cutlets in it and fry them in oil until they turn brown.

ing: Oil – for frying and for stuffing
steps: To knead the dough:
Add ajwain (carom seeds) and salt to maida (all-purpose flour), mix well, add 4 spoons of oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour), and knead a medium-firm dough with water.
Cover it and keep it aside to set for 20-25 minutes. For the stuffing:
Heat oil in a pan, once the oil is hot, add ginger-chillies and fry a little, then add green peas and fry for a while, add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and cashews, and stir for 1 minute.
Then add potatoes, garam masala, roasted cumin powder, and salt, stir for 2-3 minutes, and turn off the gas.
Then mix coriander into it.
After the spice mixture cools down, add chaat masala and amchur (dry mango powder) powder to it and mix well. For the samosa:

Make small dough balls, roll them into a slightly thick roti, cut it into two parts, fold one part and fold from the other side to make a samosa shape, fill the stuffing inside, apply water on top, and stick the two opposite layers together to fold it.
Once the samosa is folded this way, heat oil and let the samosa fry slowly on low flame while turning gently until light brown. (If fried on low flame, it takes about 7-8 minutes.)
Samosas can be served with spicy chutney or sauce.
For making the dough:
Mix maida (all-purpose flour), ajwain (carom seeds), salt and oil, add water to knead a slightly firm dough and let it rest. For the stuffing:
Heat oil and add cumin seeds to it.
Once it turns brown, add ginger and leave it for 30 seconds.
Then add green chillies and after 2 minutes add fresh coriander leaves and leave for 30 seconds.
Then add coriander powder, turmeric, chaat masala, potatoes and mix well.
Then mix green peas, leave it for 2-3 minutes, add salt and set it aside to cool down. For shaping the samosas:
Divide the dough into 7 equal parts and make smooth balls.
Then roll out a roti, cut it into two halves, shape one half of the samosa, fill it with stuffing and seal the samosa using water.
Fry the samosas in hot oil on low heat until they turn slightly light brown.
Samosas can be served with sweet chutney.
For making the dough:
Add ajwain (carom seeds) and salt to maida (all-purpose flour), mix well, add 4 spoons of oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) and knead a proper dough.
Cover it and keep it to rest for 20-25 minutes. For the stuffing:
Once oil is heated in a pan, add ginger-chilli and fry a little, then add green peas and fry for a while, then add turmeric, red chilli powder, cashew nuts and stir for 1 minute.
Then add potatoes, garam masala, roasted cumin powder, salt, stir for 2-3 minutes and turn off the gas.
Then mix coriander.
Once the mixture cools down, add chaat masala and amchur (dry mango powder) powder and mix well. For the samosas:

Make small dough balls, roll them into a slightly thick roti, cut into two halves, fold one half, fold from the other side to make a samosa shape, fill with stuffing, apply water on top and seal by joining the two opposite layers.
Shape the samosas this way, heat oil and let them fry on low heat until light brown.
Cut the pav into two pieces from the middle.
Now roast the pav in the middle with butter and place a samosa inside.
Break the samosa if needed so that the pav can be closed properly.
Pav samosa can be served with spicy chutney or sauce.
In maida (all-purpose flour), add ghee, salt, knead a medium-soft dough with water, apply oil and keep it aside.
Now heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a pan.
Add cumin seeds, when the color of cumin changes, add ginger, green chillies, and salt, and sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Add mashed and finely chopped potatoes, salt, chaat masala, and garam masala, and mix everything well.
Sauté it for 2-3 minutes, take it out in a bowl, and let it cool.
Then make dough balls, roll out square rotis, and cut rectangular strips with a knife to make samosas of proper size.
Give it a triangular shape, fill the stuffing, and fold it into a square.
And seal the border with water.
Then heat oil in a kadai, and once the oil is hot, fry them on low heat until light brown.
They can be served with sauce.
To make the stuffing:
Heat oil in a non-stick pan, when the oil is hot, add ginger and leave it for 30 seconds.
Add French beans, carrot, cabbage, green chillies, and salt, and roast on high heat for 3-4 minutes.
Add noodles, mix soy sauce and vinegar, and keep on medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes.
Then keep it aside. To knead the dough:
To knead the dough, mix maida (all-purpose flour), ghee, lemon juice, and salt well, and knead a medium-soft dough with water. To shape the samosas:
Divide the stuffing into 16 equal parts.
Divide the dough into 8 equal parts, make balls, roll out rotis, cut the roti right from the center, and make two equal halves.
Take one half in hand, make a cone to fill the samosa, and seal it with the help of water.
Fill the stuffing from the top and seal the top side with water too.
Once all samosas are ready, fry them in hot oil on low heat.
It will take about 7-8 minutes to finish frying one batch of samosas.
Can be served with tomato sauce.
211.note: Chop the carrots and cabbage into long pieces. Chop the French beans in a round shape, about one inch per piece.

ing: finely chopped fresh coriander leaves – 1/2 cup
steps: Mix both flours in a bowl and add the fenugreek leaves and fresh coriander leaves to it.
Then add all the spices, oil, and curd, and knead into a dough.
Knead the dough so that it is neither too stiff nor too soft, using water as needed.
Now make small round balls from the prepared dough and roll them out into dhebras that are slightly larger and thicker than a puri.
Heat oil in a kadhai and fry all the dhebras in it.
These dhebras can be served hot as well as with cold curd, milk, or chutney.
214.note: Instead of frying, the dhebras can also be made by roasting them like parathas or theplas.

steps: Mix both flours in a bowl.
Then add all the spices, oil, and curd, and knead into a dough.
Knead the dough so that it is neither too stiff nor too soft, using water as needed.
Now make small round balls from the prepared dough and roll them out into dhebras that are slightly larger and thicker than a puri.
Heat oil in a kadhai and fry all the dhebras in it.
These dhebras can be served hot as well as with cold curd, milk, or chutney.
215.note: Instead of frying, the dhebras can also be made by roasting them like parathas or theplas.

steps: First combine both flours, add grated bottle gourd, ginger-chilli paste, turmeric powder, and salt, and mix in some oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour).
Then knead the dough using curd.
Knead the dough so that it is neither too stiff nor too soft, using water as needed.
Now make small round balls from the prepared dough and roll them out into dhebras that are slightly larger and thicker than a puri.
Heat oil in a kadhai and fry all the dhebras in it.
These dhebras can be served hot as well as with cold curd, milk, or chutney.
216.note: Adjust the quantity of flour according to the moisture of the bottle gourd. Instead of frying, the dhebras can also be made by roasting them like parathas or theplas.

steps: First combine both flours, add grated beetroot, ginger-chilli paste, turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, and salt, and mix in some oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour).
Then knead the dough using curd.
Knead the dough so that it is neither too stiff nor too soft, using water as needed.
Now make small round balls from the prepared dough and roll them out into dhebras that are slightly larger and thicker than a puri.
Heat oil in a kadhai and fry all the dhebras in it.
These dhebras can be served hot as well as with cold curd, milk, or chutney.
217.note: Instead of frying, the dhebras can also be made by roasting them like parathas or theplas.

steps: First mix pearl millet (bajra) flour and wheat flour in a bowl.
Then add all the above spices and chopped spinach, and knead into a dough using curd.
Add water only if needed (because the spinach will release water over time).
Now cover the dough and set it aside for 15 minutes to rest.
Now make small round balls from the prepared dough and roll them out into dhebras that are slightly larger and thicker than a puri.
Heat oil in a kadhai and fry all the dhebras in it.
These dhebras can be served hot as well as with cold curd, milk, or chutney.
218.note: Instead of frying, the dhebras can also be made by roasting them like parathas or theplas.

steps: Method for corn dhokla batter:
First, take semolina (rava) in a large bowl, add curd, ginger-chilli paste, and turmeric, and mix well.
Then add half a cup of warm water and oil to it, cover it, and keep it aside.
Let it ferment based on how sour you want it (6 to 8 hours).
If you do not want it sour, you can also make it in 2-3 hours. Method:
Grate the raw corn and add it to the batter, mixing well.
Take a dhokla plate and grease it with oil.
Place a dhokla maker/steamer on the gas and add 2 glasses of water.
Add white sesame seeds, 1 tsp eno/soda, and lemon juice to the batter, along with about 1 tablespoon of water, and mix.
Immediately pour it into the greased plate.
Sprinkle sesame seeds all over the top of the batter.
Then place the plate in the dhokla maker, and after 10-15 minutes once done, take it out and cut pieces with a knife. Make the remaining dhokla in the same way. For tempering (vaghar):
Heat oil in a tempering pan, add mustard seeds, white sesame seeds, chopped green chillies, and curry leaves. Pour this tempering over the dhokla and add fresh coriander leaves.
First, put 2 glasses of water in the dhokla maker to heat and grease a large plate with oil.
To make the green batter, take semolina (rava) in a vessel, add spinach puree, lemon, salt, and ground green chilli.
Then stir it, add 2 tsp of oil and 1/2 tsp of eno, and mix.
Now pour it into the oiled plate, place it in the dhokla maker, and steam for 4 minutes.
To make the white batter, take semolina (rava), curd, and salt in a vessel, add water as needed, add 1/2 tsp of eno, and stir.
Then spread this over the green batter plate and let it steam for 4 minutes.

For the orange batter, mix gram flour (besan), tomatoes, turmeric, and water. Then add 2 tsp of oil, salt, and 1/2 tsp of eno, stir, and spread this orange batter over the white batter. Cook for 18-20 minutes.
Take the plate out of the dhokla maker and cut it into square pieces. For tempering:
First, take oil in a black pan, add mustard seeds, 10-15 curry leaves, 2 tsp of white sesame seeds, and 4 pieces of chopped green chillies.
Then turn off the gas and pour the tempering over the dhokla.
Grated coconut can also be sprinkled on top.
220.note: Let all three batters soak by preparing them 20 minutes in advance. They turn out better if made this way, and mix the eno and oil only at the time of making. Do not stir too much after adding eno, and soda can be used in place of eno. Carrot puree can also be used to make the orange batter.

steps: First, take rice and chana dal in small portions and grind them in a mixer to prepare a batter.
Take the ground batter and cornmeal in a bowl, add sour buttermilk, and stir.
Then add lukewarm water while stirring continuously.
Keep the batter thick and cover it to ferment for 8 hours.
Now put water in a dhokla cooker and let it heat.
In the soaked batter, now add turmeric, salt, and ginger-chilli paste, and stir.
Take it in a vessel, add soda or eno (1/2 tsp), add lemon juice on top, and stir.
Now grease a dhokla-making plate with oil and spread the batter in it.
Sprinkle red chilli powder all around on top, place it in the dhokla cooker, and let it cook for 10-15 minutes.
Once done, take out the plate and cut square pieces. For tempering:
Take oil in a tempering pan, add mustard seeds, 10-15 curry leaves, white sesame seeds, and chopped green chillies.
Pour this tempering over the dhokla.
Grated coconut can also be sprinkled on top.
221.note: Dhokla can also be made by adding grated bottle gourd to the batter.

steps: First, wash moong dal and rice and soak them for 5 to 6 hours.
Now drain the water from the soaked dal and rice and grind them. Grind by adding a little curd as needed.
Now add salt, turmeric, and ajwain (carom seeds) to this batter and mix.
Now prepare a plate by applying oil to it.
Take as much batter as fits in that plate in a vessel, add 1 spoon of eno, and mix.
Now take the prepared batter in that plate and sprinkle red chilli powder and fresh coriander leaves on top.
Now place it in a hot steamer and keep it on medium flame.
Once the dhokla is cooked, cut it and serve hot.
This dhokla can also be served with a tempering of mustard seeds, sesame seeds, and curry leaves.
First, mix all three flours thoroughly.
Take lemon juice in a bowl, add oil, add a little water, add 1/4 soda, and mix.
Add this mixture to the flour.
Then add all the flours, salt, turmeric, coriander-cumin powder, sugar, and ginger-chilli paste to the grated bottle gourd and mix well.
Then keep adding water little by little to knead the dough.
Now put 2 glasses of water in the dhokla maker, place a stand, roll them into logs in a perforated sieve, and steam for 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, check with a knife and then cut into small pieces.
Put oil in a vessel, add mustard seeds, curry leaves, sesame seeds, and chopped green chillies to make the tempering.
Then pour the tempering over the muthiya, mix well, and finally add fresh coriander leaves on top.

ing: fresh fenugreek leaves chopped – 500 grams (as needed)
sweet neem leaves (curry leaves) – as needed
steps: First, mix all the flours together, add the chopped fenugreek leaves, and mix well.
Then add oil, red chilli powder, salt, turmeric, garam masala, coriander-cumin powder, sugar, and ginger-chilli paste and mix.
In a small bowl, mix a little lemon juice, oil, water, and baking soda, and add it to the dough.
Then knead a firm dough, using buttermilk as needed.
Now, pour 2 glasses of water into the dhokla maker, grease the perforated plate with oil, and arrange all the rolls.
After steaming for 30 minutes, let them cool and cut them into small pieces.
Heat oil in a pan, make a tempering with mustard-cumin seeds, oil, and curry leaves, and garnish with coriander on top if desired.

ing: split black gram dal (udad dal) – 1 bowl
steps: First, soak the udad dal and rice for 5 hours.
Now take the mixed dal and rice in a mixer jar, add curd and water, and grind to prepare a batter.
Then leave this batter to ferment for 14 hours.
Afterward, add salt and ginger-chilli paste to the batter and stir.
Add a little water and a spoon of oil to this batter, then add baking soda if needed and mix for a short while.
Then place a plate in the steamer, grease it with oil, pour the batter, and sprinkle black pepper powder and chaat masala on top.
Steam for 20 minutes.
Now take the plate out, heat oil in a small bowl, prepare a tempering of mustard-cumin seeds and curry leaves, and pour it over the idda.

ing: fresh coriander leaves – 3 tbsp finely chopped
steps: Mix buttermilk with gram flour (besan), add salt and turmeric, and make a batter.
Now place a pan on the gas, take the prepared batter in it, and keep stirring continuously until it thickens.
Once ready, spread a very thin layer on a platform or flat surface.
Once cooled, cut long strips and roll them.
Now heat oil, add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, sweet neem leaves, and round-cut rings of green chillies.
Add sesame seeds to make a tempering and then pour it over the khandvi.
Finally, sprinkle chopped fresh coriander leaves and grated dry coconut on top.

ing: fresh coriander leaves chopped – as needed
steps: Take gram flour in a vessel, add salt, citric acid crystals, and sugar to it, add water, and mix well.
Make a batter that is neither too thick nor too thin and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Take water in a steamer and put it on to heat.
Now prepare the steamer plate by greasing it with oil.
Add Eno to the prepared batter and stir it in only one direction for 30 seconds.
Then pour this mixture into the greased plate and place it in the steamer for 25 minutes.
Now we need to prepare the tempering for the khaman.
Heat oil in a pan and temper it with mustard seeds, green chillies, curry leaves, and sugar.
Add water, let it boil properly, and pour it over the sliced cooked khaman dish.
Garnish on top with chopped fresh coriander leaves.
First, soak the rice and fenugreek seeds in water for 5 hours.
After 5 hours, drain the rice and grind it in a mixer along with poha, coconut, and water as needed to make a smooth batter.
Now, take warm water in a small bowl, dissolve the sugar, add the yeast, and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Now add this yeast mixture to the prepared batter and mix well.
Cover and keep this batter to ferment for 8 hours.
After 8 hours, stir the batter slightly, add salt and water to make a slightly thin batter.
Now heat a pan with a lid on medium heat, pour a ladleful of batter into it, and immediately spread it in a circle like a dosa.
Cover the pan with a lid and let the appam cook properly in the steam.
Prepare all the appams in this way.
Appam can be enjoyed with coconut chutney and sambar.
First, take all the grains according to the measurements and soak the jowar for eight to ten hours.
Now wash all the remaining grains nicely and soak them for one hour.
Drain the soaked jowar and churn it in a mixer two to three times for two seconds each so that its outer husks come off.
Then add one and a half cups of water to the prepared jowar dalia and pressure cook it for two to three whistles.
Now add all the other grains, salt, and 3 1/2 times water to the boiled jowar dalia and cook the khichdo for 3 to 4 whistles.
If green chickpeas are not available, soak dry chickpeas and add them to be boiled with the jowar dalia.
So the sattvic and delicious khichdo is ready, add ghee to it and serve hot.
Keep the moong dal soaked for 3 to 5 hours.
Then wash well, take a little dal in a mixer jar along with ginger and chilli, and grind in the mixer.
After that, grind the remaining dal without adding water.
Grind the dal coarsely and make sure the batter does not become smooth.
Then add salt as required to this batter and add finely chopped fresh coriander leaves.
Then place oil on the gas for frying and fry the vadas in the oil.
Fry the vadas on medium gas.
To make potato balls:
Mash the boiled potatoes and add white sesame seeds, pepper powder, ginger, salt, and powdered sugar to them.
Now add dry coriander powder, mashed green spicy chillies, and fresh coriander leaves, and mix well.
Now roll them into balls and arrange them on a dish. To make the batter:
First, add a little water to the gram flour (besan), add soda to it, pour lemon juice over it, and stir.
Add only enough water so that the batter remains as thick as kadhi, and add salt to taste. To make potato vadas:
Put oil to heat. After the oil gets hot, turn the gas to medium.
Now keep dipping the prepared balls into the batter and drop them into the oil one by one.
Fry until a light golden color appears.
The wheat and jowar flours should be kept slightly coarse.
Then we will add 2 spoons of dhokla flour to it.
Then add crushed green chillies and ginger to it.
Add a few sesame seeds right when kneading the dough.
Then mix turmeric and every other thing nicely while adding water little by little.
Take care that the dough does not become too loose.
Add salt to taste and keep it aside for 5 to 6 hours.
Then add 1/4 spoon of soda to it, add 1 spoon of oil, and stir well.
Heat oil in a kadai and fry small vadas.
Fry the vadas on medium heat so that they become crispy from outside and soft from inside.
239.note: It is necessary to maintain the proper texture of the dough. Urad flour can also be added in place of dhokla flour. You can also add red chilli powder according to your requirement.

steps: First soak the cashews and chana dal for 2 hours.
Then remove them from water and put them in a mixer jar.
Now add green chillies, ginger, cumin seeds and black pepper, and grind coarsely.
Now take this mixture in a bowl, add rice flour, fennel seeds, turmeric powder, salt and cashew pieces, and mix well.
Now put oil to heat.
Then make small balls from the prepared mixture, flatten them with your palm and fry them in hot oil.
Fry until they turn golden brown color.
Hot cashew vadas are ready.
First mix both the flours mentioned above.
Then lightly roast cumin seeds, coriander seeds, black pepper and fennel seeds, and crush them in a mortar and pestle.
Then add turmeric powder, salt, red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, garam masala, fenugreek leaves, sesame seeds and sugar.
Add water as required to make a stiff batter.
Then add 1 tea spoon of soda, squeeze lemon juice over it and pour two to three spoons of hot oil.
Mix everything and fry gota of moderate size.
Keep the gas low and increase it slightly when needed.
241.note: Rice flour can be used instead of coarse gram flour. Vadas become very crispy with rice flour. These gota taste very delicious with curd. Roasted chana dal flour can also be used with the above ingredients.

steps: First slit the chillies and remove their seeds.
Crush the gathiya, crumble the laddoos into it, add lemon juice, salt and fenugreek leaves, and mix well to make the stuffing.
Stuff this mixture inside the whole chillies.
Take gram flour (besan) in a bowl, add water, salt, turmeric powder and lemon juice, and make a batter of pouring consistency.
Then dip the chillies in that batter and fry them in hot oil on low heat.
First mix both flours and add all the spices to them.
Then add all the vegetables and water as required to make a batter suitable for making bhajiyas.
Fry the bhajiyas in preheated oil.
243.note: Vegetables of choice can be added. Lemon juice or dry mango powder can be added as needed. Fry the bhajiyas until hard and crispy. The quantity of vegetables can be increased and flour decreased. This will make the bhajiyas very crispy. Adjust spices according to taste.

ing: Finely chopped fresh fenugreek leaves – 250 grams
steps: First add chopped fenugreek leaves, coriander leaves and ginger-chilli pieces to gram flour (besan).
Then add whole coriander seeds by crushing them slightly.
Add red chilli powder, turmeric powder, 1 spoon of sugar, whole black pepper, 1/2 spoon of salt and knead/mix well.
Then add water as needed to make a batter that is neither too thin nor too stiff.
Add baking soda to it.
Then fry small portions of bhajiyas in preheated oil.
Make sure they do not remain uncooked from the inside.
244.note: Fry on high flame first, then lower the flame. Pouring hot oil over the soda makes them whiter. Black pepper can also be used coarsely crushed. Coarse gram flour or about 50 grams of rava can also be added while making.

steps: First, wash the fenugreek leaves and coriander, chop them finely, and keep them ready.
Prepare a paste of ginger and chillies.
Take gram flour (besan) in a bowl and mix the fenugreek and coriander into it.
Add salt, chilli-ginger paste, and lemon juice, and mix very well.
No water should be used, so add only as much gram flour (besan) as the greens can absorb.
Pay close attention while frying; drop small bhajiya specifically using your fingers and thumb.
245.note: While dropping the bhajiyas, you can keep a bowl of water nearby and dip your hands so the bhajiyas come out small and separate. Add plenty of ginger and chillies.

steps: First, take gram flour (besan) in a bowl and blend in the fresh coriander leaves and ginger-chilli paste.
Then add salt, coriander-cumin powder, lemon juice, and a little water, and mix well.
Next, slice the bananas and mix them in.
Now, heat oil in a kadhai and drop the banana slices one by one into the oil as bhajiyas.
When they turn brown on a slow flame, remove them onto a plate using a slotted spoon.

ing: cashews, raisins, grated dry coconut – 2 spoons
steps: First, mix salt and water into the gram flour (besan) to prepare a thick batter and set it aside.
Now, mash the boiled potatoes and mix in salt, sugar, ginger-chilli paste, finely chopped fresh coriander leaves, garam masala, lemon juice, cashews, raisins, and grated dry coconut.
Now mix powdered sugar into the butter, make small balls of it, and place them in the fridge to chill.
When you want to fry the bhajiyas, put oil to heat in a kadhai.
Then take the butter balls out of the fridge, flatten the potato mixture like a puri.
Place the butter ball in the center, cover it completely with the potato mixture in a spherical shape, and put it back in the fridge.
After 10-15 minutes, take the balls out of the fridge, dip each ball into the gram flour (besan) batter, and fry them in oil.
247.note: Take out only as many balls from the fridge as needed right at the time of frying. You can also make direct butter bhajiyas: roll chilled butter balls in dry gram flour and let them rest for a while. After a while, dip them in the prepared batter, drop them immediately into hot oil, and remove them. Let them cool for a short while, then dip them in the batter again and fry them properly in oil.

steps: First, heat oil for tempering, and add whole coriander seeds, bay leaves, and green peas to temper.

Add garam masala, red chilli powder, amchur (dry mango powder), turmeric, coriander-cumin powder, fresh coriander leaves, ginger-chilli paste, and mashed boiled potatoes, mix well, add lemon juice, and prepare the filling.
Next, take gram flour (besan), add a pinch of soda, ajwain (carom seeds), and salt to prepare a thick batter.
Then take very firm tomatoes and cut off half an inch from the top.
Scoop out the inner juice and seed portion with a knife to make hollow shell-like tomatoes.
Then stuff the potato mawa (khoya) tightly inside the tomatoes.
Next, dip the stuffed tomatoes into the gram flour (besan) batter.
Now, heat oil for frying in a kadhai, drop the bhajiyas one by one, and take them out once they turn brown.
Cut these bhajiyas before serving and you can serve them by sprinkling amchur (dry mango powder) on top.
Boil the potatoes and mash them.
Take oil for tempering in a kadhai, add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and crushed ginger-chilli paste, and sauté.
After a short while, add cashews, raisins, and the mashed boiled potatoes, and mix well.
Now blend in fresh coriander leaves, salt, lemon juice, grated dry coconut, and garam masala.
Now trim the crusts of all the bread slices.
Then dip a bread slice into a bowl filled with water and press it between both hands to squeeze out the water.
Now place the potato mixture in the center and shape the bread into a ball using your hands.
Give it a ball-like shape ensuring the bread is not open from any side.
Now take gram flour (besan), add a pinch of soda, ajwain (carom seeds), and salt to prepare a very thin batter.
Now dip into the prepared gram flour (besan) mixture and fry on a low flame in oil.
Remove once it turns golden brown.
249.note: The bread balls can also be fried directly.

steps: First take gram flour (besan) in a bowl and add ajwain (carom seeds) and pepper powder to it.
Now add salt, baking soda, ginger-chilli paste, two teaspoons of oil, fresh coriander leaves, and finely chopped spinach into it.
Add water little by little to the batter and mix to prepare the mixture.
Make this mixture such that it is neither too thick nor too thin.
Now heat oil in a kadhai (pan).
Then drop portions of the prepared mixture into the oil to make pakoras and take them out once they turn golden brown.
250.note: Whole chilli pakoras turn out great when fried on low heat for a longer time. A masala of potatoes, peas, etc., can also be stuffed inside the chillies.

ing: salt and black salt – to taste
steps: First take gram flour (besan) in a bowl and add corn starch to it.
Then add soda, ginger-chilli paste, red chilli powder, turmeric, coriander-cumin powder, ajwain (carom seeds), salt, and black salt.
Then add a little water first and mix it well.
Then add water as needed, making sure not to make the batter thin, keep it thick.
Prepare the batter in this way.
Peel the outer skin of the ridge gourd and cut it into round or oval slices.
Take oil in a heavy-bottomed pan, and once it is hot, dip the ridge gourd slices into the batter and mix.
Then drop the slices into the oil and fry them until they turn golden brown, then remove them.
251.note: Vegetables of choice can be added. Lemon juice or dry mango powder can be added as needed. Fry the pakoras until hard and crispy. The quantity of vegetables can be increased and flour decreased, which will make the pakoras very crispy. Adjust spices according to taste.

ing: chaat masala or garam masala – 1 teaspoon
steps: First, coarsely crush the boiled corn in a bowl.
Add gram flour (besan) and rice flour to it along with all the spices.
After that, first add turmeric and red chilli powder, then add chaat masala.
Then add ginger-chilli paste and finely chopped curry leaves.
Next, add salt to taste and mix everything well.
Add a little water if needed, and do not add water if it is not needed.
Heat oil and drop the corn pakoras into it to fry.
Thus, crispy corn pakoras will be ready.
252.note: Fry on high flame first, then lower the flame. Pouring hot oil over the soda makes it whiter. Crushed pepper can also be added. You can also make it by adding about 50 grams of coarse chickpea flour or semolina.

steps: First mix coarsely crushed dry coriander seeds, turmeric, red chilli powder, and salt into the gram flour (besan).
Then add water to it to make a batter of medium thickness.
Next, heat oil in a kadhai, add a pinch of soda and lemon juice to the batter, and mix well.
Once the oil is hot, dip the carom leaves into the batter and drop them to make pakoras.
Then they can be served with sauce, spicy or sweet chutney.
Cut thin chips of brinjal.
Add 1/2 teaspoon red chilli powder and 1/2 teaspoon salt to them, mix well, and let them rest for 15 minutes.
Then add ajwain (carom seeds), cumin seeds, coriander, red chilli powder, turmeric, salt, and fresh coriander leaves to the gram flour (besan).
Add water to it, mix well, and prepare a batter of moderate thickness.
Now put oil in a kadhai, and once the oil is hot, dip the brinjal chips in the batter and put them in the oil.
Remove them from the oil once they turn slightly golden brown.
Brinjal pakoras can be served with sauce.
Soak the rice in water for 2-3 hours.
Then grind it into a paste in a mixer and transfer it to a bowl.
Cut the poi leaves into appropriate-sized pieces.
Now take them in a bowl, add gram flour (besan), turmeric, black pepper, ginger, green chillies, rice paste, and salt, and mix well.
Next, heat oil in a kadhai, and once the oil is hot, drop portions of the batter into it to fry the bhajiyas.
You can sprinkle chaat masala on top.
Serve the bhajiyas with mint chutney or sauce.
Wash and wipe the chillies dry.
Now slice the chillies vertically down the middle into two halves.
Remove all the seeds and veins from them.
Now mix salt, lemon, and turmeric into the chillies.
Now mix gram flour into the chillies.
Add only 3-4 spoons of water, just enough for the gram flour to stick to the chillies; do not add too much water.
Now heat oil in a kadhai.
Once the oil is hot, drop the chillies one by one into it and fry them until they turn light golden.
Crispy chilli patti bhajiyas are ready.
256.note: If the chillies are very large, they can also be cut into four strips. These bhajiyas can also be made by preparing a gram flour batter and dipping the chillies in it.

steps: Remove the veins of the arbi leaves using a knife and chop them finely.
Then add salt, ajwain (carom seeds), cumin seeds, turmeric, ginger paste, and green chillies to 1 cup of gram flour.
Now add red chilli powder, amchur (dry mango powder) powder, chaat masala, finely chopped arbi leaves, and baking soda.
Then add a little water and mix everything well to make a batter of medium thickness.
Heat oil in a kadhai.
Once the oil is hot, drop medium-sized portions of the batter into it as bhajiyas.
Fry on medium heat until brown.
The bhajiyas can be served with sauce.
Cut the potatoes into small pieces. Heat about 6 spoons of oil in a kadhai, add the potatoes, and keep stirring until they turn golden brown.
Now add green peas, salt, ginger, chillies, black pepper, lemon, and garam masala, and let it cool down.
Now add poppy seeds and fresh coriander leaves to prepare the stuffing.
Next, knead a dough using maida (all-purpose flour), food colour, salt, and oil (60 ml).
If the food colour already contains salt, do not add salt to the dough.
Now roll out small puris from the dough.
Shape this puri into a cone, fill it with the stuffing, and give it the shape of a stuffed chilli.
Fry these prepared chillies just like samosas.
Marwadi chillies are ready.
First, add salt, red chilli powder, and baking soda to the gram flour.
Now add water and mix well to prepare a thick batter.
Let it rest for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel the potatoes and slice them into evenly-sized chips.
Dip them in the batter and fry them in hot oil until golden brown.
Then remove them onto a tray and sprinkle some chaat masala on top.
Batata puris can be served with sauce.
First, take 2 cups of gram flour (besan), urad dal flour, and rice flour in a bowl.
Then add curd and 2 cups of water to it and mix well.
Cover and keep this mixture in a warm place for 8-9 hours to ferment.
After fermentation, add bottle gourd, potatoes, cabbage, ginger, green chilli, turmeric, salt, and water to the mixture.
Stir the handvo batter well, and add water to thin it out if necessary.
Now heat oil in a non-stick pan and make a tempering of mustard seeds, dried red chillies, sesame seeds, and curry leaves.
Add this tempering to the handvo batter and mix well.
Now take a portion of the mixture in a small vessel, add baking soda and lemon juice, and mix well.
This will make the handvo rise nicely and become soft.
Spread the handvo batter over the prepared tempering.
Cover the pan and cook the handvo on low heat.
Once the handvo turns golden brown in color, flip it to the other side.
Handvo is ready.
First, wash the rice and toor dal 2-3 times, soak them for 4-5 hours, and grind them.
Now add crushed ginger-chillies, grated bottle gourd, turmeric, and salt to this batter and mix well.
Next, heat oil in a pan, make a tempering of mustard seeds and sesame seeds, and add this tempering to the batter.
Now heat a little oil in a skillet, pour a ladleful of the prepared batter like a thick pancake, cover it, and let it cook. Once cooked on one side, flip it and let it cook on the other side.
261.note: Adding baking soda or eno to the batter makes the dangela soft.

steps: Mash the boiled potatoes by hand and add green peas, salt to taste, coriander-cumin powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, and fresh coriander leaves, mixing everything well.
Now take maida (all-purpose flour), mix salt and oil thoroughly, and knead a moderately soft dough with water.
Apply oil, cover it, and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Then make equal-sized dough balls, roll them into oval rotis, and fill the stuffing in the center.
Now bring both sides together and seal them like a ghughra.
Heat oil in a kadhai and fry all the ghughras on medium heat until they turn light brown.
Make a hole in the center of the ghughra and top it with all the chutneys, sev, masala peanuts, and fresh coriander leaves before serving.
First, break the ganthiya into bite-sized pieces and spread them evenly on a plate.
Then arrange pieces of pav on the plate and pour spicy chutney over the top.
Mix maida (all-purpose flour), salt, and ajwain (carom seeds) in a bowl.
Add water to knead a dough and keep it aside covered.
Next, grind ginger, chillies, and tomatoes in a mixer to make a paste.
Heat oil in a pan, add cloves, and add the prepared paste.
Add red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, and pav bhaji masala, mixing well.
When oil starts separating from it, add boiled potatoes and peas.
Then add salt to taste, let the bhaji simmer for 5 minutes, and add lemon juice and fresh coriander leaves.
Now roll out the previously kneaded dough into a roti, cut it from the center, and divide it into 2 parts.
Place one part onto a cone mold, apply water to the edge of the roti, and seal it.
Shape all the cones this way, place them on cone molds, heat oil, and fry them.
As they fry, the cones will automatically separate from the cone molds.
Once the cones cool down, fill them with bhaji, grate cheese on top, and sprinkle fresh coriander leaves.
Delicious bhaji cones are ready.
