Boil water in a pan.
Then add jaggery to it.
Once the jaggery melts, crumble the rotis and add them along with ghee.
Mix well and stir like sheera until it becomes thick.
Turn off the gas and keep it covered for a while.
Then add cardamom powder and serve.

ing: (red chilli powder, turmeric, coriander-cumin powder, salt, sugar) – to taste
steps: Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds and cumin seeds to it.
Then add buttermilk, salt, and sugar, and let it boil.
Cut the rotis into 1 to 1.5 inch pieces and add them to the buttermilk.
Now add turmeric and red chilli powder and mix well.
Now cover and simmer on low heat until the buttermilk evaporates.
Once ready, garnish with coriander-cumin powder and fresh coriander leaves and serve.

ing: chana dal – 500 grams (soaked for 4 hours beforehand)
citric acid crystals (limbu na phool) – 1 teaspoon
steps: First take the soaked chana dal, citric acid crystals, and green chillies, crush them in a mixer adding water as needed and add salt.
Take a plate and grease it with oil, then add baking soda to the batter and stir continuously in one direction.
Then put 2 glasses of water in a dhokla maker and place the stand at the bottom.
Pour the batter into the plate and place it in the dhokla maker.
After 20 minutes turn off the gas and let it cool, then cut it into pieces and crumble it. For Tempering:
Heat oil in a kadhai, then add mustard seeds, sesame seeds, green chillies, curry leaves, and turmeric, stir and then add water.
Next add sugar, then add the crumbled khaman, add lemon juice and mix.
Now add pomegranate arils, sev, and fresh coriander leaves and serve.
272.note: Sev khamani can be enjoyed with green chutney.

ing: finely chopped fresh coriander leaves – 4 tablespoons
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into small pieces.
Then wash the poha, soak it for about 5 minutes, and strain it in a colander.
Heat oil in a vessel on the gas and add mustard seeds, sesame seeds, green chillies, curry leaves, and cinnamon-cloves powder.
Now add potatoes, turmeric, and salt, cover and let them cook.
Then add sugar and lemon, add the poha, and mix well.
After that, add cashews-raisins and pomegranate arils, mix well and take it off the heat.
Transfer bataka poha to a dish and sprinkle fresh coriander leaves and grated dry coconut on top.

ing: citric acid crystals (limbu na phool) – 1/2 teaspoon
steps: Heat oil in a vessel on the gas.
Now take poha in a perforated vessel and fry it in the oil, then transfer it to a large bowl.
Add turmeric and chilli powder proportionate to the poha so that the spice mixes well.
Then fry the peanuts, and fry cashews and raisins on low heat and transfer them to the bowl containing poha.
Next, fry curry leaves and green chillies and add them to that bowl.
Now add salt, chilli powder, turmeric, powdered sugar, sesame seeds, fennel seeds, citric acid crystals, etc., to the poha.
Once the chevdo is ready, add 2 teaspoons of whole sugar.
Tasty peanut poha chevdo is ready.
First, take oil in a pan for frying.
In that, fry the corn poha and remove them using a slotted spoon.
Then fry the rice poha and afterwards fry the peanuts.
Take oil in a vessel on the gas, add curry leaves to it, and then add the murmura.
Add powdered sugar and salt, mix well, then add the fried rice poha, corn poha, and peanuts, and add turmeric and red chilli powder and mix thoroughly.
Soak the peas in water overnight.
Now dry and wipe the peas clean.
Now heat oil in a kadhai.
Now fry the peas, peanuts, cashews, and chana dal one by one in that oil.
Drain the excess oil from them and mix them in a bowl.
Now roast the curry leaves and add them to the bowl.
Now mix the sev, bundi, salt, red chilli powder, chaat masala, and mango powder well in the bowl.
Peas chevdo is ready.
276.note: When frying the peas, cover the kadhai from above after putting them in.

steps: First, take large potatoes, peel them, use a grater with large holes, and grate the potatoes.
Wash the grated potatoes 2-3 times with water and wipe them with a cloth.
Then spread them on a cloth and let the grated potatoes dry for 1 to 2 hours.
Now take oil in a kadhai for frying, heat it, put the grated potatoes in it, and fry until golden brown.
Then fry the peanuts and raisins.
Now take the grated potatoes, peanuts, and raisins in a vessel, add salt, powdered sugar, red chilli powder, and pepper powder, and mix well.
277.note: Chana dal can also be added to it. Soak it for 4 hours, fry it, and then mix it in. Sesame seeds can also be added to it.

steps: Put oil in a kadhai to heat.
Once the oil is properly hot, fry the corn poha.
Then fry the peanuts as well.
Add salt, chili, and sugar to the fried poha and peanuts and mix well.
Crispy corn poha chevdo is ready.

ing: amchur (dry mango powder) powder – to taste
steps: First, put oil to heat.
Once the oil is properly hot, fry the wheat poha in it.
Then fry the peanuts and cashews in the same oil.
Now mix the poha, peanuts, and cashews and mix all the spices in it.
Wheat poha chevdo is ready.
279.note: Murmura, sev, fried chana dal, etc., can be added to this chevdo according to your preference.

ing: Citric acid crystals (limbu na phool) – 2 tablespoons
steps: Soak the chana dal for 4-5 hours.
Then drain it, let it dry slightly, and fry it in hot oil on a low flame.
Grate the potatoes and fry them on a low flame.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a kadhai and first add the green chillies and curry leaves to it.
Then add the sesame seeds and turmeric powder, and mix well.
Spread this tempering over the fried chana dal and grated potatoes.
Now add the cashews-raisins, powdered sugar, citric acid crystals, and salt to taste.
The chevdo is ready.
Roast all the urad papads and keep them aside.
Roast the nylon poha in a pan for 5-6 minutes.
Then heat oil in the same pan, add the peanuts, and sauté on a low flame for 1-2 minutes.
Then add the cashews and sauté for 15-20 seconds.
Now in the same pan, add sliced green chillies and curry leaves, followed by dry raisins, sesame seeds, and grated dry coconut.
Then add turmeric powder and amchur (dry mango powder), and after 15-20 seconds, add the roasted poha and mix everything well.
After that, add salt, powdered sugar, and papad pieces, and mix everything together.
Soak the wheat in water for 2 days. Change the water 4 times in 2 days.
After 2 days, rub the wheat well 2-3 times and wash it with plain water.
Then drain the water using a strainer, add the wheat and about 12 cups of water into a cooker, and let it whistle 2-3 times on medium flame.
Then drain 3 cups of water from the wheat, add a little salt, papadkhar, and baking soda, mix everything well, and let it whistle 1 more time.
Once the cooker cools down, drain all the water using a strainer. When the wheat cools down completely, let it dry in a cotton cloth under the sun for 2-3 days.
Once completely dry, heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a kadhai, add the wheat in small batches one by one, and let it pop on medium flame until it starts popping. Prepare wheat flakes this way.
Then heat about 1 teaspoon of oil in a kadhai, roast the peanuts in it, and then add curry leaves and grated dry coconut, and sauté for 2 minutes.
Then add daliya and cashews, sauté while stirring for 30 seconds, add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and a pinch of salt to prepare the tempering this way.
Then mix the roasted wheat into it. The chevdo is ready.

ing: Citric acid crystals (limbu na phool) – 1/4 teaspoon
steps: Roast the nylon poha in a kadhai.
Heat oil in a kadhai and sauté the peanuts and roasted chana dal until their color changes.
Now add the cashews and sauté until they turn light brown.
Then sauté the dry raisins and dry coconut until golden brown.
Now in the same, add sliced green chillies and curry leaves for tempering.
Then lower the flame and mix in cumin seeds, sesame seeds, turmeric powder, citric acid crystals, poha, dry fruits, roasted chana dal, and peanuts—everything together.
Then sprinkle red chilli powder, salt, and powdered sugar on top and mix everything thoroughly.
Nylon chevdo is ready.
283.note: Sauté everything until well and truly crispy, so the chevdo doesn't get soggy from moisture.

ing: Citric acid crystals (limbu na phool) – to taste
steps: Mix all the above ingredients well in a vessel.
Nadiadi chavanu is ready.
First, add a pinch of soda, salt, turmeric, and oil moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) to the gram flour and knead into a dough.
Fill the sev maker with the dough and press out sev.
Then change the plate of the sev maker to the fafda plate and press out fafdas.
Then press out gathiya using the gathiya plate.
Next, fry all the above-mentioned lentils separately.
Then fry the rice flakes and corn flakes.
Finally, in a bowl, combine the sev, fafda, gathiya, lentils, rice flakes, corn flakes, and all the above spices, and mix well.
Surti Bhusu is ready.

ing: Citric acid (limbu na ful) – to taste
steps: First, add a pinch of soda, salt, turmeric, and oil moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) to the gram flour and knead into a dough.
Fill the sev maker with the dough and press out sev.
Then change the plate of the sev maker to the fafda plate and press out fafdas.
Then press out gathiya using the gathiya plate.
Next, fry all the above-mentioned lentils separately.
Then fry the rice flakes and corn flakes.
Finally, in a bowl, combine the sev, fafda, gathiya, lentils, rice flakes, corn flakes, and all the above spices, and mix well.
Surti Bhusu is ready.
286.note: All the ingredients can be mixed together, and a tempering (vighar) of oil, mustard seeds, sesame seeds, and dried red chillies can be poured over the chavanu.

steps: First, roast the corn flakes in a pan.
Stir continuously while doing so.
Once fully roasted, mix in turmeric powder, red chilli powder, powdered sugar, and salt.
287.note: They can also be made by frying, but roasted poha is better for health.

steps: In a vessel, mix water and oil well and whisk it until frothy.
Now add salt and hand-crushed ajwain (carom seeds) to the gram flour.
Add the water and oil mixture to the flour and knead it well to form a dough.
Now take 1 teaspoon of oil in your hands and knead the dough for 7-8 minutes.
Grease the gathiya machine with oil, fill it with the dough.
On medium flame, rotate the press in circular motions to drop the gathiya into the oil and fry them.
They will fry in about a minute and a half to two minutes.
288.note: There is no need to use soda in this method. The gathiya will turn out soft. They will stay good for 1 month. Black pepper powder can also be added.

steps: Heat a little oil in a vessel on medium flame.
In another vessel, add oil and an equal amount of water.
Mix well and stir thoroughly for 2-3 minutes.
Gradually add the gram flour little by little to prepare the dough.
Apply some oil to your hands to prevent sticking and make the dough smooth.
Now grease the press with oil and fill it with the dough.
Put oil on heat for frying; the oil should be at medium heat.
Then rotate and fry them.
Take flour in a vessel, add all the above spices and mix well.
Add water little by little and knead a dough.
Now oil the sev maker (sancha) and fill it with the dough.
Put oil to heat for frying, the oil should be medium hot.
Then fry by turning them over.
Take salt and soda in a small bowl, add 3 spoons of water to it and mix well.
Make a well in the center of the gram flour, add the soda water and 2 spoons of oil.
Mix the dough and add ajwain (carom seeds) and pepper to it.
Take a little oil and knead the dough thoroughly.
Put oil to heat in a kadhai.
Now take a small portion of the dough, grease it with oil and press it gently with the help of your palm directly on the platform to roll out gathiya.
Fry them on slow to medium flame.
291.note: Vanela gathiya are served with fried spicy chillies and raw papaya sambharo. The more we knead the dough, the softer the gathiya become.

steps: Mix papadkhar and salt, and roast on a griddle (lodhi) for 20 seconds.
Add salt, khar and oil in a vessel and mix.
Now add gram flour to it and mix.
Add water little by little and knead a soft dough.
Put oil to heat in a kadhai.
Now take some dough, place it on a perforated strainer (jhara) and rub it with the help of your palm.
Keep the gas low while dropping the gathiya so that hands do not get burned.
Once dropped, fry on high flame.
First, cut the rotlis into very small pieces.
Now heat oil in a kadhai.
Then add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, chopped green chillies and curry leaves for tempering.
Next, add peanuts and let them roast for a while.
Now add turmeric, salt and chilli powder and stir a little.
Then immediately add the rotli pieces and mix everything well.
Roast until the rotli pieces become completely crisp.
Now add coriander-cumin powder, lemon, sugar and pomegranate arils and mix well.
Hot chandan kachori is ready.
First take wheat flour in a vessel.
Add grated cheese, salt to taste and oil to it and mix everything well.
Then keep adding water little by little, knead a firm dough and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Then make small dough balls from it.
Now roll out very thin khakhras from them.
Then roast them on a griddle on low flame and after roasting a little, add two or three drops of oil and roast by pressing with the help of a cloth.
294.note: You can also make these khakhras in a roti maker machine instead of a griddle.

steps: First apply oil to your hands.
Then peel the suran, slice thin wafers, and drop them directly into water.
Now take 3-4 glasses of water in a pan, add a large pinch of salt, and heat it on medium flame.
Once hot, add the suran wafers to it and let them heat for 5 minutes.
Then take them down, remove the wafers from the water, dry them on a cloth, and gently dry them further with another napkin.
Now take oil in a pan and heat it on medium heat.
Once hot, add the wafers and keep stirring them.
Once crispy, remove them.
Sprinkle black pepper powder, sugar, salt, and lemon juice on top to taste.
First peel the potatoes and make thin slices using a slicer.
To prevent the potato slices from turning black, immediately keep them in a bowl filled with water.
Now spread these slices on a cotton cloth and cover them with another cotton cloth.
Keep them covered until the slices are dried.
Once the slices are dried, take them out onto a plate.
Now heat oil in a kadhai. After the oil is properly heated, fry the wafers.
If you want to eat salted wafers, just sprinkle salt.
But if you want to eat masala wafers, you can sprinkle chili powder or chaat masala along with salt.
301.note: Make sure that the oil is not excessively hot, otherwise the wafers will burn.

steps: First peel the bananas.
Do not peel all at once because the bananas will turn black. Peel 2-3 pieces of bananas at a time.
Then put oil in a kadhai to heat.
When the oil is hot, slice the bananas directly into the oil using a slicing machine.
Keep the gas medium initially, then lower it and let them fry.
While these wafers are frying, peel the next batch of bananas.
Once the wafers are done, take them out into a bowl and when slightly cooled, add black pepper powder, salt, and black salt to it.
Peel the purple yam.
Put oil to heat, and while the oil is heating, wash the purple yam and slice thin chips directly onto a cotton cloth.
Once the oil is hot, add the sliced chips into it and let them fry on low flame.
Let them fry until crispy, then take them out into a bowl.
Then mix black pepper powder, black salt, and salt on top of it to taste.
Wash and boil the potatoes, then peel and grate them.
Add gram flour (besan), salt, chili powder, black pepper, cinnamon-cloves powder, and 1 tablespoon of oil to knead a dough.
Press the sev into hot oil using a perforated ladle (jhara) or a sev maker (sancha).
304.note: If a certain variety of potatoes causes the sev to turn dark, add 1/2 teaspoon of citric acid crystals (limbu na phool).

steps: First, mix both the flours well and add salt, pepper powder, and oil to mix thoroughly.
Now, gradually add water to knead a soft dough and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Next, heat the appropriate amount of oil and press the sev into it using a sev maker or a perforated ladle.
Stir the sev gently so that it does not form lumps.
First, chop the tomatoes, put them in a mixer jar, and grind them into a paste.
Then, take besan in a bowl, add salt, chilli powder, and garam masala, and sift it through a sieve.
Add the tomato paste to it and mix well.
Next, add five teaspoons of oil and knead the dough, adding water if necessary.
Now, heat oil in a kadhai and start pressing out the sev using the machine.
First, sift the flour well, then add salt, oil, and turmeric to prepare the flour mixture.
Then, add a little water at a time to knead the dough.
Now, heat oil in a kadhai and press the sev into it using the machine with a sev disc.
Both thick and thin sev can be made from this dough.
First, mix cinnamon, cloves, pepper, cumin, and star anise and roast them on low flame.
Then, turn off the gas, add chilli seeds, and crush them in a mixer.
Add garam masala, black salt, salt, and dry ginger powder to it and sift well.
Take water in a bowl, add 2 teaspoons of oil, and mix both.
Then, add about 6 teaspoons of the prepared Ratlami masala to it and mix well.
After that, add salt, keep adding besan little by little while stirring, and prepare the dough properly.
Then add a little oil to soften the dough.
Put the dough in the sev machine and fry the sev on low heat until it turns light golden brown.

ing: ajwain (carom seeds), black pepper - to taste
steps: Wash the spinach leaves and grind them in a mixer with a little water.
Then, add the ground spinach, red chilli powder, ground ajwain (carom seeds), and pepper to the gram flour (besan).
Next, add baking soda, lemon, sugar, and salt, and knead a dough slightly softer than bhakri dough.
Heat oil in a kadhai on the gas. Fill the dough in the sev press and press the sev on medium flame.
After all the sev is made, sprinkle black salt (sanchal) over the sev.
Add coarsely crushed cumin seeds and salt to taste in maida (all-purpose flour), now add a little less than half a cup of melted ghee and mix it lightly with your hands.
Add little by little curd and knead the dough lightly with your hands.
Cover and keep it aside for 30 minutes, then knead it lightly.
Make small dough balls, press them with your hands to shape them like a puri.
Fry them on low heat while stirring continuously, remove them from the oil once they turn pink.
315.note: If you want to make sweet dahithra, add powdered sugar to taste while kneading the dough.

steps: First of all, sieve maida (all-purpose flour) in a bowl.
Add ghee moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) to it and mix well.
Add sugar to water and heat until it dissolves, then let the water cool and use it to knead the dough.
Soak sesame seeds for 10 minutes, drain them, let them dry slightly and then coarsely crush them.
Add sesame seeds and sugar water to knead a stiff dough.
Then make equal sized dough balls and roll out thin puris.
Now let them dry for a little while and then fry them in hot oil and serve.
First take the dry flour in a cotton cloth and tie it into a bundle.
Now take some water in a cooker and place a ring inside (place the flour bundle such that it remains above the water level).
Place the flour bundle on it and steam the dry flour until 3 whistles.
Now take out the flour, add all the spices, curd and water as required and knead the dough.
Then put the dough into the chakri maker and make round chakris on a paper.
Heat oil in a kadhai, gently place the chakri in it and fry on low flame.
317.note: Take very fine flour so that the chakri will not break and will not absorb oil. If you feel it absorbs more oil, add 2 tablespoons of maida. Make sure water does not enter the flour bundle. Take out the steamed flour and sieve it first so that if there are any lumps, they are removed by sieving.

steps: Sieve urad dal flour and gram flour (besan).

Add turmeric, red chilli powder, salt, sesame seeds, powdered sugar, pepper powder, coriander-cumin powder, lemon juice, oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) and fennel seeds to it and mix well.
Now add water little by little to knead a dough like paratha.
Now take some water in a bowl, add soda to it, dissolve it, add it to the dough and knead the dough.
Now heat oil and drop tumtum using a tumtum perforated ladle.
Fry the tumtum on medium heat.
First you have to make the dough, for that mix maida (all-purpose flour), wheat flour and besan flour.
Add salt to taste and oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) to it, keep adding plain water and knead a dough like paratha.
Now you have to make the stuffing, for which first make ginger and chilli paste.
Then grind sugar, grated dry coconut and fennel seeds in a mixer and keep in a separate bowl.
Now roast poppy seeds, sesame seeds and peanuts slightly, then grind them separately and keep aside.
Now mix the ground peanuts, poppy seeds, sesame seeds, sugar, coconut and fennel seeds well.
Add red chilli powder, turmeric, garam masala, salt to taste, ginger-chilli paste to it and mix well.
Then finally add lemon juice to it and if needed add water and mix well and taste it.
Now roll the prepared dough like a big roti and apply sugar water on top of it.
Then apply the prepared stuffing well on this roti, do not apply on the edges.
Then you have to roll it.
Once rolled properly, cut it into proportionate pieces and fry them in hot oil.

ing: Oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) – 150 g
steps: In a vessel, slightly heat the oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) on medium heat.
Now take this oil in another vessel, add an equal amount of water to it, and mix well for 2-3 minutes.
Now add a little salt, ajwain (carom seeds), and soda to it and stir.
Then gradually add besan to it and knead a dough like roti dough, then knead it for 4-5 minutes.
Then make round portions of the dough, press them slightly, and make oval shapes.
Now apply pressure with your palm on a rolling board or flat surface to make long strips of the dough.
Carefully lift this thin strip from the board using a knife.
Now fry that strip in hot oil on very low heat.

ing: Oil – 100 g (for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour))
steps: In a vessel, take 100 g oil, salt, soda, and 1 cup water, and whisk with your hands.
Whisk until the mixture turns white.
Then add besan and water as required to knead a dough softer than paratha dough.
Keep the dough covered by sprinkling a little water.
Put oil to heat in a kadhai.
Until the oil gets hot, take a portion of the dough, wet your hands with water, and knead the dough very well until the color of the dough changes.
Now take the dough in your palm, place it on the fafdi perforated spatula (jhara), and rub it to make fafdi.
The spatula should be kept one to two inches above the oil, so take the oil accordingly.
Make all the fafdi on low flame.

ing: Citric acid crystals (limbu na fool) – 1 tsp
steps: Take curd, baking soda, and oil in a vessel and whisk very well.
Add gram flour (besan) to it, along with pepper, coriander, garam masala, chili, turmeric, sesame seeds, sugar, semolina (rava), and citric acid crystals.
Add a little water to keep the dough soft enough to be rubbed over a perforated spatula (jhara).
Let it soak for 2-3 hours.
Now heat boiling hot oil in a vessel, take some of that oil, add it to the soaked dough, and whisk very well.
Place the phulvadi spatula (jhara) over the oil, press the dough with your hand, and make phulvadi this way.
First sift both flours and add all the spices to them.
Finely crush and add sesame seeds and ajwain.
Dissolve papad khar in warm lukewarm water and add it.
Add water little by little using warm lukewarm water to knead a stiff dough.
Then pound the dough properly for 5-7 minutes using a pestle (dasta).
Pull and stretch the dough to make it long, do this 3-4 times.
Make a thin roll and cut out portions using a knife.
Then add a little math flour to a little oil, mix it, and roll the dough portions in it.
Then roll out thin mathiya and fry them in oil over a gas stove.
323.note: White pepper powder can also be used instead of green chilli paste.

steps: First, mix all the above spices into the maida (all-purpose flour) and knead a stiff dough like paratha.
Now mix one spoon of maida (all-purpose flour) and one spoon of oil to make a paste.
Then roll out a large roti, apply the paste on it, roll it up, and make small portions from it.
Now roll out these portions to the size of a single puri.
So that small cracks will form in the puri automatically and you won't need to make them separately with a knife.
Now fry the puris on medium heat.
324.note: If cracks do not form in the puri, the puri will puff up. Instead of only maida, you can also take 400 g roti flour, 200 g maida, 100 g rava like this. About 125 pieces of puris will be made from 1 kg of flour.

steps: First, soak the peanuts in 1/2 glass of water for 5 minutes.
Now, in a bowl, mix the gram flour and all the spices well.
Do not add any water to this mixture.
After five minutes, strain the peanuts using a strainer and transfer them to a wide bowl.
Now, add 3 to 4 spoons of the flour-spice mixture and mix gently with your hands.
Since the peanuts are wet, the flour will stick to them.
Add a little more flour again and mix gently.
Leaving it for a little while will make it dry.
Then pour 2 to 3 spoons of water over the peanuts.
Now again add 2 to 3 spoons of flour on top and mix gently.
Let it rest like that for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add 2 to 3 spoons of flour again and mix.
Now all the peanuts will start separating and will get a nice coating of flour.
If you feel the need, you can add a little more flour.
Now heat oil in a kadhai (pan).
The spiced peanuts must be fried on medium heat.
Now put the prepared peanuts into the oil.
Initially, all the peanuts will be clumped together, but as they fry, they will separate and start floating to the top.
There is no need to stir until they are fried and float to the top.
After frying, take them out on a dish and sprinkle the top sprinkling masala over them.
Fry all the peanuts in this manner.
325.note: Spiced peanuts should be fried on medium heat. Keeping the spiced peanuts in an airtight container keeps them good for 20 to 25 days.

steps: First, add all the given spices to the flour and mix well.
Add ghee moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour), knead a stiff dough, and knead/massage it very well.
After kneading the dough, let it rest for 20-25 minutes and knead it again.
Then roll out a large roti and cut shakkarpare out of it.
Now drop them into the oil, fry them on low heat first, and once 50% fried, fry on full flame.

ing: For ghee moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) – 4 spoons
For oil moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) – 4 spoons
steps: First, warm the water or milk and dissolve the sugar in it.
Now combine both flours, add moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) of both ghee and oil along with cardamom, and mix well.
Now add the warmed water or milk, knead a dough like paratha dough, and knead it very well.
Let it rest for a short while, then roll out a roti thicker than normal and cut into shakkarpare.
Now after putting the shakkarpare in oil, fry them first on low heat and after 50% fried, fry on full flame until they turn light brown.
327.note: Mon can be made with pure ghee alone. Pure ghee can also be used exclusively for frying.

steps: First, mix gram flour and rice flour in a deep bowl.
Now mix all the spices and baking soda into it as well.
Now add a little water to prepare a medium-thick batter.
Keep adding water as needed.
Whisk it continuously for a while so that there are no lumps in it.
Whisk until the color of the batter becomes somewhat whitish.
Now heat oil in a kadhai (pan).
As the oil gets hot, pour the batter over a perforated ladle (jhara) on medium heat to make bundi.
Fry until crisp and golden.
Thus, hot and spicy bundi is ready.
First, knead a dough in a bowl by adding all-purpose flour, salt, baking powder, baking soda, and warm water.
Knead the dough for a little while to make it completely smooth.
Now divide this dough into three equal parts.
Heat 45 ml ghee and 60 ml water in a pan.
Now break one portion of the dough into small pieces and add them to the pan.
Stir it until everything is mixed well.
Now let it cool down.
Then add it to the remaining dough and mix both flours nicely.
Now make small balls out of it, flatten them with your palms, and make a hole in them using your finger.
Now heat oil in a kadhai (pan).
Khajli must be fried on very low heat, otherwise it will remain raw from the inside.
Once it turns golden brown, take it out onto a dish.
Let it cool down, meanwhile mix all the spices and sprinkle them over the prepared khajli and serve.
First wash the chickpeas and soak them for seven hours.
Then boil them in a cooker for one whistle.
After that, wash them with water and dry the chickpeas.
Then take them one by one on a plate and press them to flatten.
Then place them separately on a plate and dry them in the sun or under a fan's breeze.
Then the next day, heat oil and fry them in it.
To make the masala, mix all the spices given in the ingredients.
Sprinkle the masala on the fried chickpeas and mix well.
330.note: They will become crispy only if fried on low heat, otherwise they will remain raw from the inside.

steps: First take besan and soybean flour in a bowl.
Add red chilli powder, pepper powder, turmeric, ajwain (carom seeds), cumin, coriander-cumin powder to it.
Now add baking soda, 4 tablespoons of oil and salt to taste, and mix well.
Now add water little by little and knead a soft dough.
Keep covered for 15-20 minutes.
Then apply oil on your hands and knead it a little.
Heat oil in a kadhai.
Now take the machine, attach the star design disc, fill it with dough, grease a plate with oil and press out the soya sticks.
Once the oil is hot, add the soya sticks and fry on medium heat.
Remove when they turn golden brown.
Thus the soya sticks are ready.
First put oil to heat in a vessel.
After the oil is hot, add turmeric, salt and red chilli powder and mix.
Now turn off the gas, take the vessel down, add mamra and mix with the spices.
Then add sev and mix everything well.
Mix such that the red chilli color should come properly on the mamra.
Sev mamra is ready.
332.note: Do not turn off the gas after adding spices otherwise the spices will burn. You can add sugar, amchur powder etc. according to your taste. If you like it spicy, you can also add more red chilli.

steps: Put all the dough ingredients in a bowl, and knead the dough well.
Let the dough stay in the bowl for 30 minutes.
After kneading the dough, prepare the topping.
Boil water in a vessel then add baking soda to it, dissolve until the soda dissolves completely.
Set the mixture aside for the water to become lukewarm.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Take a baking tray and grease it with oil.
Place the kneaded dough on a slightly oiled surface and divide into 6 equal pieces.
Roll the 6 pieces of dough into 30cm to 38cm rolls.
Cut each roll into about 12 equal pieces.
Place all the pieces in a large plate and pour the cooled baking soda water over it.
Gently move the pieces around so the mixture coats all sides.
Let the pieces stay in the plate for a few minutes.
Place the pieces on the oiled baking tray and sprinkle whole or coarse salt on top.
Bake the pieces for 12 to 15 minutes or until light brown in color.
Now take the tray out of the oven, apply melted ghee on top of the pieces and sprinkle a little salt.
Put the pieces to cool down.
Now your pretzel bites are ready to eat.
333.note: If you are not going to eat the pretzel bites immediately, cover them in a container and keep outside (do not put in the fridge). Whenever you want to eat the pretzel bites again, eat them after warming slightly. You can eat pretzel bites with melted cheese or eat the pieces by themselves. Use yeast in larger quantity in winter and lesser quantity in summer for the dough. Keep the dough soft between spring and autumn.

steps: First take 1 big spoon of rajgira in a kadhai and heat it.
Put rajgira in the kadhai and keep moving it with a cloth.
As the dhani (popped grains) starts popping, pop the remaining dhani similarly.
334.note: First take 1 big spoon of rajgira in a kadhai and heat it. Put rajgira in the kadhai and keep moving it with a cloth. As the dhani starts popping, pop the remaining dhani similarly.

steps: First, place a cooker on the gas stove to heat it, then add oil to it.
Once the oil is hot, add the corn kernels along with turmeric powder and salt.
Mix well, remove the gasket (rubber ring) and whistle from the cooker lid, and close it; the popcorn will start popping.
Turn off the gas, open the lid after a short while, the dhani is ready.
First, heat an aluminum vessel thoroughly on the stove.
Then add the jowar kernels and keep stirring them using a cotton cloth.
Once about 50% of the grains have popped, lower the flame, and as more start to pop, keep covering the vessel with a cotton cloth.
Keep lifting and stirring at brief intervals; after all the grains have popped, keep the cotton cloth covered for 3 minutes.
First, take one and a half cups of flour, add oil and salt to it, and knead the dough by adding water little by little while continuing to knead.
Knead it firmly with your fists for two to three minutes.
Then add one teaspoon of oil, knead again, and let it rest covered for ten minutes.
Then knead a little bit again, make equal-sized dough balls, roll out a round roti, and roast it on a preheated tawa (griddle).
Now, keep the gas low to roast the roti on one side and let very few light spots appear.
When flipping to the other side, increase the gas flame and roast that side properly.
Now flip it back to the first side and roast that part properly as well.
Afterward, apply ghee nicely.
337.note: Salt or oil can be added while kneading the dough; take special care that the dough is neither too hard nor completely soft.

ing: Oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) - approximate
steps: First, take the flour, add oil and salt to it, and knead the dough by adding water little by little while continuing to knead.
Knead it firmly with your fists for two to three minutes.
Then add one teaspoon of oil, knead again, and let it rest covered for ten minutes.
Then knead a little bit again, make equal-sized dough balls, roll out a round roti, and roast it on a preheated tawa.
Now, keep the gas low to roast the roti on one side and let very few light spots appear (roast it semi-cooked).
When flipping to the other side, increase the gas flame and roast that side properly.
Now, take the side that is less cooked and place it directly on the burner flame so it puffs up like a ball.
Afterward, apply ghee nicely.

ing: Oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) - approximate
steps: First, add oil and salt to the flour and mix well, then add water as needed to knead a medium-soft dough.
After kneading the dough, make small dough balls out of it after 10-15 minutes.
Then take two medium dough balls and roll both of them out to the size of a puri.
Apply oil and flour to them, join both sides that have oil and flour applied, press gently with light hands, and roll out a thin roti.
Then roast the roti, separate the layers, and apply ghee on both sides.
339.note: You can also flatten the dough balls by hand, apply ghee and flour, and roll them out.

steps: First, take 500 grams of flour in a bowl, add salt, 50 grams of oil, and water as required to knead a dough like a roti.
Cover and let the dough rest for a short while.
Now divide it into five parts and make round dough balls of all of them.
Take one dough ball on the rolling board and roll it into a roti.
Now apply oil on that roti and properly dust dry roti flour over it.
Then fold it from the middle, it will form a semi-circular shape.
Again apply oil and dry flour on the top side and fold it in half once more.
Now fold its edges and make a round dough ball again.
Then gently roll it to make a round roti.
Now roast it on a tawa or griddle on both sides.
After it is roasted, apply ghee on it and serve.
340.note: Satpadi roti turns out better on a tawa. It stays soft even if kept for a long time.

ing: Oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) – 100 grams
steps: Add oil, salt, turmeric, and chilli to the flour.
Add enough water to knead a soft dough like plain roti.
Make equal-sized dough balls, roll out the roti, roast it on the griddle, and then apply ghee to it.
Mix both flours in a bowl, add water and salt, and knead the dough.
Knead the dough very well, take a large dough ball, and using dry flour, roll it like a roti or pat it gently by hand to make a roti.
Then roast it on a non-stick griddle, puff it up on the gas stove, and then apply ghee on top.
342.note: Use wheat flour only if the roti does not form properly, otherwise not. The roti will only form if the bajra flour is fresh, otherwise it will not.

steps: Take maida (all-purpose flour) and salt in a bowl and mix, then add milk and water to knead the dough.
Knead the dough very well, make it sticky, then cover it with a damp cotton cloth and let it rest for 10 to 15 minutes.
Then add ghee and water and knead again, until it becomes smooth.
Then cover it with a damp cotton cloth and set it aside for 1-2 hours.
Next, place a kadhai upside down on the gas and let it heat.
Take a dough ball from the dough and roll a thin roti, using dry flour if needed.
Now mix salt and half a cup of water and sprinkle it on the tawa so that the roti does not stick to the tawa.
Now roast the rolled roti.
Once the roti is roasted, apply ghee to it and serve.
First, heat water in a vessel, add ghee and salt to it, and bring it to a boil.
After a while, slowly add the flour to it, mix and stir, and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Then take the dough out, and when it is slightly cool, knead the dough very well, then cover the dough with a damp cloth.
Then roll out the roti like a regular roti.
When roasting the roti on the tawa, run a wet hand with water over one side so that cracks do not form.
Roast it while pressing with a cotton cloth.
Then apply ghee nicely on the roti.
First, take maida (all-purpose flour), baking powder, baking soda, salt, curd, and lukewarm water as needed in a bowl to knead the dough.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes.
Then cover the dough with a cloth and set it aside for 2 hours.
After 2 hours, knead the dough a little and make small dough balls.
Then take a dough ball, add some sesame seeds and fresh coriander leaves to it, and roll it into an oval shape.
Then heat a tawa (griddle), take the kulcha in your hand, apply water on one side, and stick it onto the tawa.
After a little while, when it is cooked, flip the tawa upside down and roast it directly over the flame.
Roast the kulcha on both sides in this manner.
Then apply butter on top of it.
In a bowl, mix wheat flour, salt, baking soda, curd, and water as needed to knead the dough.
Then add oil, knead for a little while, and keep it covered with a cotton cloth for 10 to 15 minutes.
Then take a dough ball and roll out a thick roti.
Next, sprinkle water on the tawa and place the roti on it.
Cook it until both sides are roasted, then apply ghee on the roti and serve.
346.note: Tandoori roti is traditionally made in a tandoor.

ing: oil - 4 spoons (for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour))
steps: First, take wheat flour, gram flour (besan), kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), ajwain (carom seeds), turmeric, salt, and oil in a bowl, and knead a soft dough like roti.
Knead the dough, cover and let it rest for 10 to 15 minutes, then take a portion from the dough and roll out a roti.
Then cook the roti on a tawa, and after it is roasted, apply ghee on top and serve.

ing: bajra rotla (pearl millet flatbreads) - 2 pcs (from yesterday evening)
steps: First, crumble the rotlas to a medium consistency in a bowl.
Then add ghee and jaggery to it and mix well.
Khurmo is ready; serve it with rice papad.
Take wheat flour, add salt and oil to it, and gradually add water to knead the dough.
Make small balls from that dough to make rotis, and apply one small spoon of ghee on each roti.
After applying ghee, sprinkle powdered sugar or jaggery on top according to taste.
After adding ghee and sugar or jaggery, roll the roti to make papuda.
Take pearl millet (bajra) flour in a vessel, add salt, and adding little by little water,
knead a dough that is neither too soft nor too hard, and knead the dough very well.
The more you knead the dough, the better the flatbread turns out.
Make a dough ball, pat it between both palms without applying too much pressure, and slowly enlarge it only from the edges.
Heat an earthenware griddle properly, place the flatbread on it, and roast it well on both sides.
Apply ghee once it is cooked.
353.note: If you do not know how to shape the flatbread by hand, you can also make it by placing a smooth paper on a rolling board.

steps: Take sifted maize flour in a vessel, add salt and wheat flour, and gradually add water to knead a dough that is neither too soft nor too stiff; knead the dough very thoroughly, as the more it is kneaded, the better the rotla turns out.
Make a portion of dough and pat it between both palms, taking care not to apply too much pressure, gradually flattening and expanding it along the edges.
Heat a clay griddle (tavdi) properly, place the rotla on it, and roast it well on both sides.
Once it is cooked through, apply ghee on top.
355.note: If you do not know how to flatten the rotla by hand, it can also be shaped by placing a smooth paper or plastic sheet on a rolling board.

steps: Take coarse wheat flour in a vessel, add turmeric powder, salt, red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, whole cumin seeds, sesame seeds, and oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour), and knead a stiff dough.
Take a large dough ball, roll it into a slightly thick bhakhri, place it on a well-heated griddle (lodhi), apply oil on both sides, and press and roast/fry it so that the bhakhri becomes crispy.
If you want to roast the bhakhri without frying, cook it on both sides on a flat pan (tavadi).
Then apply ghee and serve hot.

First, take wheat flour in a wide pan (kathrot), add fenugreek leaves, fresh coriander leaves, ginger-chilli paste, ajwain (carom seeds), sesame seeds, salt, and oil/ghee for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour).
Then mix everything well and knead a stiff dough.
Take a large dough ball and roll it into a slightly thick bhakhri.
Once the griddle (lodhi) is properly heated, place the bhakhri on it, apply oil on both sides, and press and fry it so that the bhakhri becomes crispy.
If you want to roast the bhakhri, cook it on both sides on a flat pan (tavadi).
Then apply ghee and serve hot.
358.note: Coarse wheat flour can also be used for this.

steps: First, take wheat flour in a wide pan (kathrot), add almond powder, milk, oil, and salt, and mix well.
Then add water as needed and knead a stiff dough.
Take a large dough ball and roll it into a slightly thick and small-sized bhakhri.
Place the griddle on the gas stove, let it heat well, then put the bhakhri on it, apply oil on both sides, and press and fry it so that the bhakhri becomes crispy.
359.note: By adding ajwain, coriander-cumin powder, and red chilli powder to it, Masala Badam Bhakhri can be made.

ing: oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) – 4 ladles / tablespoons
steps: First, take wheat flour and semolina (rava) in a vessel, add oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour), salt, and coriander-cumin powder, and mix well.
Then, adding water little by little, knead a dough that is stiffer than regular rotli dough.
Then cover it and let it rest for 10 minutes.
After 10 minutes, make small dough balls and roll out puris.
Then heat oil in a kadai (pan) and fry the puris.
360.note: Do not let the rolled puris dry out, otherwise they will not puff up.

ing: oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) – 50 grams
steps: First, take wheat flour in a vessel, add sesame seeds, and add oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour).
Then heat water to dissolve the jaggery in it.
Once the jaggery dissolves, use that jaggery water to knead the dough.
Then make small dough balls and roll out small-sized puris.
Now place a kadai (pan) with oil, let it heat, and then fry the puris.
361.note: Sugar can also be used in place of jaggery.

ing: oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) – 50 grams
steps: Take maida (all-purpose flour) in a vessel, make a small well in the center and add baking soda, salt, sugar, curd and oil for moyan, then mix very well.
Afterwards, knead the dough using warm water.
Make the dough soft, such that it is neither too loose nor too hard.
Once the dough is kneaded, apply a little oil with your hands on top and cover it in a warm place for two hours.
Then take dry flour on your hands, knead the kneaded dough and then make dough balls.
Next, dust with dry flour and roll out oval-shaped bhatura.
Put oil to heat in a kadhai, and when the oil becomes hot, fry the bhatura one by one.
362.note: Half wheat flour can also be taken instead of maida.

ing: oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) – 1 tablespoon
steps: Take flour in a vessel.
Mix grated potatoes, salt and red chilli into it.
Mix oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour), coriander, cumin, ginger chilli and turmeric.
Then keep adding water and knead a very smooth dough.
Then make small dough balls and roll out puris.
Now put oil to heat in a kadhai.
When the oil gets hot, fry the aloo puris.

ing: oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) – 2 tablespoons
steps: First of all, take wheat flour in a vessel.
Grind spinach and ginger-chilli in a mixer.
Mix that spinach paste into the flour along with salt and oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour).
Then add water and knead a very smooth dough.
Cover and let the dough rest for 15 minutes.
After 15 minutes, apply a little oil to your hands and knead thoroughly.
Then make small dough balls and roll out puris.
Put oil to heat in a kadhai.
When the oil gets hot, fry the puris.
364.note: Spinach can be boiled in hot water to make the paste.

steps: First of all, take semolina (rava) in a vessel.
Then add curd.
Add ajwain (carom seeds) and salt to it.
Then add water to it and knead a soft dough.
Cover and let it rest for 10 minutes.
After 10 minutes, apply a little oil to your hands and knead the dough.
Then make small dough balls and roll out puris.
Put oil to heat in a kadhai.
Then fry the puris one by one.
Add red chilli powder, turmeric, cumin, salt, fresh coriander leaves and oil to wheat flour and mix everything well.
Knead a soft dough of proper consistency with the help of water and let it rest for 15 minutes.
Now put oil to heat in a kadhai, then fry the puris in it.
On the side, make proper-sized dough balls, roll them into round and appropriately thick puris, and fry them in oil until they turn slightly golden brown.

ing: warm water – for kneading the dough
steps: Mix the rajgira flour and moraiya flour together, add salt, rub in the ghee for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour), mix well, and knead into a dough using lukewarm water.
Let it rest for 10 minutes, then make small-sized dough balls, roll them into puris, and fry them in hot oil.
367.note: Adding boiled potatoes makes it easier to handle the dough and make the puris, and prevents them from cracking while rolling.

ing: oil – for cooking / roasting the pudla
steps: Boil the corn kernels in a cooker for 2-3 whistles, then coarsely crush them and mix into the gram flour (besan). Add tomatoes, capsicum, green chillies, fresh coriander leaves, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and salt, mix everything well, add water, and make a batter of medium consistency.

Grease a non-stick pan with 2-3 teaspoons of oil. Once the pan is hot, spread a ladleful of the batter, drizzle oil around the edges, and let it cook for 1-2 minutes. Then flip it and cook the other side for 1-2 minutes.
The pudlas are now ready. These corn pudlas can be served with tomato sauce.
Take the jaggery in a vessel and dissolve it completely in 2-3 cups of water.
Then add the wheat flour to the water and mix everything thoroughly.
If needed, add more water to bring the batter to the right pouring consistency.
Next, heat a non-stick pan, apply oil at the bottom, and spread the batter over it.
Drizzle oil around the edges of the pudla and let it cook for 1-2 minutes.
Then flip it and cook the other side for 1-2 minutes. The pudlas are ready to be served now.
369.note: The amount of jaggery can be adjusted according to taste. Roasting the pudlas in ghee instead of oil will enhance the taste.

steps: In a bowl, combine gram flour (besan), turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, red chilli powder, green chillies, ginger paste, salt, fresh coriander leaves, and water as required. Mix everything well to make a batter of medium consistency.
Heat a non-stick pan, grease it with 1 spoon of oil, and spread the batter evenly over it.
After a little while, once one side is cooked, flip it and cook the other side. The pudla is ready.
370.note: Add 2 spoons of hot oil to the batter.

steps: Soak the moong dal in water for 2-3 hours, then grind it into a coarse paste.
Then add turmeric powder, ginger-chilli paste, fresh coriander leaves, and salt to taste into the paste, and mix everything well.
Then add water as needed to make a batter of the right consistency for making pudlas.

Now place a non-stick pan on the gas, apply 2-3 spoons of oil on it, spread the batter, and let it cook for 1-2 minutes. Add oil around the edges if needed, then flip and cook/roast the other side for 1-2 minutes.

In a bowl, add gram flour (besan), rice flour, 5 tomatoes gravy, turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, red chilli powder, chaat masala, green chillies, salt, fresh coriander leaves and a little water.
Mix everything well to make a batter of pouring consistency.
Now spread 2 tsp of oil in a non-stick pan and pour a ladleful of batter to make pudla.
Drizzle oil around the edges and once one side is cooked, flip and roast the other side.
Thus, pudla are ready and can be served with sauce.
To make dudhi thepla, first mix all the ingredients given above and knead into a dough.
Use water only if needed because moisture from dudhi will help knead the dough.
Once the dough is ready, add 1/4 tsp of oil and knead it smooth.
Make small dough balls and roll out into theplas.
Heat a tawa (griddle) and roast the theplas using oil until golden brown on both sides.

ing: chopped fresh fenugreek leaves (methi) – ¾ cup
steps: First, to make methi thepla, mix all the given ingredients and knead a dough.
Add water little by little while kneading the dough.
Once the dough is ready, add 1/4 tsp of oil and knead it smooth.
Make small dough balls and roll out the theplas.
Then heat a tawa and roast the rolled theplas on both sides with oil until golden brown.
First, to make plain thepla, mix all the given ingredients and knead a dough.
Once the dough is ready, add 1/4 tsp of oil and knead it smooth.
Then make dough balls and roll out the theplas.
Heat a tawa and roast the theplas on both sides with oil until golden brown.
Mix salt and oil (2 tablespoons) in wheat flour, add water gradually to knead a medium-soft dough, knead well for 2-3 minutes and set aside for 20-25 minutes.
Meanwhile, to prepare the stuffing, heat oil in a non-stick pan, add cumin seeds and when they turn slightly brown, add coriander-cumin powder and ginger-chilli paste.
Then add spinach, salt, red chilli powder, amchur (dry mango powder) powder and cabbage, and sauté everything well for 2-3 minutes.
Next, add mashed boiled potatoes, mix everything well, add fresh coriander leaves, mix well and turn off the gas.
Now take portions of the prepared dough, roll them into 3-4 inch rotis, apply a little oil, fill with the prepared stuffing, seal the edges and roll out into a round paratha.
Now cook the paratha on a tawa using oil on both sides just like a paratha.
The parathas are ready and can be served with curd or sauce.
First, mix ghee, salt, and water in the wheat flour, knead into a moderately soft dough, and let it rest for 20-25 minutes.
Next, heat a non-stick pan.
Now, make dough balls from the prepared dough, roll them into a triangular shape, and roast them on both sides in the pan using oil.
The parathas are ready; they can be served with fried chilies, potato bhaji, pav bhaji sabzi, or Punjabi sabzi.

ing: oil - for kneading the dough and for roasting
steps: First, mix the wheat flour and maida (all-purpose flour), add salt and 2 tablespoons of oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour).
Mix everything well, knead into a moderately soft dough using lukewarm water, and set it aside to rest for 25-30 minutes.
Once the dough is set, make medium-sized balls, roll them into a thin, even roti, apply butter on it, and fold two edges of the roti towards the center (up to the middle).
Now its shape will look rectangular; spread grated cheese over it.
Next, fold the remaining two edges in a way that covers the cheese, and press all the edges down with your fingers to seal them; now it will look square in shape.
Now, gently roll this square-shaped paratha a little thick using a rolling pin.
Then, place it on a non-stick pan with a little oil at the bottom, add a little oil around the edges, and roast it on both sides.

ing: oil - for roasting and kneading the dough
steps: First, add ajwain (carom seeds), grated cabbage, red chilli powder, garam masala, salt, and 2 teaspoons of oil to the wheat flour, adding water as needed to knead into a moderately soft dough.
Cover it and let it set for 10-15 minutes.
Then make dough balls, roll out the parathas, and roast them on both sides with oil on a non-stick pan.
The parathas are ready and can be served with sauce, green chutney, or sweet chutney.
Add salt and 1 teaspoon of oil to the wheat flour, knead into a moderately soft dough using water, and set aside to rest for 20-25 minutes.

Mash the boiled potatoes by hand and mix in a little salt, red chilli powder, green chillies, coriander-cumin powder, amchur (dry mango powder) powder, ginger paste, fresh coriander leaves, and garam masala, mixing everything well.
Now, grease the set dough, knead it smoothly, make balls, and roll out a slightly thick roti.
Then, place a portion of the prepared potato mawa (khoya) in it, seal the roti from all sides to form a ball again, and roll it out into a round paratha.
Now, heat a non-stick pan, grease it with oil, and roast the paratha on both sides by adding oil. The parathas are ready; they can be served with sauce or any chutney.
380.note: After filling the stuffing, seal the roti properly and roll the paratha very gently, otherwise the paratha will tear.

steps: Add milk, sugar, and salt to the wheat flour, add water as needed, and knead into a moderately soft dough.
Then apply oil and let it rest for 10-15 minutes.
Then make medium-sized balls, take two balls, apply oil on one side of both, sprinkle flour, join the balls together, and roll out a double-layered roti.
Then apply oil on the roti again, sprinkle flour, and fold it into a square shape.
Then roll it out into a square paratha.
Then roast that square paratha in a non-stick pan on both sides using butter.
The parathas are ready and can be served with pav bhaji or Punjabi sabzi.

ing: ghee – 1 tablespoon for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour)
ghee – for rolling and cooking the parathas
steps: Add salt, gram flour (besan), and ghee for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour) to the wheat flour, mix everything well, knead a soft dough of appropriate consistency, and set it aside.
Take a kadhai, add green peas and a little water, and put them to boil.
Now add a little salt and sugar to it so that the color of the peas does not change.
Once the water evaporates, wash the peas with plain water, drain them, and spread them out on a cloth.
Once dried, fold the cloth from both sides and roll a rolling pin over it to coarsely crush them.

Then take those coarsely crushed peas in a bowl, add a little salt, black pepper, red chilli powder, garam masala, amchur (dry mango powder), green chillies, coriander powder, ajwain (carom seeds), and fresh coriander leaves, and mix everything well.
Make portions of the dough of equal size, roll out half a roti, apply ghee on it, dust some flour, and make a small-sized ball from the pea stuffing.
Place it on top of that roti, pack it, make a dough ball again, and roll it out into a round shape.
Cook the paratha on both sides on a non-stick pan using ghee.
The parathas are ready and can be served with sauce or chutney.

ing: oil – for cooking and for the dough
steps: Mix gram flour (besan) into the wheat flour, add ginger paste, red chilli powder, ajwain (carom seeds), salt, and oil, and mix everything well.
Then coarsely crush or chop the cleaned fenugreek leaves, add them to the flour, knead a soft dough of appropriate consistency using water, and apply oil on top of it.
Now make portions of the dough, roll them into a round shape, fold them twice to make a triangular shape, and roll it into a triangle again, sprinkling oil and flour while folding.
Now heat a non-stick pan, apply oil on it, and cook the paratha on both sides.
The parathas can be served with sauce or chutney.
In a bowl, add wheat flour, salt, 2 tablespoons of ghee, and water as needed, knead a soft dough of appropriate consistency, and let it set for 20-25 minutes.
Now grate the paneer.
Add salt, coriander powder, amchur (dry mango powder), garam masala, green chillies, red chilli powder, and fresh coriander leaves to it, and mix everything well.
Once the dough is set, make portions of it, roll out half a roti, and take a small ball from the prepared paneer stuffing and place it on the roti.
Pack it from all sides, make a dough ball again, and roll it into a round paratha.
Heat a non-stick pan, apply ghee on it, and cook the paratha properly on both sides using ghee.
The parathas are ready, now serve them hot.

ing: oil or ghee – for cooking the parathas
steps: Cut the tomatoes into large pieces, add green chillies, ginger pieces, 2 teaspoons of cumin seeds (jeera), and salt to them, and coarsely crush them in a mixer.
Now take this in a bowl, add wheat flour and fresh coriander leaves, mix everything well, knead a soft dough of appropriate consistency, and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Then make portions of the dough, roll out parathas like roti, and cook them on both sides in a non-stick pan using oil.
386.note: The dough must be kneaded using only the tomato gravy without taking water, and if needed, make more gravy.

steps: In a bowl, add maida (all-purpose flour), semolina (rava), salt, powdered sugar, and butter, mix well, and knead a soft dough of appropriate consistency using water.
Then cover it and keep it aside to set for 10 minutes.
After 10 minutes, make equal portions of the dough and apply oil on them.
Now take one dough ball and roll it into a thin round roti.
Then apply oil on top of it and make thin strips in the roti using a knife.
Then gather those strips and stack them one on top of the other.
Then roll it into a round shape starting from one end to make a dough ball, then gently roll it out with a rolling pin to make a paratha and cook it on the griddle (tava).
If you do not want to cut it with a knife, apply oil to the rolled roti and fold the roti inward and outward in one-inch strips from one side.
By doing this, a long strip of rolled roti with many different layers will be formed at the end.
Now start folding this strip from one end to make a round dough ball again.
Gently roll it out again to make a paratha and cook it on the griddle (tava).
First, put maida (all-purpose flour), sugar, baking powder, and salt in a bowl and mix it.
Then add curd and oil to it, and knead the dough using lukewarm water.
Knead a softer dough than roti, and then take oil and knead it well.
Take a cloth dipped in lukewarm water, squeeze it out, cover the dough with it, place a plate over it, and keep it aside for 2 hours.

Now make a large dough ball from it, dip it in maida (all-purpose flour) and roll it, then put mozzarella cheese and fresh coriander leaves in the middle, seal the roti from all sides to make a ball, and roll it again.
Heat a griddle (lodhi), place this naan on it, and roast it on both sides using oil.
Or else, once the griddle gets hot on the gas, apply water to the naan and put it on the griddle so that it will stick.
Now roast it on one side.
Then invert the griddle and roast the naan directly on the gas flame.
389.note: When stuffing cheese in the naan, chat masala, mixed herbs, and oregano can also be added. Baking soda can be taken instead of baking powder.

steps: First, in a large mixing plate, add maida (all-purpose flour), powdered sugar, baking soda, salt, curd, and oil, and knead into a dough using lukewarm water.
Knead it slightly softer than roti dough and knead it thoroughly.
Cover this dough with a damp cloth, cover with a plate, and let it rest for 2 hours.
Now take butter in a bowl, add fresh coriander leaves to it, and mix well.
After 2 hours, make slightly large dough balls, dip them in dry maida (all-purpose flour), and roll them out; they can be rolled round or oval.
Once the iron tawa heats up on the stove, apply water to one side of the naan and place it on the tawa so that it sticks.
Now roast it on one side.
Then invert the tawa and roast the naan directly over the gas flame.
Once roasted, apply the butter and fresh coriander leaves mixture on top.
First, take small brinjals, remove their stems, make one vertical slit and another slit from the bottom (opposite to the top). Prepare all the brinjals by making these slits.

Now, in a dish, mix crushed peanuts, dry coconut, crushed white sesame seeds, melon seeds and crushed cashews, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, lemon juice, gram flour (besan), salt, sugar or jaggery.
Now heat 5 tablespoons of oil in a pressure cooker.

Then stuff the prepared masala into the brinjals, put those brinjals in the cooker, and if any masala is left over after stuffing, add it to the cooker as well. Close the cooker and whistle for 4 whistles.
Once ready, add fresh coriander leaves and serve hot.
First, chop the brinjals into small pieces.
Now heat oil in a pressure cooker, add cumin seeds, curry leaves, ginger-chilli paste, and tomato pieces, and then add the chopped brinjals and green peas and mix them well.
Next, add red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, turmeric powder, and salt, stir well, add half a glass of water, and let the cooker whistle for one to two whistles.
Then open the cooker and garnish the curry on top with grated dry coconut and fresh coriander leaves.
First, chop the brinjals and potatoes into small pieces and make the ginger-chilli paste.
Now heat oil in a pressure cooker, add cumin seeds, curry leaves, ginger-chilli paste, and tomato pieces, and then add the chopped brinjals and potatoes and mix them well.
Then add red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, turmeric powder, and salt, stir well, add half a glass of water, and let the cooker whistle for one to two whistles.
Open the cooker and garnish the curry on top with grated dry coconut and fresh coriander leaves.
If you prefer potato curry with skin, chop into appropriately sized pieces with the skin on; otherwise, peel them and chop into appropriately sized pieces.
Now put oil in a cooker, and when it gets hot, add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, and ginger-chilli paste.
Then add chopped tomatoes, stir, and then add potatoes and mix well.
Next, add red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, turmeric powder, salt, sugar, garam masala, and lemon juice, and stir well.
Add half a glass of water to it and let the cooker whistle 4 times on low flame.
Now open the cooker and sprinkle fresh coriander leaves on top of the curry.
396.note: It can also be made directly in a deep pan without a pressure cooker.

steps: Boil the potatoes in a cooker until there are 2 whistles.
Then when they cool down, peel them and cut them into medium-sized large pieces.
Then heat oil in a kadhai, add mustard seeds and dry red chillies.
When the mustard seeds crackle, add cumin seeds, and when they turn slightly brown, add curry leaves and green chillies and sauté for a while.
Now add turmeric powder, lemon juice, powdered sugar, salt, and potatoes, mix and stir for a little while, then add fresh coriander leaves on top and mix everything well.

ing: Mustard seeds and cumin seeds – 2 teaspoons
steps: Peel the potatoes, cut them into appropriate-sized pieces, and shell the green peas and keep them ready.
Heat oil in a pan, add mustard seeds and cumin seeds. Once they crackle, add turmeric powder and green chillies, and saute.
Then add chopped tomatoes. Once they are cooked, add the potatoes and green peas.
Now add red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, and sugar, and mix everything well.
Add about 1/2 cup of water and pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Once ready, garnish with fresh coriander leaves on top.
Shell the pigeon peas and keep them ready, and chop the brinjal into small pieces.
Heat oil in a pan, add mustard seeds. Once they crackle, add ginger-chilli paste, then add the brinjal, pigeon pea seeds, and 1 cup of water, and let it cook. Once the curry is cooked,
add fresh coriander leaves on top and serve.

ing: green chillies – 4-5 pcs (cut into large pieces)
steps: Heat oil in a pan, add mustard seeds and cumin seeds. When they turn brown, add green chillies, chopped cabbage, and peas. Once they cook a little, add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, and salt. Mix everything well, cover the pan with a plate, pour a little water on top of the plate, and let it cook for 10 minutes.
Putting water on the covered plate prevents the curry from sticking.
Then, once the curry is cooked, mix in the fresh coriander leaves.
Wash and cut the cauliflower, and keep it immersed in hot water with salt for 3-4 minutes so that any pests or chemicals are removed.
Heat oil in a pan, prepare a tempering of mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and turmeric powder, and add the chopped cauliflower to it.
Now add salt, sugar, red chilli powder, and coriander-cumin powder.
Then cover the pan with a dish, stirring it at regular intervals. After 10-12 minutes, check whether everything is cooked or not, and then turn off the gas.
Wash the cluster beans and chop them into 1-2 inch pieces.
Heat oil in a cooker, add ajwain (carom seeds) and cumin seeds. Once they are roasted, add turmeric powder and then add the chopped cluster beans.
Next, add salt and saute for 3-4 minutes.
Then add red chilli powder and coriander-cumin powder, mix everything well, add 1/2 glass of water, and pressure cook for 3 whistles before turning off the gas.
Open the cooker and mix in the coriander leaves.

Heat oil in a pan, temper with mustard seeds and cumin seeds, then add turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, chopped ridge gourd, and salt, and sauté the ridge gourd while stirring for 3-4 minutes.
Then add red chilli powder and let it cook on low heat.
If needed, add only 1/2 cup of water.
After 10-12 minutes, check the curry. If it is cooked, turn off the gas and garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
Heat oil in a pan, temper with cumin seeds and green chillies, then add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, and salt, and let it cook for 1 minute.
Then add the carrots along with 1/2 cup of water and let it cook on a low flame.
After 10-12 minutes, check the curry. If the carrots are cooked, turn off the gas and garnish with fresh coriander leaves.

ing: green chillies – 12-13 pcs (according to spice preference)
steps: In a mixer, add ginger, cumin seeds, green chillies, ajwain (carom seeds), peanuts, and sesame seeds, crush everything coarsely without water, then add fresh coriander leaves and mint leaves, and grind again to prepare a paste.
Make four slits in the potatoes without cutting them all the way through, cut sweet potatoes into round pieces, and peel and cut the yam into slightly larger pieces.
Now add 1 cup of salt in a cooker, place 1 stand, put a perforated plate on that stand, and close the cooker lid (for preheating).

Take the prepared paste in a bowl, add turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, salt (to taste), garam masala, and peanut oil, mix everything well, and stuff this masala into the slits of the potatoes.
Then, mix the papdi, papdi seeds, sweet potatoes, and yam into the remaining masala, and mix the stuffed potatoes along with all the vegetables.
Now take all this vegetable mixture in a foil paper and pack it properly.
Then place it inside the salt-filled cooker, close the lid without the rubber ring and whistle, and let it steam for 1 hour.
Carefully take out the hot packet, open it, add fresh coriander leaves and lemon juice to the vegetables, and mix everything well.
Trim the ends of the tindora and make a slit, then apply a little salt inside using a knife.
Next, take gram flour (besan) in a pan and roast it on a low flame for about 3-4 minutes.
Add red chilli powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, coriander-cumin powder, sugar, salt, and lemon juice to the gram flour (besan) and mix everything well to make the masala.
Now stuff this masala tightly inside the tindora so that no cavity is left empty.
Heat oil in a pan, add mustard seeds for tempering, add the stuffed tindora, and cover with a lid.
Then stir every 2 minutes. It will take about 10-15 minutes.
Now add any remaining masala to the tindora, cover again, and let it cook for 3-4 minutes.
Boil the green chickpeas in a cooker for up to 1 whistle.
Crush the cumin seeds coarsely in a mortar and pestle.
Crush the green chillies and ginger.
Then heat oil in a non-stick pan, add mustard seeds, crushed cumin seeds, and crushed ginger-chilli, mix well, and sauté for 2-3 minutes, then add turmeric powder and sauté for 1 minute.
Now add red chilli powder, garam masala, coriander-cumin powder, salt, and a little water (about 1/2 glass), and sauté until the oil separates on top.
Then add the boiled chickpeas and let them cook for 3-4 minutes.
Once the curry is cooked, turn off the gas and garnish with fresh coriander leaves.
407.note: Use slightly more oil for tempering than the usual method.

steps: First, slice the parwal a bit thinly so that they cook quickly.
Heat oil in a pan and add mustard and cumin seeds to it.
Then add the ginger-green chilli paste and chopped parwal.
Cover it with a dish and place a little water on top of that dish.
Stir it every 3-4 minutes so that it does not stick to the bottom.
Once it is slightly cooked, add coriander-cumin powder, turmeric, red chilli powder, and salt, stir well, and let it cook.
If you want to add sugar, you can add it.
First, boil the green peas in water, then cut the carrots and potatoes into pieces and chop the tomatoes.
Now take oil for frying in a pan, and once it is hot, fry the carrots in it, then fry the potatoes.
Heat 10 tablespoons of oil in a pan and make a tempering (vaghar) with mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and ginger-green chilli paste.
Then add turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, salt, and garam masala, add the chopped tomatoes, stir, and let it cook for a while.
Then add water and cover it with a dish.
After that, add the potatoes, carrots, and peas and cover the dish again.
After a while, check if the curry is cooked, then turn off the gas, add chopped fresh coriander leaves, and mix well.
Peel the bottle gourd and cut it into small pieces.
Now heat oil in a pressure cooker and add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, dried red chillies, and curry leaves, and stir.
Then add the bottle gourd and tomatoes, along with turmeric, coriander-cumin powder, red chilli powder, garam masala, salt, lemon juice, sugar, and a little water, and mix well.
Close the cooker and after 4 whistles, open the cooker and put fresh coriander leaves on top of the curry.
410.note: Potatoes can also be added to bottle gourd curry.

411.t: Peas and Flower Vegetable Stir Fry
steps: First, cut the cauliflower into medium-sized pieces, shell the peas, and chop the tomatoes.
Soak the cauliflower pieces in salted water for a short while so that any insects in them are removed.
Now take oil in a pan, place it on the gas, and heat the oil.
Then add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, ginger-green chilli paste, and curry leaves, and saute.
Now first add the peas, cover with a dish, and let them cook for 4-5 minutes.
Then add the cauliflower and tomatoes and stir.
Place a dish on top and let it cook.
Put a little water on top of the dish and add a little water to the curry.
When it is almost cooked, add turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, salt, and garam masala, and stir.
Then cover it, turn off the gas after 2-3 minutes, take out the curry, and sprinkle fresh coriander leaves on it.
First, wash the native mango, peel it, cut it into medium-sized pieces, and keep the crushed jaggery ready.
Take oil in a pan, and once it is hot, add dried red chillies, mustard-cumin seeds, curry leaves, kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), and turmeric powder.
Then add the mango pieces, add salt, and let it cook uncovered.
When the mango becomes slightly soft, add the crushed jaggery.
Then add coriander-cumin powder and red chilli powder and stir.
Once the gravy becomes slightly thick, turn off the gas while continuing to stir, and then add fresh coriander leaves.
412.note: If you want more gravy, water can also be added.

steps: First, take the tomatoes in a mixer jar to prepare a puree, then add 50 grams of cashews to it and blend to make a puree.
Now, heat oil in a pan, fry 50 grams of cashews, and take them out in a dish.
Then add cumin seeds, ginger-chilli paste, curry leaves, bay leaves, and dry red chillies to the oil and stir.
Now add the tomato-cashew puree to it.
Then add red chilli powder, Kashmiri chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, salt, sugar, and garam masala, and let it cook.
After 5 minutes, add a little buttermilk, stir, and let it cook.
Now add the fried cashews, then add the ganthia, mix well, and let it cook for 2 minutes.
Now turn off the gas, add fresh coriander leaves, and serve.
413.note: You can also choose not to blend cashews into the puree and just fry all of them and add them.

steps: First, heat the oil.
Once the oil is hot, temper with cumin seeds and turmeric powder.
Then add the broccoli.
Next, add salt, red chilli powder, and coriander-cumin powder.
Mix well and then cover the pan for 10 minutes.
Then add lemon juice and black pepper powder.
Mix well again and garnish with coriander leaves.
Now your broccoli curry is ready.
First, chop the cluster beans and boil them in a cooker for 3 whistles.
Now in a bowl, add gram flour (besan), wheat flour, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, salt, coriander-cumin powder, garam masala, sugar, lemon juice, and 3 tablespoons of oil.
Then add water as needed to knead a dough like roti, then add a little oil and knead it well.
Now take 7 tablespoons of oil in a large pan, add curry leaves and ajwain (carom seeds), stir, add 1 ½ glasses of water, and heat it.
Roll a thick roti and cut it diagonally and vertically with a knife to make dhokli pieces.
Now add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, salt, coriander-cumin powder, garam masala, sugar, and lemon juice to the pan and stir.
After it comes to a good boil, add the dhoklis one by one and cook for 4 minutes.
Then add the boiled cluster beans and cook for 2 minutes.
First, soak the split Bengal gram in warm water for one hour.
Peel the bottle gourd and chop it into small pieces.
Now heat oil in a cooker and temper with mustard seeds, cumin seeds, dry red chillies, and curry leaves.
Then add tomatoes, bottle gourd, and split Bengal gram to it.
Now add turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, red chilli powder, garam masala, salt, lemon juice, sugar, and water, and mix well.
Now close the cooker and let it cook for 4 whistles on low heat.
Then open the cooker and garnish the curry with fresh coriander leaves on top.
First, wash the ridge gourd with water, then peel it and cut it into medium-sized pieces.
Now heat oil in a pan, add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, green chillies, turmeric powder, and salt, then add the ridge gourd and stir.
Cover it; there is no need to add water.
Keep stirring every 3-4 minutes and keep the gas flame medium.
Now add coriander-cumin powder, red chilli powder, and garam masala, mix well, and let it cook uncovered.
Once the curry is cooked, add fresh coriander leaves to it.
417.note: You can also make it by adding potatoes and tomatoes. If you want to make Sev Turia curry, make it the same way and add sev at the end, taking it off the heat after 2 minutes.

steps: Wash the okra (bhinda), wipe them dry with a cloth, and cut them into round pieces or long slits.
Heat oil in a kadhai, temper with mustard seeds, and add the okra.
Add turmeric powder and add salt after a short while.
Let the dish cook on medium heat.
When it is almost cooked, add red chilli powder and coriander-cumin powder.
Let the dish roast for a little while.
418.note: Adding salt first releases water, so add it after a short while. Tempering with ajwain (carom seeds) and cumin seeds instead of mustard seeds will enhance the flavor.

steps: Roast the gram flour (besan) in a kadhai.
In a bowl, mix roasted gram flour (besan), red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, sesame seeds, sugar, amchur (dry mango powder) powder, and salt to prepare the stuffing masala.
Now wash the okra, wipe it with a cloth, and make a lengthwise slit in the center of each.
Stuff the prepared masala into the slit okra.
Heat oil in a pan. Once the oil is hot, gently place the stuffed okra in the oil and let it roast.
If any masala is left over after stuffing the okra, add it on top.
To make Patra
Take gram flour (besan) in a bowl, add red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, garam masala, sugar, salt, tamarind water, lemon juice, and oil to prepare a mixture.
Add baking soda to it and add water only if needed; this mixture should be thick.
Now take the Patra leaves and remove their thick veins.
Take one Patra leaf, put the prepared mixture on it, and spread it evenly on all sides.
Similarly, place another leaf on top of it and apply the mixture.
Apply the mixture on all the leaves in this way and stack them one on top of the other. Place a maximum of 3 leaves in one roll.
Then roll them up tightly and steam the roll in a steamer.
Once the Patra rolls are steamed, slice them into half-inch pieces.
Now heat oil in a pan and temper with cumin seeds and dry red chillies.
Then add ginger-chilli paste and sauté.
Add cashews and raisins and let them roast for 1/2 minute.
Then add ridge gourd pieces followed by salt, red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, garam masala, and 1/2 cup of water, and let the ridge gourd cook.
After the ridge gourd is cooked, add the Patra pieces, mix well, and cover the pan to cook for 15 minutes.
Keep checking in between and stirring the curry; add a little water if needed.
Add lemon juice and fresh coriander leaves on top, and turn off the gas.

ing: Radish leaves – Use only chopped tender radish leaves.
steps: Dry roast the gram flour (besan). Roast until the color changes (approximately 4-5 minutes).
Now take another vessel and put oil to heat.
