Add mustard seeds to the oil, then add the chopped radish and radish leaves.
Cover for a while. After 2-3 minutes, add salt, jaggery powder, red chilli powder, and turmeric powder, and stir.
Let the curry cook on a low flame.
It will take about 8-9 minutes; water will release from the radish and radish leaves. Let the curry cook until that water evaporates.
Now add the roasted gram flour (besan) and let the curry cook for 3-4 minutes. Then turn off the gas.

ing: yellow moong dal (split skinless moong dal) – 1-1/4 cups
steps: Soak the moong dal for 1 hour.
Heat oil in a vessel and add mustard seeds and cumin seeds.
Add the turaiya and soaked moong dal and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add 2-1/2 cups of water, ginger-chilli paste, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, sugar, and salt, and let the sabzi cook on low heat for 12-15 minutes.
Stir the sabzi occasionally in between.
After the sabzi is cooked, lemon juice can be added on top and fresh coriander leaves can be sprinkled.
Wash the bhindi and wipe them dry with a clean cloth. Cut off both ends and make a slit down the middle.
Prepare all the remaining bhindi in this way.
Take a bowl to mix all the spices.
Now combine all the stuffing spices in this bowl.
Mix everything well so that the stuffing masala is ready.
Stuff the prepared masala into the slit bhindi.
Take a microwave-safe bowl, add 1 tablespoon of oil, and put the stuffed bhindi and any leftover masala into it.
Cover the bowl and place it in the microwave at 80 degrees for 45 minutes.
Serve the hot bhindi sambariyu garnished with coconut and fresh coriander leaves sprinkled on top.
Wash the suran, peel it, cut it into medium-sized pieces, and chop it.
Chop one tomato as well. Heat oil in a cooker and add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, and red chillies to it.
Then add the chopped tomatoes, turmeric powder, salt, red chilli powder, and coriander-cumin powder, and sauté the tomatoes.
After that, add the suran pieces and 1/2 cup of water, and cook for 2 whistles on high flame and 1 whistle on low flame.
The suran curry is ready.
Chop the karela and potatoes.
Heat oil in a vessel and add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, 2 teaspoons of sesame seeds, and turmeric powder.
Add the chopped karela and potatoes, add salt, cover with a plate, and pour a little water on top of the plate to let the curry cook so that it doesn't stick.
When the curry is almost cooked, add red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, and jaggery, and let the jaggery melt.
Then add the cashews, peanuts, and raisins, and mix.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves on top.
First, clean the kantola with water, make vertical slits, and chop them.
Now heat oil in a pan and sauté cumin seeds and ginger-chilli paste in it.
Then add the chopped kantola along with red chilli powder, turmeric powder, salt, and coriander-cumin powder, mix well, and stir.
Cover with a lid and let it cook. After 5 minutes, stir and check if the curry is cooked.
Then take it off the heat, add fresh coriander leaves on top, and mix well.
First, peel the karela and chop them into long strips. Remove their seeds.
Then wash the karela, add salt to them, and let them rest covered.
Now take oil in a pan and fry the karela strips.
In the same pan, take oil for tempering and heat it.
Add the karela along with salt, chilli powder, turmeric powder, and coriander-cumin powder, and stir.
Then add amchur (dry mango powder) powder and stir.
Once cooked, take it off the heat and add coriander leaves.
427.note: Jaggery can be added if desired.

steps: Wash the tomatoes, finely chop them, and make a puree of two tomatoes.
Heat the oil for tempering in a pan and add mustard seeds and cumin seeds for tempering.
Now add turmeric powder, tomatoes, and tomato puree along with salt, and mix well.
Then add red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, and sugar, and stir.
Let it cook until the oil separates from the tomatoes.
Once cooked, add water.
When the water starts boiling, add sev, mix, and turn off the gas.
Then garnish the top with chopped coriander leaves.
First, clean the yam with water and chop it into small pieces.
Now, sauté the yam pieces in a pan by heating some oil.
Now, in the same hot oil, add a little more oil and temper with mustard seeds, cumin seeds, bay leaf, 1 piece of cinnamon, and ginger-chilli paste.
Now finely chop the tomatoes, add them in, and keep stirring.
Now add coriander-cumin powder, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, garam masala, and salt.
Then add the fried yam and half a glass of water, and let the curry cook.
Once the curry is cooked, take it off the heat and add fresh coriander leaves.
Wash the tindora with water and cut them into long slices.
Heat the oil for tempering in a pan. Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and then curry leaves for tempering.
Now add the tindora, add salt, and stir.
Now add turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, and red chilli powder, and cover it.
After 10 minutes, check if it is cooked and stir.
Add garam masala and fresh coriander leaves to it.
Once the curry is cooked, take it off the heat.
Cut the drumsticks into pieces, take water in a pressure cooker, and boil these pieces in it.
Place a pan on the heat with oil, add turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, red chilli, and salt, and sauté.
Then add gram flour (besan), stir and roast, then add the drumstick pieces and mix well; the drumstick curry is ready.
431.note: If anyone prefers tanginess, curd or buttermilk can be added to it.

steps: First, peel the melon, remove the seeds, and cut it into small pieces.
Place a pan on the heat and add oil to heat.
Then add mustard seeds and cumin seeds to it.
When they crackle, add finely chopped tomatoes and stir.
Add red chilli powder, turmeric powder, salt, and coriander-cumin powder, and mix.
Once the oil separates, add the melon and stir.
Then add 1/2 glass of water, cover, and let it cook.
After 10 minutes, check and if it is cooked, take it off the heat.
Add fresh coriander leaves.
Place a kadhai on the gas stove and heat the tempering oil.
Once hot, add mustard seeds and cumin seeds to make the tempering.
Then add curry leaves and one glass of water.
Add red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, and salt (slightly less).
Add the Ganthiya only after the water comes to a good boil.
Add the Ganthiya and stir well. Then remove it from the heat.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve.
433.note: Buttermilk can be used instead of water. Ensure the Ganthiya does not make the curry too hard. Enjoy it while served hot.

steps: First, prep and chop the Valor beans.
Finely chop the tomatoes.
Place a kadhai on the gas stove to heat.
Add the tempering oil.
Then add mustard seeds, let them pop, then add cumin seeds, followed by turmeric powder and the Valor beans, along with salt to taste.
Mix and stir well.
Let it cook on a low flame for a short while.
Add red chilli powder and coriander-cumin powder, and stir.
As the Valor beans slowly start cooking, add the tomatoes.
Mix well and add half a glass of water.
Then cover and let it cook for 10 minutes.
Open to check, add fresh coriander leaves, and mix.
434.note: Add water in measured amounts. Valor beans will release their own water.

steps: Wash, open, and chop the Papdi beans.
Dry roast the sesame seeds separately.
Now, take a pressure cooker, add tempering oil, and heat it.
Then add mustard seeds and cumin seeds; once they pop, add the ginger-chilli paste.
Stir well. Then add the Papdi and mix thoroughly.
Now, add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, and salt.
Next, add half a glass of water, stir, and cover with a lid.
After one or two whistles, turn off the gas and take it off the heat.
Add the sesame seeds and grated dry coconut, and stir.
After that, add fresh coriander leaves.
Finally, add the lemon juice.
435.note: 1/2 teaspoon of sugar can be added. 1 potato can also be added.

steps: For the gravy:
In a mixer grinder, add tomatoes, peanuts, and grated dry coconut, grind to make the gravy ready.
First, wash and chop the carrots, French beans, and tomatoes.
Now, heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a kadhai, add the carrots, French beans, and salt, then pour in 1/2 glass of water.
Now cover with a plate and cook for 10 minutes.
Now take 6 tablespoons of oil in another kadhai and heat it.
Once hot, add cumin seeds, followed by turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, ginger-chilli paste, and the tomato gravy.
Then add red chilli powder and sugar, and cook until the oil separates from the masala.
Next, add a little water, salt, garam masala, French beans, and carrots, stir, and cook for 4 minutes. Finally, add fresh coriander leaves.
436.note: Can also be made without gravy by cooking the carrots and French beans first and then tossing them with a peanut and coconut masala. If you want it spicier, you can also add bay leaves and dried red chillies. For a tastier version, you can sprinkle crumbled paneer at the end.

steps: First, cut the raw jackfruit into medium-sized pieces, then heat oil in a kadhai and fry the jackfruit pieces. To make the paste:
In a mixer grinder, add roasted split chickpeas, poppy seeds, grated dry coconut, shahi jeera, and salt, and grind into a paste. For the masala:
Grind bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, black pepper, cloves, mace, cumin seeds, ginger-chilli paste, salt, and water in a mixer to prepare the masala.
Now take 8 tablespoons of oil in a kadhai and heat it on the gas stove.
Then add the ground masala and red chilli powder, and cook for 5 minutes.
Next, add turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, and the daliya paste, and cook.
Then add the jackfruit and stir. Add salt, half a glass of water, amchur (dry mango powder) powder, and kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), and cook for 2 minutes.
Finally, add fresh coriander leaves.
Paste:
In a mixer, grind together melon seeds, white sesame seeds, grated dry coconut, tomatoes, roasted peanuts, and ginger-chilli paste.
First, chop the purple yam, sweet potato, potato, and eggplant into medium-sized pieces, and shell the green peas.
Heat oil in a kadhai, fry the eggplant first, and then remove it.
Next, add the sweet potato and potato pieces, fry them, and remove them.
Then add the purple yam pieces, fry them, and remove them.
Boil the green peas slightly in water.
Take 8 tablespoons of oil in a kadhai and once it heats up, add cinnamon, bay leaves, and cloves.
Add the paste to it, then add red chilli powder, Kashmiri red chilli powder, salt, turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, and garam masala, and add water.
Then add all the fried vegetables, cover the dish with a lid, and cook for 5 minutes.
For making the paste:
Take tomatoes, ginger, and green chillies and make a paste in a mixer.
First, peel the sweet potatoes and cut them into medium-sized pieces.
Now, heat oil in a cooker, add cumin seeds, turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, and tomato paste, and stir.
Add red chilli powder. Once the oil separates from the masala, add the sweet potato pieces and stir.
Add half a glass of water, let it boil, then add curd (do not use cold curd), mix well, and then add salt.
Then close the cooker, give 1 whistle, lower the flame, cook for 3 minutes, and then turn off the gas.
Once the cooker cools down, take out the sabzi and garnish it with garam masala and fresh coriander leaves.
First, cut potatoes, elephant foot yam, purple yam, and sweet potato into medium-sized pieces.
Chop cluster beans, flat beans, hyacinth beans, and french beans and keep them aside.
Shelled pigeon peas and green peas and keep them aside.
Make slits on both sides of the small brinjals.
Make a paste of tomatoes, fresh coriander leaves, ginger, and chillies. Stuffing masala for brinjals:
Mix gram flour (besan), coriander-cumin powder, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, salt, sugar, garam masala, and oil, and stuff the brinjals with this masala. To make muthias:
Add gram flour (besan), wheat flour, fenugreek leaves, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, salt, lemon juice, baking soda, oil, and sugar, mix well, and shape them into muthias.
Now, heat oil in a pan, add bay leaves, mustard seeds, dry red chilli, cumin seeds, ajwain (carom seeds), turmeric powder, and fresh coriander-chilli paste.
Stir and sauté for 2 minutes, then add flat beans and pigeon peas and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add potatoes, elephant foot yam, purple yam, and sweet potato.
Then add the stuffed brinjals, mix well, and add salt.
Cover the dish with a lid and put water on top of the lid.
Let it cook for 4-5 minutes.
Stir every 4-5 minutes.
Then add the leftover stuffing masala, 2 tablespoons of coriander-cumin powder, and 2-1/2 tablespoons of red chilli powder, and mix.
Cover again and let it cook, then add the tomato paste.
Take 5-6 muthias and crush them.
Now add 2 tablespoons of sugar, half a bowl of water, and the crushed muthia into the sabzi.
Then add the whole muthias, cover with a lid, and stir after 5 minutes.
Sprinkle garam masala and fresh coriander leaves on top.
440.note: Muthias can be added both boiled or fried.

steps: First, place a large kadhai on the gas to heat and put 1 tablespoon of oil in it to heat.
Sauté cumin seeds and ginger-chilli paste in it.
On the other side, dissolve gram flour (besan) in a little water.
Then add that mixture to the tempering and put turmeric, red chilli powder, salt, and coriander-cumin powder in it while stirring continuously.
After it becomes completely thick, add another 1 tablespoon of oil from the top.
So that the dhokli will get taste and shine.
Then cover it and let it cook for 5 minutes.
Then grease a plate with oil, put the dhokli mixture in it and spread it.
Now heat oil in a kadhai, add cumin seeds, dried red chillies, and curry leaves to it and stir.
Then add curd and stir, and put turmeric, coriander-cumin powder, and red chilli powder in it and stir.
Then add a little water to make gravy, add salt, stir it, cover and boil for 2-3 minutes.
Cut the dhokli into diamond shapes and put the dhokli in the prepared gravy and stir.
Then mash and add 2-3 pieces of dhokli into that gravy so the gravy will become thick.
After 3-4 minutes, turn off the gas and sprinkle fresh coriander leaves on top.
441.note: Spread the dhokli mixture in the plate and let it cool down completely. Add salt to the curd while adding the curd itself, otherwise the curd will curdle in the tempering. Here, instead of water, 1/2 bowl of thick buttermilk and 1 ½ bowls of water can also be taken. But if you want to take buttermilk, add salt to the buttermilk itself so that the buttermilk does not curdle.

steps: Take ghee in a kadhai, once it heats up add mustard seeds, cumin seeds and when they crackle, sauté the ginger chilli paste.
Add the grated corn and sauté for 5 to 7 minutes.
On the other side, put milk to warm slightly, once the grated corn is roasted properly then add milk to it.
Mix well, cover and let it cook for 20 minutes.
Keep stirring in between.
Once all the milk evaporates and the grated corn is cooked, add salt, red chilli powder, turmeric and mix.
Turn off the gas and serve Makainu Dano.
First, wash the brinjal with water, make four slits to check if there is any rot inside.
Now place a wire mesh on the gas stove and roast the brinjal on all sides.
Once roasted, turn off the gas and peel off the burnt skin.
Then remove the stem and mash the brinjal well.
Now heat oil in a pan and make a tempering with mustard-cumin seeds and ginger-chilli paste.
Now add chopped tomatoes and let them cook for 2-3 minutes.
Now add turmeric, coriander-cumin powder, and red chilli powder, and mix well.
Add the mashed brinjal and salt, and stir well.
Now cover it with a dish and let it cook for 3-5 minutes.
Turn off the gas and add fresh coriander leaves.
443.note: Raw bharthu can also be made without any tempering. In this version, add oil, chopped green chillies, and salt directly to the prepared brinjal mixture. Then garnish with coriander on top. Curd can also be added.

steps: First, peel the bottle gourd, cut it into large pieces, and boil it in a cooker with water.
Now crush the tomatoes to make a gravy and chop the fresh coriander leaves.
Once the bottle gourd is boiled, mash it.
Now heat oil in a pan.
Add cumin seeds, dry red chillies, and ginger-chilli paste for tempering.
Then add the tomato gravy and let it cook.
Add turmeric, coriander-cumin powder, red chilli powder, salt, and garam masala, and stir well.
Let it cook until the oil separates from the mixture.
Then add the mashed bottle gourd, mix well, and cover for 2-3 minutes.
Now add curd and malai, mix well, and let it cook covered for 1 minute.
Turn off the gas and add fresh coriander leaves.
444.note: Boiled green peas can also be added to it.

steps: Method for making vadis:
Soak the moong dal for 5-6 hours, then drain the water.
Coarsely grind it in a mixer.
Now take whole coriander seeds, fenugreek seeds, black pepper, cumin seeds, and fennel seeds, and grind them in a mixer to prepare the spice blend.
Add this spice mix to the dal paste (batter) and stir to combine.
Now take a large flat tray and grease it with oil.
Drop small vadis from the moong dal batter using your hand onto the tray.
Dry them in direct sunlight for 5-6 days.
These vadis can be stored for up to 1 year. Method for making the curry:
First, heat oil in a pan, fry the vadis, and remove them onto a dish.
Now heat 4 tablespoons of oil in another pan.
Add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and ginger-chilli paste for tempering.
Then add turmeric, coriander-cumin powder, red chilli powder, and salt, and stir.
Now add buttermilk and bring it to a boil.
Add the fried vadis, stir well, cover the dish, and let it cook for 3-5 minutes.
Then turn off the gas and add fresh coriander leaves.
445.note: Just like moong dal vadis, Urad dal vadis and soybean vadis can also be made. Finally, raw urad papads can be added to make Papad-Vadi curry.

steps: First, peel the pumpkin and cut it into medium-sized pieces.
Now heat oil in a pan, and once hot, add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds, dry red chillies, and ginger-chilli paste, and stir.
Then add the pumpkin pieces.
Next, add turmeric, red chilli powder, salt, coriander-cumin powder, and black salt along with water, and mix well.
Cover it with a dish and cook for 6 minutes.
Now add jaggery and tamarind paste, stir well, close the dish, and add fresh coriander leaves.
446.note: Roasted chickpea flour (besan) can also be added at the end.

steps: First, peel the tindora, cut them into medium-sized pieces, and finely chop the tomatoes.
Now heat oil in a pan, and once hot, add whole cumin seeds, fennel seeds, ginger-chilli paste, and turmeric powder.
Then add the tindora pieces, stir well, cover, and let them cook.
Next, add salt, red chilli powder, and coriander-cumin powder, stir, add water, cover, and cook for 5-7 minutes.
Now add chopped tomatoes, garam masala, and amchur powder, stir well, and cook for 2 minutes.
Once ready, turn off the gas and add fresh coriander leaves.
First, wash the zumkhadi and peel its skin.
Chop it into evenly sized pieces.
Now, heat oil in a kadhai and make a tempering of mustard seeds and cumin seeds.
Now add thezumkhadi pieces to it.
Then add salt and turmeric powder, mix well, cover and let it cook for a while.
When it is more than half cooked, add red chilli powder, sugar and coriander-cumin powder, and mix everything.
Let it cook for a little longer.
Once fully cooked, finally add lemon juice and mix well.
Hotzumkhadi shaak is ready.
448.note: Zumkhadi is a vegetable belonging to the ridge gourd family, looking somewhat like a ridge gourd but about the size of a small bitter gourd.

ing: Red chili powder – 1 ½ tea spoon
steps: First, wash the raw bananas and peel their skin.
Then cut them into 1-inch round pieces.
Heat oil in a kadhai and fry the banana pieces.
In another kadhai, heat five spoons of oil and once hot, make a tempering with mustard seeds, cumin seeds and curry leaves.
Then add tomato gravy to it, followed by turmeric, salt, red chili powder, coriander-cumin powder, and garam masala, and mix well.
Let the gravy cook until oil separates from it.
Then add the fried banana pieces, add a little water, cover with a lid and let it cook for 10 to 15 minutes.
Cook until the bananas become slightly soft.
Then add coriander leaves. It can be served with roti, puri or paratha.
449.note: The shaak can also be made by directly boiling the banana pieces.

ing: Fresh coriander leaves (finely chopped) – 1 small bowl
steps: First, peel the bananas and cut them into 1-inch round pieces.
Heat oil in a kadhai and make a tempering using mustard seeds, cumin seeds and curry leaves.
Then add chopped green chillies and stir.
Once the chillies are sautéed, add turmeric, salt, coriander-cumin powder and red chilli powder and stir.
Now add the chopped bananas and mix well.
Immediately turn off the gas, add lemon juice and mix everything properly.
Sprinkle chopped fresh coriander leaves on top.
450.note: Do not stir too much and do not keep it on the gas for too long, otherwise water will release from the bananas. Sugar can be added if desired. If the peel is good, the shaak can be made by chopping the bananas with the peel on.

ing: Red chilli powder – 1 ½ tea spoon
steps: First, wash the zucchini.
Cut the zucchini into small pieces.
Heat oil in a kadhai, and once the oil is hot, add cumin seeds and sauté.
Now add finely chopped chillies, salt, ginger-chili paste and turmeric powder and sauté.
Then add finely chopped tomatoes.
Next, add red chilli powder and garam masala and let it cook.
Then add the zucchini pieces, stir, cover and let it cook for a while.
Once the zucchini is cooked, add lemon juice and coriander leaves, and mix.
Clean the methi bhaji, finely chop it, and then wash it 3-4 times with water.
Now heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds and let the cumin seeds crackle.
Now add tomatoes, turmeric powder, red chilli powder and ajwain (carom seeds).
Let it cook on low heat.
Once the tomatoes are cooked, add the chopped methi bhaji and salt, and let it cook.
The methi bhaji will cook in the tomato gravy itself, so there is no need to add extra water.
If you want to make the bhaji with gravy, you can add more water.
Let it cook for about 8-10 minutes.
452.note: Dry roasted gram flour (chana flour) can be added when the bhaji is almost cooked. Be very careful while adding salt in any kind of bhaji because adding just a little salt to leafy greens provides enough flavor.

steps: First, wash the spinach and chop it finely.
Now take oil in a pan, then add cumin seeds to it.
Once the cumin seeds crackle, add tomatoes, turmeric, red chilli powder, and ajwain (carom seeds), and let it cook on low heat.
Once the tomatoes are cooked, add the chopped spinach, salt, and water, and let it cook for about 7–8 minutes.
453.note: If you want to make the spinach gravy-based, more water can be added to it.

steps: First, wash the purslane leaves and chop them finely.
Now take oil in a pan, then add cumin seeds to it.
Once the cumin seeds crackle, add tomatoes, turmeric, red chilli powder, and ajwain (carom seeds), and let it cook on low heat.
Once the tomatoes are cooked, add the chopped purslane leaves, salt, and water, and let it cook for about 7–8 minutes.
454.note: If you want to make the purslane sabzi gravy-based, more water can be added to it. This sabzi can also be made in ghee.

steps: First wash and chop the greens.
Heat oil in a kadhai on low heat.
Now add cumin seeds, ajwain (carom seeds), fenugreek powder, ginger-chilli, and turmeric, and add the ajwain leaves.
Then add salt and sugar to it.
Let the sabzi cook for 4 minutes.
Now sprinkle gram flour (besan) over it and let it cook covered for 4-5 minutes without stirring.
Then add coriander-cumin powder, chilli powder, and garam masala, and mix well.
So the ajwain leaves sabzi is ready.
First, wash the dill leaves and chop them finely.
Now take oil in a pan, then add cumin seeds to it.
Once the cumin seeds crackle, add tomatoes, turmeric, red chilli powder, and ajwain (carom seeds), and let it cook on low heat.
Once the tomatoes are cooked, add the chopped dill leaves, salt, and water, and let it cook for about 7–8 minutes.
456.note: If you want to make the dill leaves sabzi gravy-based, more water can be added to it. This sabzi can also be made in ghee.

steps: First, separate the amaranth leaves, wash them well, and chop them.
Then wash the tomatoes and crush them in a mixer.
Next, add oil to a kadhai.
Then add cumin seeds, and once the cumin seeds crackle, add the tomato gravy.
Once the gravy is cooked, add the chopped dill leaves (amaranth leaves), salt, and turmeric, and let it cook for about 7–8 minutes.
When the sabzi is almost cooked, add coriander-cumin powder and red chilli powder, and mix well.
457.note: The sabzi can also be made without tomatoes.

steps: First, wash the radish leaves thoroughly and chop them finely.
Dry roast the gram flour in a pan.
Then, heat oil in a pan, add ajwain (carom seeds), turmeric powder, and the chopped leaves, and let them cook while stirring occasionally.
Once the leaves are cooked, add the roasted gram flour (besan) along with red chilli powder, sugar, and salt to taste, and mix well.
Then add the lemon juice to it.
458.note: Radishes can also be added by cutting them into small pieces.

steps: For the koftas:

Mash the boiled potatoes, add grated paneer, green chillies, fresh coriander leaves, salt to taste, garam masala, red chilli powder, and 2 tablespoons of maida (all-purpose flour) to make a soft mawa (khoya).
Then make small round portions from the mawa, place 2-3 cashew pieces in the center, and shape them into round balls.
Heat oil in a pan and fry these balls.
Turn them gently, otherwise the koftas will break and spoil the oil. For the gravy:
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds, and when they turn brown, add cinnamon, bay leaves, cloves, cardamom, and black pepper for tempering.
Now add large chunks of tomatoes, cashews, and salt, cover, and let it cook for 3-4 minutes.
Once it cools down, grind it in a mixer.
Also, grind the ginger along with it.
If you prefer, you can remove the bay leaves, cloves, black pepper, and cinnamon from the gravy. For the tempering:
Then heat oil and butter in a pan and first add the red chilli powder.
Quickly add the prepared gravy and mix everything well.
Add coriander-cumin powder and turmeric powder, and stir well.
Let it cook for 2-3 minutes, then add the Punjabi masala.
Then add tomato sauce, kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), and cooking cream, and mix everything well.
Cover and cook on low heat for 4-5 minutes until the oil separates on top.
Add fresh coriander leaves and mix.
Now take the gravy in a bowl and pour it over the plate of koftas.
Pour enough gravy so that all the koftas are completely submerged.
Garnish with a little cooking cream and fresh coriander leaves on top.

ing: Kashmiri red chilli powder – 1 tea spoon
Kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) – 2 tea spoons
steps: Peel the boiled potatoes and poke holes in them using a fork.
Add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and salt to them, and mix everything well.
Then heat 4-5 tablespoons of oil in a pan, add the masala-coated potatoes, and roast them until they turn brown.
Now, heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds, and roast until they turn brown.
Add cinnamon, cloves, and opened big cardamom, stir a little, and lower the heat.
Now, make a gravy in a mixer using cashews, ginger, green chillies, and tomatoes.
Mix it into the pan, let it cook for 2-3 minutes, then add a little water and let it boil.
After a short while, add garam masala, salt, fresh coriander leaves, and potatoes, cover, and cook on low heat until the oil separates.
Hot dum aloo is ready.

ing: Kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) – 4 tea spoons
Kashmiri red chilli powder – 1/2 tea spoon
steps: Grate the cabbage.

Add chopped green chillies, salt to taste, red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, fresh coriander leaves, and 1/2 cup of maida (all-purpose flour) (gram flour (besan) can be added more if needed), and mix everything well.
Prepare the mawa (khoya) in this manner.
Heat oil in a pan and make round koftas from the mixture.
Once the oil is hot, fry the koftas by turning them on all sides until they turn brown.
In a mixer jar, add tomatoes, green chillies, and ginger, and grind them to make a gravy.

Heat 4 tablespoons of oil in a pan, and when hot, add cumin seeds. When they turn brown, add turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, and kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), and let it cook for 30 seconds.
Then add the gravy and cook while stirring until the oil floats to the top.
To thicken the gravy, add gram flour (besan) and red chilli powder if needed, and cook on low heat for 2-3 minutes.
Add a little water, salt as required, and garam masala, cover, and cook for 6-7 minutes while stirring occasionally.
Add fresh coriander leaves and koftas to it.
Can be garnished with fresh coriander leaves.
The dish is ready.
461.note: According to your preference, cashews, melon seeds, sesame seeds, etc., can be used for the gravy.

ing: Kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) – 1/2 tea spoon
steps: Peel the yam, cut it into small pieces, and boil it in plain water with a little salt and lemon juice in a covered vessel for 15-20 minutes.
Once the yam is boiled, drain the water, mash it, and add ginger-chilli paste, cumin powder, salt to taste, and gram flour (besan) (as much as needed) to make a mawa (khoya).
Shape medium-sized round koftas from the mawa.
Then heat oil in a pan and shallow fry the koftas (do not submerge them completely in oil, take only enough oil so they touch the bottom), turning them to fry until light brown on all sides.
Heat 4-5 tablespoons of oil in a pan and sauté the ginger for 1-2 minutes.
Fry the green chillies.
Take both in a cup and grind the ginger-chilli to make a paste. (Cashews and melon seeds can also be taken for the paste)
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds, and when they turn brown, add turmeric powder and tomato gravy, along with bay leaves, cinnamon, cloves, Punjabi (Kitchen King) masala, and black pepper.
After 1-2 minutes, add coriander-cumin powder, Kashmiri red chilli powder, and the ginger-chilli paste.
Then add about 1/2 glass of water, and after 3-4 minutes, mix in salt and garam masala.
Add kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves).
Then add the yam koftas, coat them well in the gravy, cover, and cook on low heat for 5 minutes.
Mix in fresh coriander leaves.
The dish is ready.
Make a paste by adding ginger and green chillies to the tomatoes.
Make a separate paste of the cashews.
Keep both pastes aside in bowls.

Heat oil in a non-stick pan, once the oil is hot add cumin seeds, when they turn brown add turmeric, coriander powder, tomato-ginger-chilli paste, and red chilli powder, mix everything and let it cook for 3-4 minutes.
In another non-stick pan, shallow fry the paneer (oil just touching the bottom), turning it on all sides until light brown.
Now add Punjabi masala and let it cook for 2-3 minutes.
Meanwhile, add the cashew paste to the gravy.
Stir this masala occasionally.
Once the paneer is fried, remove it.
Add required water and salt to the gravy.
Add garam masala and paneer to the gravy and let it cook for 4-5 minutes.
Add fresh coriander leaves.
The curry is ready.
463.note: If the gravy becomes too thick, you can add water to make it soft. If you do not want to use fried paneer, mix 1 teaspoon of red chilli powder and 1/2 teaspoon of turmeric with the paneer and let it rest for 10 minutes. Then, put 50 grams of butter in a pan and sauté the paneer so that it becomes very soft.

ing: Oil – for frying koftas and for the gravy
steps: Peel and grate the dudhi.
Squeeze out as much juice as possible from the dudhi by pressing it between both hands.
Add gram flour (besan) (100 grams), 1 green chilli (chopped), ginger paste, turmeric, coriander powder, red chilli powder, and salt to it.
Add ajwain (carom seeds) and fresh coriander leaves, mix everything well to prepare the mawa (khoya) mixture.
Shape the mixture into round balls like dumplings (koftas).
Heat oil in a non-stick pan for frying the koftas.
Once the oil is hot, fry the koftas until they are brown on all sides.
For the gravy, heat 4 tablespoons of oil, add cumin seeds first, and when they turn brown, add ginger paste, coriander powder, and turmeric.
Then add a paste of tomatoes and 1 green chilli.
Add red chilli powder to it.
Let everything cook until oil separates from the mixture.
When the oil starts surfacing, add the remaining gram flour (besan) and cook for 2 more minutes.
After 2-3 minutes, add water as needed (about 2 cups), salt, Punjabi masala, and fresh coriander leaves.
Cover and let it cook for 4-5 minutes, then add the koftas to the gravy.
Cook again for 3-4 minutes.
The curry is ready, transfer it to a bowl and serve.
Add oil/butter in a non-stick pan, once hot, fry the cashews on low flame until they turn slightly light brown.
Remove the cashews, add more oil/butter, and when hot, add cumin seeds, cardamom, and cloves to roast.
Then add green chillies and ginger paste.
Next, add tomatoes, cover, and let them cook until the tomatoes become soft.
Once the tomatoes are cooked, turn off the gas and let all the spices cool down.
Once the masala cools down, grind it in a mixer to make a gravy.
Then add a few cashews (about 1/2 cup) into the gravy and grind again.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan, add turmeric, cumin powder, and red chilli powder, and let it roast for about 1 minute.
Then add the gravy and mix everything well.
Next, add a little water and let it boil.
After a while, add garam masala, salt, kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), and cream.
Then add the cashews.
Let it cook for 2-3 minutes until oil floats on top.
Add fresh coriander leaves.
The curry is ready and can now be served.
465.note: Punjabi masala can also be used.

ing: Cumin seeds, red chilli powder, Sugar – 1 teaspoon (each item)
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a non-stick pan, add cumin seeds, and when they turn brown, add ginger paste and green chillies.
After 1 minute, add salt, red chilli powder, sugar, turmeric, Punjabi masala, and coriander powder.
Mix everything well, and after 1 minute add tomatoes and let it cook for 5-6 minutes.
Then add fresh coriander leaves and palak, and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Turn off the gas and let it cool.
Once cooled, blend it in a mixer to make a gravy.
Next, heat oil in a non-stick pan, add bay leaf and kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), followed by the palak gravy.
Then add malai/cream, cashew-melon seeds paste, and paneer, and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Palak paneer is ready.
466.note: Mix 1/2 teaspoon of red chilli powder and 1/4 teaspoon of turmeric with the paneer and keep for 10 minutes. Then, put 50 grams of butter in a pan and sauté the paneer so that the paneer becomes very soft.

ing: Carrot, Cauliflower, French beans – 250 grams (boiled for 5-7 minutes)
steps: In a cooker, add ginger, cumin seeds, salt, cashews, magajtari, turmeric, and Kashmiri whole red chillies, and let it boil for 2-3 whistles (on medium flame).
Then grind it in a mixer to make a paste.
In a non-stick pan, add oil and butter, Kashmiri red chilli powder, and kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves).
After 20 seconds, add French beans, carrot, cauliflower, and green peas.
After 2-3 minutes, mix in Punjabi masala and salt.
After 1 minute, add the tomato paste, mix well, add 1/2 cup of water, and let it cook for 2 minutes.
Then add sugar and mix well.
Next, add paneer pieces (cut to size) and grated cheese.
Then add cream and fresh coriander leaves, and mix everything well.
The curry is ready and can now be served.
Gravy :
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a pan, add ginger, and after 20 seconds add dry red chillies.
After a short while, add melon seeds, tomatoes, cashews, and salt, let it cook for 4-5 minutes, and then let it cool.
Next, grind the above mixture in a mixer to make a gravy. Tempering (Vaghar) :
Then heat ghee in a pan and add Kashmiri red chilli powder to it.
Now add the gravy, about 1/2 cup of water, mix everything well, and let it cook for 2-3 minutes.
Then add Punjabi masala, kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), and fresh coriander leaves, cover, and let it cook on low flame for 10 minutes.
Mix milk mawa (khoya) and milk, and make a paste in a mixer.
Add that paste and cream/malai into the spiced gravy in the pan.
Add sugar, 1/2 cup of water, salt, and paneer, cover, and let it cook on low flame for 10 minutes.
The vegetable dish is ready and can now be served.

ing: Mixed vegetables (1 cup french beans, 1 cup cauliflower, 2 pcs carrots boiled in boiling water for 4 minutes)
steps: Gravy:
In a non-stick pan, add 1 tablespoon ghee, ginger, cloves, cinnamon, cardamom, and bay leaf, mix everything, and sauté.
After 2 minutes, add melon seeds, cashews, Kashmiri red chillies, and tomatoes, and let it cook for 4-5 minutes.
Once the tomatoes are cooked, turn off the heat, let it cool, add 1/2 cup of water, and grind it into a gravy in a mixer. Tempering:
Add 1 tablespoon of oil in a pan.
Then add 1 tablespoon of butter, and once it heats up, add cumin seeds.
Now when it turns brown, add the ginger-green chillies paste and sauté for about 2 minutes.
Next, add the tomato and cook for 2 minutes, then add the capsicum (red, green, yellow) and sauté for 1 minute.
After that, add red chilli powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, Punjabi masala, mixed vegetables (beans, cauliflower, carrot), and salt, mix everything well, and sauté for 2 minutes.
Then add the gravy and about 1 cup of water, mix everything well, cover, and let it cook on low flame for 2 minutes.
Next, add the malai (mixed with saffron) and kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), and let it cook for 2-3 minutes.
Then add fresh coriander leaves.
Vegetable Jaipuri is ready and can be served decorated with roasted or fried urad dal papad.
469.note: Instead of red, green, and yellow capsicum, only green capsicum can also be used.

steps: Paste:
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a non-stick pan and add cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, black pepper, dry red chillies, dry coriander seeds, and white sesame seeds to it.
Mix everything well and sauté until aromatic.
Add grated dry coconut and let it cook for 2 minutes.
Then crush this spice mixture in a mixer to make a paste.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a pan, add cumin seeds, and when they turn brown, add ginger paste and let it cook for 1 minute.
Now add tomatoes to it.
Now add salt, coriander powder, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, and garam masala, and mix everything well.
Let it cook for 3-4 minutes, then add the paste and cook again for 2-3 minutes.
Now add potatoes, carrot, cauliflower, French beans, and green peas.
Let it cook for 1 minute, then add water and paneer, and cook again for 1 minute.
Mix in fresh coriander leaves.
The sabzi is ready and can now be served.

ing: kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) – 1/2 tea spoon
steps: Make a mixed paste of tomatoes, ginger, and chillies.
In a kadhai, add 1 tea spoon of butter and roast the cashews until they turn slightly light brown, for about 1-2 minutes.
Add oil in a kadhai, and once the oil is hot, add cumin seeds, cloves, cinnamon, and cardamom, and sauté for 30-40 seconds.
Then add the tomato and ginger-chilli paste to it.
Next, add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, salt, and coriander powder, and let the gravy cook until it thickens a bit.
Then add a paste made from 10-15 cashews blended with 1/2 cup of water.
After that, add malai/cream, garam masala, and kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), and let it cook for 2 minutes.
Then add the cashews, remaining butter, and about 150 ml of water, cover, and let it cook for 5-6 minutes.
Then add fresh coriander leaves. Kaju curry is ready. It can now be served.
Peel the bitter gourd, make a slit in the middle, stuff it with salt, and cut each bitter gourd into 2 to 3 pieces.
Let it rest for 15-20 minutes so that its bitterness goes away.
Peel the sweet potatoes and potatoes and cut them into large pieces.
Make four vertical slits from the back of the brinjals without separating them, and keep them aside.
Trim the stem ends of the okra and make a single vertical slit.
Heat enough oil in a non-stick pan to submerge the vegetables, and fry the brinjals when the oil is hot (takes about 3 minutes on medium flame).
Then fry the okra (about 2 minutes), followed by sweet potatoes (about 3 minutes).
Then fry the potatoes (about 5 minutes), and then the bitter gourd (about 3 minutes).
In a bowl, add red chilli powder (1 teaspoon), chaat masala (1 teaspoon), and salt (1/2 teaspoon) and mix everything well.
Sprinkle and mix this spice blend separately over all the vegetables.
In a pan, heat 2 tablespoons of oil. Alongside this, crush tomatoes, green chillies, and ginger in a mixer to make a paste.
Once the oil is hot, add this paste. Then add turmeric, coriander powder, fennel seeds powder, red chilli powder, and cumin powder.
Mix everything well and let it cook while stirring until the oil separates on top.
Then add salt and kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) and mix well.
Then add punjabi masala and fresh coriander leaves (keep the masala slightly thick).
Heat a tava on a low flame and arrange the prepared spiced vegetables around its edges.
Keep the center part empty.
Then, whichever vegetable you want to serve, put a little butter in the empty center part of the tava and take that vegetable.
Add the mixed spice blend and a little water, stir for 1-1 ½ minutes, and transfer that vegetable to a bowl.
Sprinkle chaat masala on top.
Alternatively, you can add butter and vegetables all together, add the mixed spices and a little water, mix everything well, and let it cook for 2-3 minutes.
Arrange nicely on a plate and sprinkle chaat masala on top.
Sprinkle fresh coriander leaves on top.
472.note: You can take other vegetables according to your preference such as cabbage, cauliflower, capsicum, etc. In addition, paneer and cheese slices can also be used.

steps: In a bowl, add maida (all-purpose flour), corn flour, ginger-chilli paste, pepper, salt to taste, and a little water.
Make a moderately thick batter.
Coat the capsicum pieces in the batter, heat oil in a pan, and once the oil is hot, fry them on medium heat until light golden brown.
Then place them on a paper towel so the excess oil is absorbed.
Similarly, fry the cauliflower and potatoes one by one and place them on paper to drain.
Heat oil in a pan, and once hot, add green chillies ( chopped) and sauté for 1-2 minutes.
Then add Schezwan chutney, red chilli sauce, tomato sauce, soya sauce, vinegar, and salt to taste, mixing everything well.
Next, add the fried vegetables and mix everything thoroughly.
Sprinkle fresh coriander leaves on top.
The dish is ready, now it can be served.
473.note: You can add other vegetables of your choice such as French beans, red and yellow capsicum, etc. If Schezwan chutney is not available, red chilli chutney can be used.

steps: Cut the vegetables into small pieces.
Cut the paneer into about 1-inch cubes.
Crush the tomatoes, green chillies, and ginger in a mixer to make a paste.
Heat oil in a pan and add cumin seeds.
Once they turn brown, add turmeric powder, coriander powder, and the tomato paste.
Let it cook for 3-4 minutes.
When oil starts separating on top, add the chopped vegetables, salt, red chilli powder, and half of the Punjabi masala, and let it cook for 2-3 minutes.
Then add 1 tablespoon of water and let it cook for 10-12 minutes.
If needed, add more water and cook further until tender.
Once cooked, mix in the remaining Punjabi masala and fresh coriander leaves.
Mix Vegetable Fry is ready and can now be served.
474.note: If you do not want to cook the vegetables too much in water, you can first sauté them separately in oil until light brown, then add them to the gravy and cook for only 3-4 minutes. Paneer is optional.

ing: Fresh vegetables – 3 cups (carrot, French beans, potatoes, peas, cauliflower (chopped))
steps: In a steel vessel, chop peas, carrots, French beans, cauliflower, and peeled potatoes, cover and cook on the stove until properly boiled.
Grind cinnamon, cardamom seeds, fennel seeds, cloves, cumin seeds, whole coriander seeds, turmeric powder, and red chilli powder together in a mixer into a fine powder.
Add green chillies, ginger, fresh coriander leaves, coconut, poppy seeds, cashews, tomatoes, and water (about 1 ½ cups) to it and blend everything well to make a puree.
Heat oil in a kadhai, and once hot, add the puree and let it cook for 3-4 minutes, then add the boiled vegetables along with their water.
Add salt to taste.
Once the gravy reaches a moderate consistency, add the Punjabi masala.
The dish is ready and can now be served.

ing: Mixed vegetables – 1 ½ cups (carrot, peas, French beans (pieces))
steps: Heat ghee in a pan, add ginger-chilli paste, and sauté for 2 minutes.
Add coriander-cumin powder, red chilli powder, and turmeric powder, and let it cook for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and cook for another 1 minute.
Add cashews and 2 tablespoons of water, and let it cook on low heat.
Now add the mixed vegetables and paneer, and let them cook on low heat for 3-4 minutes.
Now add salt, milk-corn flour mixture, fresh cream, garam masala (Punjabi), sugar, pineapple, and raisins.
Once cooked properly, serve piping hot.
476.note: If you want the gravy to remain white, do not add tomatoes.

steps: First, take 1 cup of water in a vessel.
Chop and add tomatoes to it.
Now add 2 cinnamon sticks, green chilli, ginger, and cashews, and keep it on medium heat for 15 minutes.
Then grind everything in a mixer to prepare the gravy.
Next, heat oil and butter, and temper with whole cumin seeds, dry red chillies, bay leaves, and peppercorns.
Add the gravy to it and let it simmer on medium heat for 20 minutes.
Add garam masala, Kashmiri chilli powder, turmeric, curd, and coriander-cumin powder, and cook for 5 minutes.
Melt butter in a kadhai and sauté the paneer pieces in it.
Mix this prepared paneer into the gravy.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves on top and serve.
Grate about 50 grams of paneer and add cashews, almonds, pistachios, raisins, ginger paste, fresh coriander leaves, and salt to it.
Mix everything well to make a stuffing.
Now, make a thin batter by adding a little salt and water to the corn flour.
Cut large pieces of paneer, make a slit in the middle, and fill the prepared stuffing inside.
Dip the stuffed paneer pieces into the corn flour batter.
Now, heat oil in a kadhai and fry the paneer until light brown on both sides.
In a mixer jar, add green chillies and tomatoes, and grind them to make a gravy.
Heat oil in a kadhai, add cumin seeds, kasuri methi, coriander powder, turmeric, and ginger paste, and let it cook.
Then add the tomato gravy and red chilli powder, and let it cook until the oil separates.
Next, add the cream and let it cook.
Then add 1 cup of water, Punjabi masala, salt, and fresh coriander leaves, and mix well.
Now add the paneer pieces, turn off the gas, and let it rest for 2-3 minutes.
Now the curry is ready and can be served.
478.note: If you want to use cashews, melon seeds, poppy seeds, and sesame seeds with tomatoes for the gravy, you can do so.

steps: Heat oil in a kadhai and fry the cashews on low flame until light brown.
Now, in the same kadhai, add the remaining oil or butter, and add cumin seeds, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, and ginger, and let it cook for 1 minute.
Now add the tomatoes, cover, and let it cook for 3 – 4 minutes.
Take this mixture in a mixer, add 8-10 pcs of cashews and melon seeds.
Also add a little water and grind everything well to make a gravy.
Heat a little oil in a kadhai and add turmeric, coriander powder, and red chilli powder.
Sauté the spices for 20 seconds, add the tomato gravy, and stir continuously for 2-3 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup unsweetened mawa (khoya) and mix well.
Then add 1 cup of water, cover, and let it cook for 4-5 minutes.
After that, add Punjabi masala, salt to taste, kasuri methi, and cream. After 2 minutes, add the cashews and let it cook for 2-3 minutes.
Mix in fresh coriander leaves.
Kaju khoya is ready and can now be served.
Take about 3 liters of water, add a little salt, and bring it to a boil.
Cut the top part of the capsicums about 1/2 to 1 inch and arrange them upright. Remove the seeds from inside.
Chop the removed top portion of the capsicums and drop the upright capsicums into boiling water for 3 minutes.
After 3 minutes, carefully remove the capsicums. Place them on a tray and check with a knife whether they are cooked or not.
Now, in a kadhai, add Mexican rice, both types of boiled beans, chopped capsicum, and tomato puree.
Add all the spices and stir. Fill this mixture into the capsicums and sprinkle cheese on top.
Place them on a tray and bake in the oven at 180 degrees Celsius for 15 minutes.
Cut the stem part of 6 pcs of tomatoes in a round shape, scoop out the inner pulp to make a round hole, and hollow out the tomatoes.
Heat a non-stick pan, add 2 teaspoons of oil, and roast 1/4 teaspoon of cumin seeds until light brown.
Now lower the gas, add ginger and green chillies, and sauté for 1-2 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup grated cauliflower and 1/2 cup boiled and mashed potatoes.
Now add turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, and amchur (dry mango powder), and roast while stirring for 2 minutes.
Now add a little salt and fresh coriander leaves, and mix well. The stuffing is ready.
Fill this stuffing into the tomatoes (6 pcs) and set them aside.
In a pan, add 2-3 teaspoons of oil and a little salt, place the tomatoes, and let them cook on low flame for 3-4 minutes.
On the side, in another pan, heat oil and roast cumin seeds, cinnamon, black pepper, cloves, and large cardamom.
Make a paste of 4 pcs tomatoes, ginger, green chillies, and 1/4 cup cashews in a mixer and add it to the tempering.
Add turmeric, coriander-cumin powder, and red chilli powder, and cook while stirring until the oil surfaces.
In between, turn the tomatoes to cook them from all sides.
Add the remaining stuffing, tomato pulp, and kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) to the gravy.
Once the tomatoes are soft, turn off the gas and add 1 cup of water, salt, and fresh coriander leaves to the gravy, and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Add the tomatoes into the gravy and cook on low flame for 3-4 minutes.
The curry is ready and can now be served.
Take black urad dal, rajma, and chana dal in a cooker, add a little salt and water, and let it pressure cook for 2-3 whistles.
Make a tomato paste.
Heat ghee in a pan and add the ginger paste.
After 20-30 seconds, add the tomato paste, salt, red chilli powder, and fresh coriander leaves.
Once the dal is boiled, add it to the tempering and let it cook for 7-8 minutes.
In another pan, heat butter, add red chilli powder, pour this tempering over the dal, and top it again with fresh coriander leaves.
Now add fresh cream.
Dal makhani is ready and can now be served.
482.note: Soak rajma in hot water for 5-6 hours.

steps: Add oil to a non-stick pan, add cumin seeds, and once they turn brown, add the ginger-chilli paste.
Once it is sautéed, add turmeric powder, red chilli powder, cumin powder, and coriander-cumin powder, and mix everything well.
Then add finely chopped tomatoes, fresh coriander leaves (half), and salt, and let it cook on low heat.
Grate the paneer; the paneer should be grated in slightly larger shreds.
Add it to the tempering, stir for 2-3 minutes, and mix in the Punjabi masala and fresh coriander leaves.
Paneer bhurji is ready and can now be served.
483.note: If you wish to add malai/cream, you may do so.

steps: Take warm water in a bowl and put 3-4 tablespoons of melon seeds to soak in it.
Put hot water in another pan and add coarsely chopped fenugreek leaves to it.
Then add about 1 teaspoon of salt and let it boil (let it boil for about 7-8 minutes).
Then drain the fenugreek leaves in a colander.
Heat oil in a kadhai and add grated ginger and 4 green chilli pieces to it.
Now, grind the soaked melon seeds, cashews, and the above ginger-chilli mixture in a mixer to make a paste.
Now add butter to a kadhai and add cinnamon, cloves, and cardamom to it.
After 1 minute, add 1 chopped green chilli as well as the melon seed-cashew paste, cover and cook until the oil separates on top.
After about 5 minutes, add a little water (about 1/2 glass of water) and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Then add red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, and salt, and mix well.
Now add the boiled fenugreek leaves and malai or cream to it.
Now add kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) as well as Punjabi masala and mix everything well.
The sabzi is ready and can now be served.
In a mixer, add cashews, tomatoes, melon seeds, and water, and grind to make a gravy.
Heat oil in a kadhai and fry the paneer until it is light brown.
Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in a kadhai and add ginger paste to it.
After 20-30 seconds, add cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, bay leaf, and dry red chillies, and mix everything well.
Then add the cashew-tomato-melon seed gravy.
Now let it cook for 1 minute. Then add capsicum (pieces), mix, and cook for 1-2 minutes.
Then add turmeric powder, salt, red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, and Punjabi masala, mix everything well, and cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add 1/2 cup of water and the fried paneer, mix everything well, and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Paneer handi is ready and can now be served.
First, soak makhana in water for 6-7 hours.
Place a kadhai on the gas to heat and add 1 tablespoon of ghee.
Roast the makhana on low heat until they become slightly golden.
Then take them out in a bowl.
Place a non-stick pan on heat, add 2 tablespoons of ghee, add the ginger-chilli paste to it, and sauté for 1 minute.
Then add turmeric powder, coriander powder, red chilli powder, and salt, mix well, add curd, mix thoroughly, and add mawa (khoya).
Then mix the mawa (khoya) on low heat and let it roast for 2-3 minutes.
Then add the tomato puree, mix everything well, stir and cook until the ghee separates on top, and turn off the gas.
Now transfer this masala into a cooker, add makhana, add 2 ½ cups of water, add Punjabi masala, cover the cooker, and after the whistle, let it cook on low heat for 5 minutes.
After the cooker cools down, open it, transfer it to a bowl, add cream/malai and fresh coriander leaves, and mix everything well.
486.note: Along with the tomato puree, a few cashews and melon seeds can be added according to preference.

ing: Baby corn cut into long pieces - 10-12 pcs
Dry red chillies soaked in water - 10-12 pcs
steps: First of all, in a mixer, combine red chillies, ginger, lemon juice, fresh coriander leaves, black peppercorns, roasted whole coriander seeds, roasted cumin, lemon zest, add a moderate amount of water, and grind it.
Prepare the Thai curry paste in this manner.
Heat oil in a pan and add the ground masala.
Then add paneer pieces and baby corn and stir.
Then add 1/2 cup of water and salt, and let it boil for five to seven minutes.
Then add coconut milk and let it boil for 2 minutes (do not let it thicken too much).
Then add 8-12 basil leaves and mix.
Turn off the gas and stir well.
Now your Thai curry is ready!
487.note: Vegetables can be used according to preference (potatoes, carrots, etc.). Serve Thai curry with rice and paratha.

ing: Bay leaf, dry red chillies – 2 -2 pcs
steps: First, soak the peas overnight.
Now, place a pressure cooker on the stove, turn on the gas, add oil, and let the oil heat up.
Then add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, dry red chillies, and bay leaf. After a short while, add the ginger-chilli paste and stir well.
Then add turmeric, chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, and black pepper powder, mix well, and let it cook for 1 minute.
Then add tomato paste and let it cook for 2 minutes.
Then add the soaked peas, mix everything well, and let it cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
Now add 1 ½ glasses of water, salt, and garam masala, and mix well.
Keep in mind to give one whistle on medium flame and one whistle on high flame.
Now turn off the gas and check if the peas are cooked or not. If they feel uncooked, give one more whistle.
Then open the lid, add fresh coriander leaves, and the curry is ready.
First, boil the mung beans by giving 4 whistles.
First, heat oil in a pan, then add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, dry red chillies, and sweet neem leaves and sauté them.
Now add the boiled mung beans and mix well.
Then add turmeric, coriander-cumin powder, red chilli powder, salt, and garam masala, and mix.
Then add lemon juice, jaggery, and the leftover water from boiling the mung beans, and mix everything.
Cover the pan with a lid and let it simmer for 1 to 2 minutes.
Then add fresh coriander leaves and the curry is ready.
Soak the moth beans for 5 hours, then put them in a cooker with 2 glasses of water and give 1-2 whistles.
Take 5 spoons of oil in a pan and let it heat up.
Then add cumin seeds, sweet neem leaves, turmeric, coriander-cumin powder, red chilli powder, and one tomato, and sauté.
Grate a small piece of ginger and add it.
Then add the boiled moth beans, cover and let it cook for 5 minutes, then turn off the gas.
490.note: Can also be made by adding tomato paste.

steps: First, soak the Kabuli chana for 6 to 7 hours.
Then add 1 spoon of salt and water, and boil in a cooker for 6–7 whistles.
Heat oil in a pan, add the piece of cinnamon and ginger-chilli paste, and sauté everything.
Then add the tomato paste on low heat and mix everything well.
Let it cook until the oil separates.
Then add red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, and chole masala, and mix well.
Let it sit for a little while, then crush 1 spoon of kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves) with your hands and add it; this will enhance the taste.
Then add the chickpeas into the gravy.
The thickness of the gravy can be adjusted according to personal preference.
Now add salt to taste and let it cook for 5 minutes.
Then add fresh coriander leaves to prepare the chole chana curry.
First, soak the black-eyed peas for 8–10 hours.
Then take them in a pressure cooker, add water and salt, and boil for 6–7 whistles.
Next, heat oil in a pan and sauté ajwain (carom seeds), cumin seeds, and curry leaves.
Also add besan and sauté it.
On low heat, add turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, and salt, and mix well.
Then add the boiled black-eyed peas, add amchur (dry mango powder) powder and sugar, and let it cook for a short while.
Add a little water if needed.
Then turn off the gas, add fresh coriander leaves, and the curry is ready.
First, soak the black eyed peas for 7-8 hours, take them in a pressure cooker with three glasses of water and pressure cook for 3-4 whistles.
Then heat oil in a pan, add mustard-cumin seeds, dry chillies and chopped tomatoes, mix everything and stir.
Then add ginger-chilli paste, red chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder and garam masala, and mix well.
Add boiled black eyed peas and salt to taste, and stir well.
Add about 2 glasses of water, mix 3 teaspoons of gram flour dissolved in water and sugar, then cover with a lid and cook for a while.
Then turn off the gas, add lemon juice and fresh coriander leaves, and serve.

ing: Lemon juice, sugar, salt – to taste
steps: Soak the chickpeas overnight, then put them in a cooker and boil the chickpeas.
Once oil gets hot in a pan, add mustard seeds, dry chillies and pureed tomatoes.
Add ginger-chilli paste, stir well and saute.
Then add boiled desi chickpeas, red chilli powder and salt, and add a little water.
Add 2 teaspoons of gram flour (besan) to it and let it boil for 7 minutes.
Then add lemon juice, sugar and fresh coriander leaves, and prepare.
First soak the field beans for 10 hours, then to boil them, put them in a cooker with salt and 2 glasses of water and pressure cook for 5 whistles.
Then heat oil in a pan and add mustard-cumin seeds, bay leaves, curry leaves, and dry chillies.
Also temper with 4 cloves, 1 star anise, add one finely chopped tomato and ginger, and stir well.
Then add coriander-cumin powder, turmeric powder and red chilli powder, and mix the boiled field beans into it.
And also mix the water from the boiled field beans.
Add jaggery, sesame seeds, peanut powder, tamarind water and garam masala, and let it cook for ten minutes.
Add fresh coriander leaves and turn off the gas.

ing: Chilli powder, turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder – 1 teaspoon
steps: Wash and clean the urad dal properly, put it in a cooker with ghee, salt and water, and cook for 1-2 whistles.
Crush tomato, ginger, chillies to prepare a paste.
Take out cardamom seeds, mix pepper, cloves, cinnamon in a mixer jar and coarsely grind to prepare the spice blend.

Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds, turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, curry leaves, then add the coarsely ground spice mix and mix everything well. Then add tomatoes and chilli-ginger paste and stir until oil separates.
Then add about 2 cups of water and salt, after 2-3 minutes add urad dal, mix everything well and serve garnished with coriander.

ing: coriander-cumin powder, turmeric powder, chilli powder – 1 teaspoon
steps: Soak rajma for 8-10 hours, then wash thoroughly and boil in a cooker with water, soda and salt.
Prepare tomato ginger-chilli paste.
Heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds, then add turmeric powder, coriander-cumin powder, chilli powder and tomato paste, and mix everything well. Stir it until the oil separates.
Now add boiled rajma and water as needed, and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Then add lemon, garam masala and fresh coriander leaves to prepare.
Soak the fenugreek in water for 2 hours.
First, heat oil in a pan, add turmeric, coriander-cumin powder, dry ginger powder and stir well.
Add the soaked fenugreek to it and mix everything together.
Then add salt, amchur (dry mango powder) powder, red chilli powder and mix well with the fenugreek.
After that, add half a cup of water, add chopped dates and raisins, and cook on low heat for 5-6 minutes.
After 5 minutes, check; if the fenugreek seeds are not tender, cook for another 5 minutes.
Soak the soyabeans for 10 hours.
Then, take the soyabeans in a cooker for boiling, add salt and 1 glass of water, and boil for 3 whistles.
Then heat oil in a pan, add cumin seeds, tomatoes, turmeric, and ginger paste, and stir well.
Then cook it until oil separates.
Then add the boiled soyabeans to it.
Then add salt and garam masala along with 1 cup of water, mix well, and let it simmer for 5-6 minutes.
Then add fresh coriander leaves and serve.
Put the pigeon peas in a cooker and give 2-3 whistles.
Add salt and water as required along with it.
In a pan, once the oil heats up, add cumin seeds, turmeric, chilli, and ginger, and sauté.
Then mix everything well, add the boiled pigeon peas, and mix.
Add sugar and lemon juice and stir gently.
Add fresh coriander leaves and serve.
First, wash the fenugreek and soak it for 7-8 hours, then wrap it in a cloth and keep it for 7-8 hours.
Heat oil in a pan.
Then add cumin seeds, and once the cumin seeds crackle, add green chillies paste, dry chillies, and raisins, mix, and sauté.
Add all the remaining spices like fennel seeds, mix everything, and sauté on medium heat for one minute.
Add 1/2 cup of water and salt, and mix.
Cover with a lid until it becomes slightly tender, then add amchur (dry mango powder) powder and cook for a short while.
When the water evaporates a bit, turn off the gas.
Soak the mung beans for 6-8 hours. Once soaked, put them in a cloth, tie it up, and leave them until morning.
Add 5 tablespoons of oil to a pan, add cumin seeds, turmeric, green chilli, curry leaves, red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder.
Add the sprouted mung beans to it and let them steam for a while.
Soak the moth beans overnight. Once soaked, tie them into a bundle using a cloth.
Keep the tied moth beans in the cloth for 8 hours.
In a kadhai, add oil, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander-cumin powder, garam masala, and salt, then add the sprouted moth beans.
Add a little water, let it rest for a moment, and turn off the gas.
Lemon and sugar can be added according to taste.
Soak the moong dal for half an hour. Then put it in a pressure cooker with a little water and whistle for 2 whistles.
Heat ghee in a pan, add cumin seeds, turmeric powder, salt, and then add the cooked dal.
Add about 3-4 spoons of water and some red chilli powder, then let it cook for 5-6 minutes.
Hot and ready lachko dal is ready.
Method:
Soak the horse gram overnight, then put it in a pressure cooker with 2 glasses of water, half a spoon of turmeric powder, and salt, and whistle for 6-7 whistles.
Heat ghee in a pan, add cumin seeds, ginger, green chillies, tomato gravy, coriander-cumin powder, and red chilli powder, and let it cook for a while.
Then add the boiled horse gram to it and mix well.
Then let it cook on the stove, add fresh coriander leaves to it, and serve.
First, apply oil on a non-stick pan and heat it so that the dosa does not stick while making.
Then spread one cup of dosa batter in a circular motion on the pan.
Apply butter on it and remove it from the pan once the dosa turns brown in color.
Hot plain dosas are ready, they can be served with coconut chutney.
507.note: Oil and ghee can be used instead of butter. Red chili powder can be added on top of the dosa.

ing: Mustard seeds and cumin seeds – 1 teaspoon
steps: First, sauté mustard seeds, cumin seeds, ginger-chilli paste, turmeric, and curry leaves in a pan.
Then, add chopped boiled potatoes and peas to it.
Next, add lemon juice, sugar, garam masala, cumin powder, salt, and fresh coriander leaves, and mix well.
Now, take a cup of batter on a non-stick pan and spread the dosa.
Apply the prepared potato stuffing on it.
Then, fold the dosa from both sides, remove it from the tawa, cut it into pieces, and serve with coconut chutney.
508.note: Mix one bowl of oil and water, and wipe the pan with a cotton cloth after making each dosa so that the dosas do not stick.

ing: Mustard seeds and cumin seeds – 1 teaspoon
steps: Method for making Mysore chutney:
Heat oil in a pan and roast chana dal and urad dal for 2-3 minutes.
Now add red chilli powder to it and roast again for 2 minutes.
Then mix jaggery, tamarind pulp, and pepper, and roast on low heat for 1 minute.
Now add grated coconut, red chilli powder, and salt, and roast again for 1 minute.
After the mixture cools down, add water and grind it to prepare the chutney.
Sweet Mysore chutney is ready. Method for making dosas:
First, sauté mustard seeds, cumin seeds, ginger-chilli paste, turmeric, and curry leaves in a pan.
Then add chopped boiled potatoes and peas to it.
Next, add lemon juice, sugar, garam masala, cumin powder, salt, and fresh coriander leaves, and mix well.
Now heat butter in a vessel and sauté capsicum in it.
Then add tomatoes, carrot, beetroot, cabbage, red chilli powder, pav bhaji masala, and salt, and mix.
Now add the prepared potato mixture, sauté for 1 minute, and make the stuffing this way.
Now heat a non-stick pan, take a cup of batter on it, and spread the dosa.
Then apply butter on top, spread Mysore chutney, then spread the prepared stuffing, and sprinkle fresh coriander leaves on top.
Now cook the dosa until it turns light brown, and then fold it from both sides and take it down.
Hot Mysore dosa is ready, serve it with coconut chutney.
509.note: To prepare tamarind pulp, soak tamarind in hot water for 15 to 20 minutes, strain the water, and prepare it.

steps: First, mix chaat masala into the boiled corn kernels and tomatoes.
Now, heat a non-stick pan by applying oil so that the dosa does not stick while making.
Then spread one cup of dosa batter in a circular motion on the pan.
Sprinkle corn kernels and tomatoes over it, and add grated cheese on top. When the dosa turns brown in color, roll it and remove it from the pan.
Hot sweet corn dosas are ready.
They can be served with coconut chutney and sambar.
Heat the pan, then combine water and oil in a bowl.
Soak a piece of cloth in the water and oil mixture and squeeze it.
Then gently wipe that damp cloth all over the pan.
Put a teaspoon of oil on the pan, then take about a ladleful of dosa batter and place it in the center of the pan.
Then rotate the batter in a circular motion with the ladle to spread it across the entire pan, and pour a little oil around its edges.
Spread the cheese over the dosa.
When the cheese melts and the dosa turns pinkish, roll it and serve.
Now your cheese dosa is ready.
511.note: This dish tastes best when served hot. Enjoy these dosas with sambar and coconut chutney. According to taste, red chili powder and chaat masala can also be sprinkled on top of the cheese.

steps: Method for the topping:
Heat oil in a pan, add all the above vegetables to it and add salt to taste.
Then sauté the vegetables for 2 minutes and let them cool.
Heat the pan, then mix water and oil in a bowl.
Dip a cloth in the water and oil mixture and wring it out.
Then gently wipe the entire pan with this damp cloth.
Put a teaspoon of oil on the pan, then take a ladleful of dosa batter and place it in the center of the pan.
Then use the ladle to spread the batter in a circular motion all over the pan, and drizzle a little oil around its edges.
Now spread red chilli paste on the dosa according to taste.
Then spread the sautéed vegetables over the dosa.
Once the dosa turns golden pink, roll it up and serve.
Now your spring dosa is ready.
512.note: This dish tastes best when served hot. Enjoy these dosas with sambar and coconut chutney.

steps: Wash the urad dal and rice thoroughly with water, soak them in water for six hours, and then grind them.
Then add salt to it and prepare the batter.
Heat oil in a vessel.
Now to make medu vada, wet your hands with water, place a portion of the batter on your hand, make a hole in the center, and immediately fry it in the oil.
Keep making and frying the medu vadas in this manner.
Hot medu vadas are ready, serve them with medu vada sambar and coconut chutney.
513.note: Two teaspoons of ginger-chilli paste and chopped coriander can be added to the medu vada batter. If the batter becomes too thin, add gram flour (besan) to mix; the batter should be completely thick.

steps: First, mix semolina (rava), curd, and ginger-chilli paste thoroughly.
Add one cup of water to it, stir well, and set it aside for 10 minutes.
Then, heat oil and ghee in a small vessel, add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, and curry leaves, and sauté on low heat.
Now mix this tempering into the batter.
Next, put the idli stand on to heat.
Now add Eno to the batter, pour a teaspoon of water over it, and mix well.
Grease the idli stand with oil and put 1 teaspoon of batter in each mould.
Place the vegetables (boiled green peas, finely grated carrot, and grated cabbage) on top of it.
Then add another half teaspoon of batter over the vegetables.
Allow it to steam for 10 minutes.
Then, once cooled, remove the idlis from the mould.
The idlis are ready, serve them with coconut chutney and sambar.
514.note: The vegetables used can be sautéed with a little oil and favorite spices to make a stuffing.

ing: Sajjina phool (sodium bicarbonate/baking soda) – 1 small teaspoon
steps: First, wash and soak the rice and dal in the evening, and grind them in a mixer in the morning.
Let the batter remain covered until evening. Idlis can be made in the evening.
While making idlis, mix the required amount of water and sajjina phool together, heat it slightly, and add it to the batter.
Then adjust the consistency of the batter to be moderately thin, grease the bottom of the idli stand with oil, and pour the batter in.
Let it steam for 25 minutes.
Then remove the idlis with the help of a spoon or knife. The idlis are ready.
515.note: Idlis can be garnished by sprinkling black pepper powder, red chilli powder, and coriander on top of the idli batter before steaming. Instead of sajjina phool, Eno or lemon juice can also be used.

steps: Take semolina (rava), curd, baking soda, and salt in a bowl, add water to it, and mix well.
Cover and let it rest for 15 minutes.
Add water to the idli cooker and put it on to heat.
Now apply oil to the idli moulds and pour the idli mixture into them.
Place the idli moulds in the cooker, cover, and let it cook for 10 minutes.
Then take them out and apply a little oil on top.
Serve hot rava idli with sambar and coconut chutney.
First, add required water and salt to the dosa batter and mix well.
Then spread the batter on a non-stick pan. (Do not make it too thin)
Now spread green chillies pieces and chopped tomatoes over it and cover with a lid.
Once the tomatoes are slightly cooked, flip it to the other side and roast with oil until it turns light brown.
Hot tomato uttapam is ready and can be served with coconut chutney and sambar.
517.note: A mixed spice of garam masala, red chilli powder, and black salt can be sprinkled on the uttapam. Rava can be used instead of rice while making the batter. To enhance the flavor of the uttapam, a tempering of oil, mustard seeds, and curry leaves can be added.

steps: First, add salt and water as needed to the dosa batter and mix well.
Now, spread the dosa batter on a non-stick pan (do not make it too thin).
Then add tomatoes and capsicum on top and cover it with a lid.
After three to four minutes, apply oil on the other side and roast it.
Hot and delicious vegetable uttapam is ready, can be served with coconut chutney.
518.note: You can sprinkle a mixed spice blend of garam masala, red chilli powder, and black salt on the uttapam. While making the batter, semolina (rava) can be used instead of rice. To enhance the flavor of the uttapam, a tempering of oil, mustard seeds, and curry leaves can be added. Butter or ghee can be used instead of oil for roasting. Grated carrot can also be used in the vegetables.

steps: First, heat oil in a pan, then add capsicum and tomatoes and sauté for 10 to 15 minutes.
Now, mash the tomatoes and capsicum.
Then add the mashed boiled potatoes, cabbage, and peas along with a little water.
Next, add salt, turmeric powder, Kashmiri red chilli powder, pav bhaji masala, and lemon juice, and mix well.
Now let the bhaji boil, then turn off the gas and add fresh coriander leaves and butter.
Hot bhaji is ready, which should be served with toasted pav.
519.note: Toast the pav in butter and serve with pav bhaji.

steps: In a bowl, mix grated coconut, peanut powder, cashews, raisins, sugar, salt, ginger-chilli paste, lemon juice, and fresh coriander leaves very well.
In another bowl, mix boiled potatoes with two spoons of arrowroot flour and salt.
For the patties, apply oil on your hands, take some potato mixture, make a small patty, and place a spoon of coconut stuffing in the center.
Give it a proper round shape like a ball, make all balls this way.
Take arrowroot flour on a plate and coat all the patties in it.
Now take oil in a kadhai and deep fry the patties until they are crispy.
Serve it hot.

In a large bowl, mix puffed rice, peanuts, roasted chana dal, tomatoes, chaat masala, green chutney (spicy), sweet chutney, fine sev, lemon juice, boiled potatoes (chopped), crushed sev puri puris, fresh coriander leaves, and salt to taste.
Prepare the bhel puri in this way.
First, soak moong dal and urad dal in a bowl for 6 hours.
Add sugar and salt to the curd, blend it in a mixer, and keep it in the fridge to chill.
Then, to make vadas, drain the water from the soaked lentils and grind them in a mixer.
Now add salt and ginger-chilli paste to make a thick batter.
Then make small vadas from the prepared lentil batter.
Now heat oil in a pan for frying vadas and fry the vadas in it.
Soak the fried vadas in water, squeeze out the water, and keep them aside.
Now take five to six vadas in a dish, pour chilled curd over them, and add red chilli powder, chaat masala, and cumin powder.
Garnish by sprinkling pomegranate seeds and fresh coriander leaves.
522.note: If the batter becomes too thin while grinding urad dal and moong dal and vadas cannot be formed, you can add a little semolina to make the batter stiff. Instead of frying, vadas can also be made by steaming them like idlis.

steps: Spicy water:
First, put all the ingredients for the spicy water into a mixer and grind them.
Now add a little water and grind again until completely smooth.
Then strain this mixture through a sieve and add cold water. The spicy water is ready. Potato-chickpea stuffing:
First, take boiled chickpeas and boiled potatoes in a vessel and mash them.
Add black salt, red chilli powder, amchur (dry mango powder) powder, chaat masala (1 tsp), and fresh coriander leaves, and mix well.
Prepare the stuffing this way. Panipuri:
Now take a panipuri puri and fill it with the potato-chickpea stuffing.
Add spicy water and chaat masala to it, and enjoy the panipuri.
Ragda:
First, put peas, turmeric, and salt in a cooker and add water to it.
Cook for 7 to 8 whistles in the cooker.
Then heat oil in a pan, add ginger-green chilli paste, then add the boiled peas and a little water to boil.
After 5-8 minutes, add garam masala to it and let it thicken.
Hot pea ragda is ready. Patis:
First, mash the boiled potatoes and mix corn flour, salt, and turmeric into them.
Make small patis from the prepared mixture and roast them on a non-stick pan using oil until golden brown on both sides. Ragda patis:
Take the prepared patis in a dish (4-5 patis) and pour enough ragda over them to cover the patis.
Then add tomatoes, spicy chutney, sweet chutney, chaat masala, and sev on top.
For garnishing, sprinkle fresh coriander leaves and chana dal on top.
Ragda patis are ready, serve hot.
524.note: To prepare peas in less time, soak them in water 7-8 hours beforehand and then boil them in a cooker.

steps: Stuff the panipuri puris with mashed potatoes, tomatoes, and moong, and add spicy chutney, sweet chutney, and curd on top.
Sprinkle chaat masala, cumin powder, sev, chana dal, and fresh coriander leaves over it.
Dahipuri is ready.

ing: Paprika, cumin powder, coriander - to taste
steps: Method to make Shakkarpara:
In a bowl, mix maida (all-purpose flour), corn flour, salt and pepper to taste, rub in a little oil for moyan (ghee or oil rubbed into the flour), add about 2 teaspoons of lemon juice and mix well.
Then knead a dough like chapati dough using a little lukewarm water.
Cover and let the dough rest for a while.
Then roll it out like a regular chapati.
Next, cut into about half-inch shakkarpara and fry them in oil.
Fry shakkarpara from all the dough in this way. Method to make Salsa:

From the measurements given above, take 4 tomatoes, some of the bell peppers, tomato paste, pickled chillies, cumin powder, whole jalapeños, red chilli powder, basil, oregano, coriander, and lemon juice, and grind them all together in a food processor.
Now finely chop the remaining half of the ingredients and add them to the above mixture.
Add salt and sugar to taste, stir and mix well. Method to make Bhel:
First, prepare the rajma gravy (ragda).
Take some water with the rajma and crush them slightly.
Add salt to taste and 2 ladles of salsa, and stir well.
The gravy should neither be too watery nor too thick.
Take some shakkarpara in a deep dish.
Add the bean gravy on top.
Sequentially add lettuce, finely chopped tomatoes, bell peppers, salsa, cheese, and olives.
Stir everything well so that it mixes nicely.
First, arrange puris in a dish and place mashed boiled potatoes and chopped tomatoes on top of them.
Then add spicy and sweet chutney and sprinkle chaat masala.
Add sev, fresh coriander leaves, and chana dal, and add about half a spoon of lemon juice.
Prepare sevpuri this way.
In a large bowl, mix together khari shing, spicy chana dal, chopped tomatoes, and mashed boiled potatoes.
